column1: Prevent maintainers of an anonymous and/or unrevealed collection from adding or inviting works to the collection
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*How to reproduce:*
As User A, make an anonymous and/or unrevealed collection: 
1. Log in as User A
2. Browse > Collections > New Collection
3. Fill out required information
4. Check either "This collection is unrevealed" or "This collection is anonymous" (or both!)
5. Press "Submit"
6. Log out

As User B, agree to your work automatically being included in collections:
7. Log in as User B
8. Hi, User B! > My Preferences
9. Check "Automatically agree to your work being collected by others in the Archive."
10. Press "Update"

As User B, post a work (if you don't already have one):
11. Post > New Work
12. Fill in required information
13. Press "Post Without Preview"

As User A, invite User B's work to your anonymous or unrevealed collection
14. Go to User B's work
15. Press "Add To Collections" at the bottom of the work
16. Enter the name of your anonymous or unrevealed collection
17. Press "Add"

*Variation:* You can _also_ try this without setting User B's preferences to "Automatically agree to your work being collected by others in the Archive."

*What happens:*
- The page will reload and User A will receive a blue flash message saying, "Added to collection(s): Collection Title." 
- User B's work will be added to the collection and made unrevealed or anonymous, likely freaking out User B because the work is either (a) listed as being by Anonymous or (b) just plain unfindable and inaccessible.

*Variation:* If User B doesn't have the "Automatically agree to your work being collected by others in the Archive" preference set, the blue flash message will say, "This work has been invited to your collection (Collection Title)." User B will receive and email and have to confirm that they want the work added prior to freaking out.

*What should happen instead:*
In either the primary case or the variation:
- The page should reload and User A should receive a red flash message saying, "Sorry, you can't invite works to an anonymous or unrevealed collection."
- The work should not be added to the collection.

column1: Extend work search Cucumber feature
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
The work search feature is better than the bookmark search feature was, but could still use some improvements. We'd like to expand it a bit.

Notably, this:
- corrects and extends tests for searching for anonymous works
- tests that restricted works only appear for logged in users and admins, and that admin-hidden works don't appear for anyone
- makes sure that every field on the work search form gets tested at least once (Any Field, Title, Author/Artist, Date, Complete, Single Chapter, Word Count, Language, Fandoms, Rating, Warnings, Categories, Characters, Relationships, Additional Tags, Hits, Kudos, Comments, Bookmarks, Sort by, Sort direction)
- tests searching comments and bookmarks by greater than (e.g., > 4), less than (e.g., < 6), exact number (e.g., 5), or a range (e.g. 1-20)
- tests exclusion searches in both Any Field and the header using -filter_id: ###
- tests OR searches in Any Field using ||
- tests exclusion searches in Any Field using -Tag Name
- tests searching by multiple tag types at the same time (e.g. Relationship and Category)
- tests searching for an unwrangled tag
- tests searching by tags when a number of wrangling situations exist, e.g. when a tag has synonyms or when a tag has subtags with synonyms


No manual testing needed.

column1: Downloads: Title of parent work overlaps words "This work was inspired by"
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*How to reproduce:* 1. Log in 2. Post > New Work 3. Fill in required fields - this will be the parent work 4. Post Without Preview 5. Copy the work's URL 6. Post > New Work 7. Fill in required fields 8. Check "This work is a remix, a translation, a podfic, or was inspired by another work" checkbox 9. In the "URL" field, fill in the URL from step 5 10. Post Without Preview 11. Download > Whatever format you like *What happens:* The title of the first work that inspired the downloaded work overlaps the words "This work was inspired by." I've attached images of the PDF, HTML, and EPUB downloads to illustrate; I couldn't do a MOBI screenshot, but you most likely get the idea. *What should happen instead:* The text shouldn't do that. I'd suggest getting rid of the current HTML structure, which looks like this (notice how multiple works are in the same dd tag): {code:java}
This work was inspired by
A New Work for an Existing Series by sarking (sarken), A New Work For a New Series by sarking (sarken)
{code} And instead stealing the basic list structure we use on the work itself: {code:java}
  • Inspired by A New Work for an Existing Series by sarking (sarken).
  • Inspired by A New Work For a New Series by sarking (sarken).
{code} While the version on the work itself repeats the "Inspired by" text, that's intentional -- we've long had vague plans to allow for more specific relationships between works, e.g. "Remix of" or "Podfic of" or "Inspired by," which would mean each parent work might need different text.

column27:

*What happens*

{code:java}Dear <%= style_bold(@user.default_pseud.byline) %>,

The collection maintainers of <%= style_link(@collection.title, collection_url(@collection)) %> have changed the status of your work <%= style_link(@work.title.html_safe, work_url(@work)) %> to (anonymous || unrevealed || anonymous and unrevealed).

Anonymous works are included in tag listings, but not on your works page. On the work, your user name will be replaced with "Anonymous."

AND/OR (DEPENDING ON WHAT THE WORK WAS SET TO)

Unrevealed works are not included in tag listings or on your works page. Anyone who follows a link to the work will receive a notice that it is currently unrevealed, and they will be unable to access its content.

If you do not want your work to be (anonymous || unrevealed || anonymous and unrevealed), please visit your <%= style_link("Approved Collection Items page", user_collection_items_url(@user) + "?approved=true") %> to remove it from this collection.

For more information, visit our <%= style_link("Collections and Challenges FAQ", archive_faq_url(@archive_faq, anchor: collectionoptions)) %>.{code}

This message will be sent regardless of whether the user has the “Turn off emails from collections” preference set. Please also check that the help text for that section of the user preferences page has been updated accordingly. The new text will be:

{quote}Enable this option if you would prefer not to receive email alerts from collections, such as creator and work reveals. 12/Feb/20 1:20 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Oh, I see what the issue is. The {{resque_mailer}} gem struggles with keyword arguments. Versions [2.4.1|https://github.com/zapnap/resque_mailer/blob/1c4b26f47e29ea2b70f659787d6df7d6133f63e7/lib/resque_mailer.rb#L57] and [master|https://github.com/zapnap/resque_mailer/blob/35c2a7c7ff9038b9bff95c50190d162f95afcd5f/lib/resque_mailer.rb#L58] allow keyword arguments to work; versions [2.4.2|https://github.com/zapnap/resque_mailer/blob/c1dd013200b43981e9555c5738159983f00c6b55/lib/resque_mailer.rb#L57] (which is the one that’s currently installed) and [2.4.3|https://github.com/zapnap/resque_mailer/blob/b38bea0b6dd3434b4e7b2769f89fef22f9485312/lib/resque_mailer.rb#L58] (which is the most recently released) don’t. Unfortunately, the gem hasn’t been updated since 2017, so I’m not sure there will be a 2.4.4 with the changes from master.

As I see it, there are several potential approaches to take:

# Downgrade {{resque_mailer}} to 2.4.1.
# Upgrade {{resque_mailer}} to the master version.
# Stop using keyword args, and just use a Ruby 1.x options hash instead.
# Stop using {{resque_mailer}} and switch over to ActiveJob. (This is a much more complex change, and while I do think it’s something we ought to do at some point, it’s out of scope for this PR.)

I’m leaning towards #3 at the moment, just because there’s less chance of a gem upgrade/downgrade breaking other things.

column1: Favorite Tag: Possible to favorite non-canonical tag
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Overview*
Users are only supposed to be able to favorite canonical tags, as they're the ones with work listings. (And if a tag is de-canonized, it is removed from people's favorites.) However, if you can find the tag_id of a non-canonical tag, you can sneakily add it to your favorite tags.

*Steps to reproduce*
1. Log in as a tag wrangler
2. Browse > Tags > New Tag
3. Fill in a name for the tag
4. Check the canonical checkbox
5. Choose a tag type
6. Press Create Tag
7. Where the page says "Edit [Tag name] Tag," follow the name of the tag to go to the tag's landing page
8. Follow the Works link
9. Using your browser's developer tools, inspect the Favorite Tag button and note the value attribute in the part that looks like: <input type="hidden" value="1217412" name="favorite_tag[tag_id]" id="favorite_tag_tag_id">
10. Where the page says "0 Works in Steps to reproduce," follow the name of the tag to go to its landing page
11. Follow the Edit link
12. Uncheck the canonical checkbox
13. Press Save changes
14. Wait a few minutes
15. Follow Browse > Tags
16. Click a tag's name to go to its works page
17. Using your browser's developer tools, inspect the Favorite Tag button and replace the value of the tag you're currently looking at with the value of the tag from step 9
18. Press Favorite Tag

*What happens:*

I get a 500 error, but the work is properly orphaned: the pseud "Pseud To Orphan" is removed from the work and replaced with "orphan_account," while "Pseud To Keep" stays on the work.

*What should happen:*

Instead of receiving an error page, I should be redirected to my dashboard (http://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME) with a success message saying, "Orphaning was successful." 

*Notes:*

column147:
19/Jan/20 12:53 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;I think the changes in creatorships resulting from the Creatorship Invitation feature fixed the 500 error, but the behavior still doesn’t match the “what should happen” description. Instead of leaving “Pseud to Keep” on the work, the orphan page removes both “Pseud to Keep” and “Pseud to Orphan,” so that the user no longer has any control over the work.

As far as I can tell, the issue is that when you click the “Orphan Works” button for the pseud, it passes the {{pseud_id}} to the {{new}} action of the {{OrphansController}}. But instead of displaying the {{orphans/orphan_pseud}} view (which wouldn’t display a list of the pseud’s works, but would include the {{pseud_id}} in the form), it displays the the {{orphans/orphan_work}} view (which does display the list of the works, but doesn’t include the {{pseud_id}} in the form). This means that when the user submits the form, {{pseud_id}} isn’t passed to the {{OrphansController}}, and so the {{OrphansController}} treats it as though the user is trying to remove all their pseuds from the works in question, instead of one particular pseud.

column1: Changes to pseud or username do not update all user creations
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When a user changes their username or pseud, there are a variety of places where the information is not updated at all, updated inconsistently, or takes much too long to update. In most cases, this is annoying and confusing, but when users are changing their names due to outing, it can be dangerous.

We need to make sure the information updates as completely as possible as quickly as possible. 

Full details will be provided in individual issues. This epic serves merely to link the issues.

Additional notes:
- Work blurbs and the works themselves update immediately for both username and pseud changes
-- If the works are cited in the "Inspired by" section of another work, that information also appears to be updated immediately for both username and pseud changes (however, any download files that have been generated will still have the old data)
- The "My pseuds" list on a user's profile (http://test.archiveofourown.org/users/changednameling/profile) appears to update immediately for both username and pseud changes
- The blurbs for tag sets (used on http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets) and the tag set pages themselves (http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/447) appear to update immediately for both username and pseud changes by owners and moderators
- When someone is subscribed to a user who changes their username, that person's Subscriptions page updates immediately

*Steps to reproduce:*

+Example 1: A series creator changes their username+
1. Log in
2. Post > New Work
3. Fill in required information
4. Check "This work is part of a series"
5. Fill in "Or create and use a new one:" with a name for your series
6. Press "Post Without Preview"
7. Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Series
8. Behold! There is your series. (This step is important. It makes sure your byline in the series blurb gets cached. If no one looks at the blurb, it doesn't get cached, and the bug won't happen.)
9. Now follow the name of the series to view the list of the works and see who is listed at the top as "Creator." Again, this is important: if no one views it, it might not get cached.
10. Hi, username! > My Preferences > Change My User Name
11. Fill in required information
12. Press "Change User Name"
13. Press "OK" to confirm the name change
14. Follow the "Series" link in your sidebar
15. Note that all of the series blurb(s) still have your old name
16. Follow the name of the series to view the list of works
17. Note that "Creator" at the top of the page still has your old name

+Example 2: A series creator changes their pseud+
1. Log in
2. Hi, username! > My Preferences > Manage My Pseuds > New Pseud
3. Fill in the "Name" field with a name for your pseud, e.g. Pseud To Change
4. Press "Create"
5. Post > New Work
6. Fill in required information
7. For "Creator/Pseud(s)," choose Pseud To Change
8. Check "This work is part of a series"
9. Fill in "Or create and use a new one:" with a name for your series
10. Press "Post Without Preview"
11. Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Series
12. Behold! There is your series. (This step is important. It makes sure your byline in the series blurb gets cached. If no one looks at the blurb, it doesn't get cached, and the bug won't happen.)
13. Now follow the name of the series to view the list of the works and see who is listed at the top as "Creator." Again, this is important: if no one views it, it might not get cached.
14. Hi, username! > My Preferences > Manage My Pseuds
15. Under Pseud To Change, follow "Edit"
16. Fill in "Name" with something different, e.g. Changed Pseud
17. Press "Update"
18. Follow the "Series" link in your sidebar
19. Note that the series blurb(s) still have your old pseud
20. Follow the name of the series to view the list of works
21. Note that "Creator" at the top of the page still has your old name

*What should happen*

The username or pseud on the series blurb should be updated as soon as possible.

*Notes*

The series blurb and series metadata do not appear to be cached -- it appears to be the byline helper (https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ab0e0b25f09613ca27de365bcb9f1a750bb80f95/app/helpers/application_helper.rb#L98) which is using the cached non_anonymous_byline helper (https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ab0e0b25f09613ca27de365bcb9f1a750bb80f95/app/helpers/application_helper.rb#L110)

28/Mar/24 6:25 PM;629dc33e9b728c006a926594;Still taking a look, but I did find my notes:

In [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4120|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4120|smart-link] (see [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4419|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4419|smart-link]) there are two separate cache invalidation mechanisms:

# syncing with pseud name changes occurs due to touching all of a pseud's comments after a pseud is updated, and having the comment cache depend on the comment's `updated_at`
# syncing with username changes occurs by having the cache key directly depend on the user's `updated_at`

Then I had some questions for myself:

Is there any sort of preference between the two approaches? I could achieve something similar to the first approach by adding `bookmarks.touch_all` to both `pseud.rb` and `user.rb`, or to the second by adding `pseud.cache_key` and `pseud.user.cache_key` to the `blurb_cache_key` in `app/views/bookmarks/_bookmark_user_module.html.erb`, or do the same sort of hybrid approach

In the git branch I found where I started working on it, looks like I’d opted for the first approach

29/Mar/24 4:01 AM;557058:baa5f297-c116-4036-bbf1-109f8a7e50a7;[~accountid:629dc33e9b728c006a926594]  Based on the conversation on the [kudos caching issue|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4264#discussion_r982890897], I think touch_all is not a good solution. So 2. would be better.

However, I think there are easier ways to create the cache key in {{_bookmark_user_module.html.erb}} than by directly adding the user and pseud {{cache_key}} into the string. Take a look at the cache key for comments and the linked guide in this PR: [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4745|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4745|smart-link] .

So, that means it should be possible to make a cache key like this:
{{["bookmark-blurb", bookmark, bookmark.pseud, bookmark.pseud.user, is_author_of?(bookmark)]}}

Though this makes it always [load the user|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4120?focusedCommentId=358747], when it previously only loaded the pseud, so maybe 1. is better. At least I am not so sure anymore that 2. is better.

29/Mar/24 2:10 PM;557058:baa5f297-c116-4036-bbf1-109f8a7e50a7;Okay, after some internal conversation we came to the conclusion that the user load is fine as long as it’s added to the {{includes:}} of the bookmark {{for_blurb}} scope to avoid the N+1 query problem and that the byline can simply be removed from the caching completely.

The byline is the only part of the bookmark_user_module that depends on the pseud and user. So the rest of the blurb cache can remain dependent only on the bookmark itself and {{is_author_of?}}. This means that moving the byline out of the cache avoids needless updates of the rest of the blurb cache when only the pseud or user changed. Breaking up the caching into a byline and blurb cache would keep the user query for computing the cache key for the byline, so that wouldn’t reduce the amount of database queries. So “just don’t cache it” is simpler overall.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps to reproduce*

1. Log in
2. Browse > Works
3. Follow a title to access a work
4. At the bottom of the work, press "Kudos"
5. Hi, username! > My Preferences > Change My User Name
6. Fill in required information
7. Press "Change User Name"
8. Press "OK" to confirm the name change
9. Return to the work and notice your old username is still in the kudos list

*What should happen*

The username information in the kudos should switch to your new username as quickly as possible. (This might take a while, since we'll have to look up every work the user has kudosed. However, in terms of performance, we're okay with doing this.)

*Notes*

Kudos belong to users, so when the user_id remains the same but the _login_ of the user changes, it's a plain old caching issue.

Kudos are cached in two places, and the cache key is dependent on whether the _work_ has been updated:

* The partial that is used at the bottom of the work: [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ff332552fadbec7161f5e0bd5a4c904f333ba88e/app/views/kudos/_kudos.html.erb#L4|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ff332552fadbec7161f5e0bd5a4c904f333ba88e/app/views/kudos/_kudos.html.erb#L4]
* The index that displays if you follow the "and # more users" link on works with lots of kudos, or which you can access by going to [http://test.ao3.org/works/#####/kudos:|http://test.ao3.org/works/#####/kudos:] [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ff332552fadbec7161f5e0bd5a4c904f333ba88e/app/views/kudos/index.html.erb#L7|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ff332552fadbec7161f5e0bd5a4c904f333ba88e/app/views/kudos/index.html.erb#L7]

If the work creator or an admin edits the work you've kudosed, that _will_ expire the cached kudos section and your name will update to match your new username.

*Testing*

The kudos list will be cached for 60 minutes, so it may take an hour (or slightly longer) for changes to appear.

*Steps to reproduce*
1. Log in as a user with archivist permissions
2. Post > Import Work
3. Paste in a URL
4. Check "Import for others ONLY with permission"
5. Fill in "Author Name"
6. Fill in "Author Email" with an email address you _can_ access, but which is _not_ the email address for an existing Archive account
7. Check "Post without previewing (STRONGLY recommended if importing for others!)"
8. Press "Import"
9. Log out
10. Follow the "Claim or remove your works here" link in the "Invitation to claim works" email you received
11. Under "Other Options," choose "Leave my works in the care of the archivist"
12. Choose "Do not email me in the future when works are imported with this email address"
13. Press "Update"
14. You'll be redirected to the homepage and see a blue flash notice: "Okay, we'll leave things the way they are! You can use the email link any time if you change your mind."
15. Repeat steps 1-8 using a different URL but the same email address

*What should happen*
I shouldn't get an email. Also, the flash message in step 14 should include the sentence, "Your preferences have been saved."

*What happens instead*
I get an email.

*Notes*
Unlike with other actions, we redirect and return immediately after saving the "leave me work in the care of the archivist" decision:
https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/external_authors_controller.rb#L67

This means we never get to the code that actually updates the do not email preference. It also means choosing *"From now on, do not import works with this email address" while choosing "Leave my works in the care of the archivist" will fail in the same way, so please test this too*.

Removing the redirect solves the issue with the preference not updating. However, it means you get the "Your preferences have been saved" notice even if you don't touch the do not email/do not import preferences, which is a little odd. However! That's what currently happens if you choose to orphan or delete the works without touching the do not email/do not import setting, so it's consistent, just... not totally right. We may or may not want to raise an issue for that.

26/Jun/17 4:22 AM;557058:85e7b59e-f3ad-4868-81c9-145d4251c741;Every time you import a work, the code rounds up all unclaimed works for that external author and adds them to the user account that claimed that external author. Since the orphaned works don't already belong to the user, it will helpfully dump them back onto the user's account. So two things probably need to happen to stop this:

1. Orphaning should also destroy any ExternalCreatorships associated with the work (so the work no longer belongs to the external author in the first place)
2. To prevent this happening for previously orphaned works and in the general interest of robustness, the claim code should exclude works belonging to the orphan_account from its "round up previous works" process

column27:
*Steps to reproduce:*
# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required information
# Press Preview
# Press Save Without Posting
# Follow Add Chapter
# Fill in required information
# Press Preview
# Press Post

*What should happen:*
Both chapters should be posted. The work should show Chapters: 2/2. You should be able to access it.

*What happens instead:*
Only the second chapter is posted. The work shows Chapters: 1/?. If you are logged in as anyone other than the work creator, you can't access the work -- you get redirected to your user page with the message, "Sorry, you don't have permission to access the page you were trying to reach." If you're logged out, you get redirected to the log in page with the same error message.

*Notes:*
If you do Post Without Preview on the second chapter, everything works fine: both chapters are posted, the work is accessible by everyone, and it shows Chapters: 2/2.

When AO3-4924 is merged, there will be a pending spec for this in spec/controllers/chapters_controller_spec.rb. 

AO3-4313 "Chapter by Chapter mode gives 500 error when a work's chapters are reordered to make a draft chapter the first chapter" might also be of interest -- this is a way to make the first chapter a draft without reordering.

column1: Series: Using "Remove Me As Author" on co-authored series does not update byline in meta
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps to reproduce:*
# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required information
# Check "Add co-creators?"
# Fill in the newly-revealed field with another user's name, e.g. testy4
# Check "This work is part of a series"
# Fill in "Or create and use a new one" with a name for your series, e.g. Test Series
# Press "Post Without Preview"
# From the posted work, follow one of the links to your series
# Choose "Remove Me As Author" on the series page
# Choose "OK" on the confirmation pop-up

*What happens*
- The page reloads with the blue flash message, "You have been removed as an author from the series and its works." 
- The buttons for editing/managing the series are gone. 
- My name is removed from the work blurb. 
- The word "Creators" in the series meta is now "Creator." 
- *However*, it still lists two creators after "Creator."

So I am indeed removed from actually _being_ a creator, but my name still appears in the byline. 

*What should happen instead*
My name should be removed from the actual list of series creators. (In other words, it should now say, "Creator: testy4" in the meta.)

*Notes*
This is the same byline caching that causes some of the issues under the epic AO3-5051 "Changes to pseud or username do not update all user creations."

column1: In the Admin user search, make it possible to search for either exact or partial matches for both username and email
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Current setup:

When logged in as Admin, the Manage Users > Find users page (http://archiveofourown.org/admin/users) currently has a single box to enter either a username or email address. Choosing "Find" will run a search for all usernames, pseuds, and emails that contain the search string.

The problem:

For short or common strings, this search can return tens of thousands of users. An admin (for example, a Support or Abuse staffer) trying to look up an email address for a given username will have to sort through many, many pages of results to find the right user.

The desired fix:

*Replace the "Name or email" box with two boxes, one for "Username" and one for "Email"
*Add a tickbox for "Exact match?", which, when ticked, will search only for usernames, pseuds, or email addresses which _exactly_ match the string entered.

(We don't want to _always_ require an exact match, to allow searching for typoed emails or usernames, all users with emails from the same domain, etc.)

h2. Steps to replicate:

1) Go to the main Collections page at [http://archiveofourown.org/collections|http://archiveofourown.org/collections]
2) Choose "Open Challenges"
3) Stay on "All Challenges" ([http://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_challenges)|http://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_challenges)] or go to "Gift Exchange Challenges" ([http://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_ge_challenges)|http://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_ge_challenges)] or "Prompt Memes Challenges" ([http://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_pm_challenges)|http://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_pm_challenges)]

h2. What you expect to see:

A list of all open challenges, all open gift exchanges, or all open prompt memes, respectively, sorted as described by the text on the page: "The following challenges are currently open for sign-ups! Those closing soonest are at the top."

h2. What you see instead:

The Gift Exchange Challenges and Prompt Meme Challenges page are each capped at 15 challenges. 

The All Challenges page is capped at 15 Gift Exchanges and 15 Prompt Memes. The page is constructed with the 15 Gift Exchanges above the 15 Prompt Memes.

h2. How things should be:

Having some currently open challenges fail to show up on the challenge page if there are more than 15 open challenges, and Prompt Memes be listed after Gift Exchanges even if they’re closing sooner, is not desirable behavior.

h3. Ideally:

* Each of the three Open Challenges page should show _every_ open challenge of the correct type
* We'd paginate the list, as we do the main Collections page
* The All Challenges page should have prompt memes and gift exchange in the same list, sorted chronologically

h3. If we could have a pony:

* The Open Challenges pages could be filtered like the main Collections page (including the sorting options)
* The sorting options would also include “Date Sign-ups Close" and the text at the top of the page would be updated to remove the sentence “Those closing soonest are at the top.”

column1: Certain search criteria (e.g. sort direction, kudos counts) disappear from "Search within results" field when filtering
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
1. Go to a fandom's work listing.
2. Add "sort:>posted" to "search within results".
3. Sort and Filter

Unexpected result: "sort:>posted"  is not shown in "search within results". It is shown in URL as "sort%3A%3Eposted". Sorting prefence IS kept, but is hidden. 

4. Go to page 2 of search.

Unexpected result: URL information changed to "sort_column%5D=created_at&work_search%5Bsort_direction%5D=asc". Sorting preference IS kept, but changed from previous information.

*Notes*

This also happens with other options like:

* words:<10000
* kudos>50
* kudos:100

It does not happen with options like:

* expected_number_of_chapters:1
* restricted:true
* -filter_ids:264659

sort:words, sort:kudos, sort:author, etc _will_ disappear from the box, _but_ the "Sort by" dropdown will be set to the correct option.

The QueryCleaner code that is responsible for this is _also_ responsible for the syntax error that occurs when attempting to search for things like {{words: 1000 OR kudos: 90}}.
column147:
24/Mar/19 6:59 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;Counting options are removed from the query field: https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/be81dfa7d28382286186dd820fdf4e31bdd5ef4f/app/models/search/query_cleaner.rb#L51

Sorting options are removed from the query field: https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/be81dfa7d28382286186dd820fdf4e31bdd5ef4f/app/models/search/query_cleaner.rb#L67 and also moved into their own fields, which is why the "Sort by" dropdown gets set.

This only happens for work filtering. Other filters don't use the QueryCleaner class.

In the end the problem is we are using the same field for multiple purposes:
- Things like {{expected_number_of_chapters:1}} are actual ES query syntax and they need to stay.
- Things like {{sort:words}} and {{words:<10000}} are not ES query syntax but our own syntax. If we leave them in the query field, they would be sent to ES and throw off search results.

So... I don't know.

column148:
01/Sep/22 1:43 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Picked a single-chapter work available on both staging & production. The text in the box was nearly identical, aside from the host name (staging vs. production). The Twitter link was identical aside from the host name. The tumblr link was not quite identical – in addition to the host name difference, it had a bunch of {{%0A}} characters (newlines) encoded in the URL.

When I clicked the two tumblr share buttons, the summary at the bottom didn’t look any different (despite the extra newlines in the URL), but the link at the top had two different titles:

* *Staging:* TITLE (100 words) by AUTHOR \[AO3]
* *Production:* TITLE - AUTHOR - FANDOM \[Archive of Our Own]

My guess as to what’s going on: when you try to share, tumblr accesses the link to retrieve the title. If it finds the title – as it does in production – it overrides the one specified by the share widget. If it doesn’t find the title – as it does in staging, because staging is password-protected – it falls back to the title specified by the widget.

That would explain the extra “Chapter 1” for the multichapter work, since for a logged out user, the work link on a multichapter work will automatically redirect to the first chapter, which has “Chapter 1” as part of its title.

*EDIT:* Yep, tried again with a restricted work, and the titles are:

* *Staging:* TITLE (111 words) by AUTHOR \[AO3]
* *Production:* New Session | Archive of Our Own

tumblr is definitely just fetching the page and using the title for production.

column1: Comment validation prevents deletion
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Create more than one comment by the same user on the same work (top level comments, not replies). Then add replies to both of them. Try to delete both original comments - the first one should work, but the second one will fail, because when a comment is part of a thread, we mark it as deleted instead of actually destroying it. When we do that, we set the content to "deleted comment", but unfortunately, we won't let you save two comments with the exact same content on the same thing.

Fix: skip the uniqueness validation when the comment is being marked deleted. Then both comments should be able to be deleted.

/^([<>]*)\s*([\d -]+)\s*(year|week|month|day|hour)s?(\s*ago)?s*$/

*NOTE: WE NEED TO REVIEW THIS ISSUE AND DECIDE WHAT THE BEHAVIOR USED TO BE*

1. Post a work
2. Choose "Add Chapter" on top of work
3. Fill in information and Preview
4. Save Without Posting to create a draft chapter
5. Choose "Add Chapter" again
6. Fill in information and post

On production, the chapter you made in steps 5-6 posts as Chapter 2, and the draft chapter gets bumped to Chapter 3.

We should stick with the production behavior. column1: Excessive calls to Tag.reset_filter_count in Tag.remove_filter_taggings
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Tag.remove_filter_taggings contains too many calls to Tag.reset_filter_count -- one for each FilterTagging that gets deleted. Since each call to reset_filter_count forces the database to count all visible works in the filter (which requires a join between two tables, and conditions on both), I believe this results in runtime quadratic in the number of works in the tag. It would be better to keep it linear, and only call reset_filter_count once per filter.

This is more of a runtime change than a functionality change, but to verify that the pull request hasn't completely stripped out the ability to fix the filter counts when wrangling, I believe this test will work:

1. Pick two small fandom tags, one canonical, one non-canonical.
2. Count the number of works in both tags.
3. Syn the non-canonical fandom to the canonical fandom.
4. Verify that when you view the canonical fandom on the Fandoms page, the number listed beside the fandom has changed. (You may have to wait a few minutes.)
5. De-syn the non-canonical fandom.
6. Verify that when you view the canonical fandom on the Fandoms page, the number listed beside the fandom has gone back down. (You may have to wait a few minutes.)

(And of course, AO3-3830 and AO3-4965 mean you might have to try a few times to get wrangling to stick.)

h2. Notes
break-word supposedly only works in WebKit browsers like Chrome and Safari, but the screenshots above are from iOS Firefox.

Word breaking only happens on very narrow screens, like phones held in portrait mode.

column1: Revisit desired autocomplete behavior
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
There are a couple of questions to consider about autocomplete behavior.

When you enter "A & B" into the tags autocomplete, what are the desired results?
- If there is a tag "A & B", exactly the same as the autocomplete, should that be the only result? Or just the first result? What if there's also a tag "A & B & C"? Or a tag "C & A & B"? Or a tag "B & A & C"?
- If the only tag containing both the token A and the token B is "B & A", should that be the only result? Or just the first result?
- What if the only tag containing both tokens is "A/B", with an incorrect symbol?
- If there are no tags matching both A and B, it seems logical to include results for tags matching A or tags matching B. Should tags matching the "&" also be included?
- Should tags starting with "A &" be prioritized over tags starting with "A/", since they contain the correct symbol?

What about the other symbols? Currently, the ampersand, the hyphen, the tilde, the double quote, the forward slash, and both left and right parentheses are handled one way, while the remaining symbols (e.g. vertical bar, period, colon, square brackets) are handled differently. So you can use autocomplete to get a list of tags containing a vertical bar, but not to get a list of tags containing an ampersand.
- Is this the desired behavior?
- Should it be possible to search for tags with just an ampersand?
- Should it be impossible to search for tags with just a vertical bar?
- Does it depend on the context? e.g. It might be too resource-intensive to do autocomplete for an ampersand in all tags, but not if you're just trying to get a list of all the "&" relationships in a particular fandom.

What about words like "the"? If the user enters "The L" into the autocomplete, it seems like it should include tags like "The L-Word" and "The Last Unicorn".
- Should it also include "The A-Team" because both tags share the word "The"?
- What about "They Live" or "Lost" or even "Thelonious Monk"?
- How should the search results be ranked? Is "They Live" automatically a better match than "Lost", or should it depend on their taggings counts?

Once elasticsearch has been upgraded, it might be good to try reimplementing the autocomplete code using elasticsearch's autocomplete capabilities. Elasticsearch probably already handles many of these questions in a reasonable way.

We've received numerous complaints, across all browsers and platforms, of ePub files for works download as zip files, or simply opening in the browser as gibberish:

 !epub_broken.jpg|thumbnail! 

It appears that if the ePub is not the first file generated (e.g. the HTML file exists), the content type is incorrectly set to text/plain:

{code:java}
curl -I http://ao3-app98:7084/downloads/Cr/Creator/2592860/File%20Name.epub
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Date: Sun, 24 Sep 2017 08:20:56 GMT
Connection: close
Last-Modified: Sun, 24 Sep 2017 08:20:36 GMT
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 18965
{code}

It should look like:

{code:java}
curl -I http://ao3-app98:7084/downloads/Cr/Creator/2592860/File%20Name.epub
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Date: Sun, 24 Sep 2017 08:20:36 GMT
Connection: close
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
Content-Type: application/epub+zip
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="File Name.epub"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary
Cache-Control: private
X-Request-Id: 20f2e13b-f870-46f7-a7cb-e1df60782ed1
X-Runtime: 0.695178

{code}

This is caused by the file cache. Because we have other types of caching, we'd like to remove this one.

The problem isn't reproducible outside production, so just make sure downloads still work on staging, and then we'll see if this resolves the issue on production.

column1: Don't display "Synonym of" field on Tag Edit Pages for Canonical Tags
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
On Tag Edit pages (tags/\[TAGNAME]/edit), there is a field in the top section labeled "Synonym of". This field allows wranglers to make the tag a synonym of another tag.

Currently, this field is active for all tags, including Canonicals. This means that a wrangler could accidentally enter a tag into that field and rename very large Canonical tags, possibly causing the servers to tip over. It also tempts wranglers to use shortcuts instead of renaming tags the long way (the long way is preferred because it prevents the filter bug AO3-4965 and tag drop bug AO3-3768, plus the aforementioned server tipping).

We would like the field to be made visible but inactive on Canonical tags for everyone except Admins. (Alternatively, it can be hidden on Canonicals instead, if that's easier.)

*To test:* 
1. Canonize a tag, or go to the edit page of a tag that’s already canonical. There should be no "Synonym of" field.
2. Decanonize the tag. The "Synonym of" field should appear again.
3. Syn the tag to another tag. The "Synonym of" field should display the canonical's name with a red "x" beside it, as it does now.
4. Log into admin. The "Synonym of" field should be present for all tags, including canonical ones.

column1: Prevent using variations on the same email address to join the queue multiple times at once
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Note:*
I don't want to accidentally use someone's actual email address here, so please just assume example.com = gmail.com below, since afaik, only Google behaves this way.

*The problem:*
e.mail@example.com, em.ail@example.com, e.m.ail@example.com and other period-based variations on the address email@example.com can all be in the invitation queue at the same time. 

Spammers use this trick and it makes the queue a pain to clean up. 

*The solution:*
We want to make it so you can't add e.mail@example.com to the queue if email@example.com or em.ail@example.com is already there. You should get an error telling you the email is already in the queue.

*Ideally* we should continue to save the email address in the format the user entered it, in case they are using the period positioning for filtering or some other purpose. (In other words, if I join the queue as e.mail@example.com, the invitation should continue to be sent to e.mail@example.com and _not_ email@example.com.) If it's possible to do that, when I try to use ema.il@example.com to join the queue a _second_ time, the error should say, "[email in format just added, e.g. ema.il@example.com] is already part of our queue as [email in format already in the queue, e.g. e.mail@example.com]."

If there is an Archive account for e.mail@example.com, you should still be able to put ema.il@example.com in the queue. This should only apply to addresses _currently in the queue_.

*Testing notes:*
Please also make sure you have to include the TLD in the email address -- for instance, email@example should not work, but email@example.com should.

column1: ES5 BOT: New indexing code doesn't call successful_reindex.
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
All Searchable objects have a successful_reindex function that's supposed to be called whenever some number of items in the class have been reindexed. The Work class uses this to update the works index cache key for its pseuds, filters, and collections, which is used to cache search results on various pages. So without the successful_reindex callback, it could take up to 20 minutes for a new work to show up in the tags.

If both the new indexing code and the old indexing code are enabled, the callbacks in the old indexing code should help ensure that the cache is properly cleared, so it may be difficult to reproduce this issue at the moment. But the callbacks should be added to the new code before stop_old_indexing is enabled.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27: We have to assume that indexing will fail some of the time, so if we don't get a successful response back from Elasticsearch, we should have a reindex_failures queue to retry those. 26/Oct/17 11:52 AM;557058:8e790ed3-0c6b-4389-8bfd-b66b32dc069d;PR is submitted. Instructions for verifying it works:

If you add `id: "#{id}-series"` back to the attributes merged into the bookmarkable_json in Series, for example, this will make reindexing in bulk Series using BookmarkedSeriesIndexer return document failures. Because the failure this creates will not be fixed with retries, you can also inspect REDIS_GENERAL for the keys BookmarkedSeriesIndexer:first_failures_store, BookmarkedSeriesIndexer:second_failures_store, and BookmarkedSeriesIndexer:permanent_failures_store. The Series IDs and error messages about their failures should eventually all end up in the permanent_failures_store.

You could also disrupt your connect to Elasticsearch and get mostly the same effect.

The IndexSweeper is supposed to fix that sort of thing. However, Elasticsearch organizes bookmarks based on their routing info, which is based on the bookmarkable type & ID, which are stored on REDIS for only two weeks after a bookmark is deleted. So if testy2 had a bookmark deleted more than two weeks before the IndexSweeper was merged (on December 19), the IndexSweeper wouldn't have been able to fix it, and the deleted bookmark would be stuck as a ghost. column1: Gift Exchange test broken by Daylight Savings Time redux
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
A few years ago, [the "Change timezone for a gift exchange" scenario|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/features/gift_exchanges/challenge_giftexchange.feature#L55-L58] broke when daylight saving ended in Alaska (AO3-4132). 

This was fixed by setting the expected non-UTC timezone to PGT (Papua New Guinea) as that timezone does not switch to daylight saving time in summer. Unfortunately, during the work to upgrade to Rails 4 in May 2017, someone set the timezone in that test to Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), so it failed in November 2017 when the expected close date for the gift exchange happened to fall in the PST period instead.

The solution is to reapply the original fix and set it to {{(GMT+10:00) Port Moresby}} and {{PGT}} again, maybe with a note why it's like that and not to change it again, thank you very much.

column1: Regular users see cached admin pages, admins see cached regular pages (again)
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
1. Log in as an admin
2. Go to Admin Posts > Archive FAQ
3. Leave the admin FAQ page open
4. Open another browser or incognito/private window and _don't_ log in as an admin
5. Go to About > FAQ

Surprise! The non-admin will find themselves looking at the admin FAQ page: it will have the teal admin navigation, the Admin | Log Out options in the upper corner, and everything else an admin should see and a regular user should not. This all _seems_ to be easier to reproduce with a logged out user than a logged in one, but it does happen for logged in users as well. 

The opposite happens, too, and it's not just the FAQ page.

1. Logged out, or logged in as a regular user, go to the languages page: http://test.ao3.org/languages
2. Open another browser or incognito/private window and log in as admin
3. Go to the languages page: http://test.ao3.org/languages

The admin will see the non-admin version of the page: no teal navigation, no indication that they are logged in as an admin. (It's tricky to reproduce this after you've already done the steps to make a regular user see the admin pages, but it can happen. You'll have better luck if you log out in both browsers and wait a few minutes.) 

The good news is the non-admin can't actually _do_ anything they're no supposed to, since it appears they're just getting a cached page, but this is still Not Good.

The easiest way to test this is to log in as an admin and then check that you have a cookie called admin_credentials.
- Instructions for checking for specific cookies in Chrome: http://www.wikihow.com/View-Cookies#Google_Chrome_sub
- Instructions for checking for specific cookies in Safari: http://www.loopinsight.com/2015/08/06/how-to-view-safari-cookies/

column1: Update Import URL Mappings Rake task to use AO3 ids
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
[AO3-5125|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5125] added a rake task to update the {{imported_from_url}} field on works imported using a temporary site. It uses a CSV file and works by matching the import URL from the temporary site and changing it to the story's URL on the original archive.

This script assumes that the works still have the original url from the temp site. However, in a recent case, the script apparently caused the works to have a nil {{imported_from_url}} field (or at least the works had a nil field several weeks later).

In this case, it would be better to use the AO3 id to find the imported work, and then replace the {{imported_from_url}} if it is nil or set to the URL from the temporary site (this will stop it overwriting import URLs in the unlikely event that the CSV contains works that were actually imported from elsewhere than the temporary site)

*Testing*
As this is a rake task, it can only be tested manually from the command line on an installation of the Archive. However, I will write an automated test for it to check basic functionality

*Update March 2019*

This task which is very rarely run anymore - partly because this bug made it undesirable to use and because Open Doors updated their policies to reflect that so they no longer offer individual story redirects. However, in the event that we did want to run this again for whatever reason, it would be better if it worked properly.

There are automated tests for it, but if someone with access to Staging wants to test it from the console:

# Update the imported_from_url on two works to, say, [http://foo1|http://foo1] and [http://foo2|http://foo2]
# Create a CSV with the following columns:

{code:java}AO3 id,URL Imported From,Original URL
<AO3 id of foo1 work>,http://foo1,http://bar1
<AO3 id of foo2 work>,http://foo2,http://bar2{code}

3. Run the rake task: {{bundle exec rake opendoors:import_url_mapping <path to CSV>}}

Once this has run successfully, the imported_from_url field for the two works should be [http://bar1|http://bar1] and [http://bar2|http://bar2] respectively.

column1: External work bookmarks don't update to reflect wrangling changes
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
External works bookmarked don't follow current wrangling of fandom tags.

*Steps to reproduce:*

1. Go to Bookmarks Search http://archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search
2. Enter "Dragon Age: Inquisition" in Tag field
3. Select "External Work" from the type dropdown
4. Hit Search
5. Get a list of works.
6. Then try the same search but with "Dragon Age All Media Types" in the Tag field.  
7. Get a list of different works, which don't include the first set of results even though the AMT tag is a parent tag of DA: Inquisition.

*Expected results:*
Searching for a tag in external bookmarks should return results for its child tags, not just that exact tag + synonyms.

*Things to test:*

Create new (sadly, this is not a retroactive fix) bookmarks of external works and series and make sure they appear on the bookmark listings for a) any metatags or mergers that already exist _or_  b) that are added after the bookmark is created. 

Also check that the bookmarks _don't_ appear on the listings for any metatags or mergers you remove after the bookmarks are created. 

Note that it may take several minutes for things to be reindexed and caches to expire.
column147:
20/Nov/17 6:50 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Basically, the problem is if an external work has a tag (kind doesn't matter), and that tag's wrangling changes (e.g. the fandom tag Dragon Age: Inquisition is made a subtag of Dragon Age - All Media Types, or the character tag Samantha Carter is de-synned from Sam Carter), the external work won't move around in bookmark listings as expected (e.g. it won't appear in the new Dragon Age - All Media Types meta tag and it will still appear in the Sam Carter tag).

This isn't due to indexing, though -- if you reindex it, the listing won't update. It's because the filter information isn't getting updated on the external work.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Currently, if you have JavaScript enabled and you edit a bookmark from a bookmark index (e.g. [your own|https://test.ao3.org/users/testy/bookmarks], [for a tag|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/bookmarks], [in a collection|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/4812SP/bookmarks]), the _form_ for updating the bookmark opens on the same page, but when you press "Update" on the form, you are redirected to the individual bookmark (e.g. https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/6785592).

To make things more efficient, the edit form should close and your bookmark information should update without redirecting you.

- If you have JavaScript disabled, the current behavior where you are taken to an edit form, make the changes, submit them, and are redirected to the individual bookmark should not change.
- If you are on a work you have previously bookmarked, choose the Edit Bookmark button, and make and submit changes, you should continue to be redirected to the individual bookmark.
- It's also possible to edit a bookmark while on the work's bookmark page (e.g. https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/710574/bookmarks). Doing this currently redirects to the individual bookmark page. The coder can choose to modify this behavior or leave it as-is -- it can always be done later.

column1: ES5 BOT: Re-enable partial matching for tag search
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Partial matching on names in tag search should work, at the same time we escape most special characters/punctuation to avoid errors.

[https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.0/query-dsl-simple-query-string-query.html]

*How to test*:

* {{abc\*}} should match {{abcd}}.
** Note that the simple query string syntax only supports \* at the end of a term; putting one at the start or in the middle of a search term does not work.
* {{abc}} should not match {{abcd}}.
* {{abc\+}} should match exactly {{abc\+}}, the {{\+}} sign should have no special meanings.
* {{\-}} should have no meaning either (previously a shorthand for exclusion). Try {{x-men}}.
* Slashes should be ignored ({{a/b}} is the same as {{a b}}) unless they're quoted ({{"a/b"}} should match exactly that).



_*ETA (Ariana): the above describes the original implementation \- see comments for the problem this caused and some testing suggestions for the new version*_
column147: 15/Dec/17 4:40 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;We need to use query strings, not simple query string -- the current wildcard behavior on production works at the beginning, middle, and end of strings, and Tag Wrangling uses that behavior frequently.
column148:
15/Jan/18 7:18 AM;557058:85e7b59e-f3ad-4868-81c9-145d4251c741;Here are the scenarios I've tested for the new change:

TagQuery
* performs a case-insensitive search ('AbC' matches 'abc')
* performs a query string search ('ab OR cd' matches 'ab cd', 'ab/cd' and 'ab “cd” ef')
* performs an exact match with quotes ('xgh OR “abc d”' matches 'abc d')
* lists closest matches at the top of the results ('abc' result lists 'abc' first)
* matches every token in any order ('d abc' matches 'abc d' and 'abc-d', but not 'abc' or 'abc+')
* matches tokens with double quotes ('ab "cd" ef' matches 'ab "cd" ef')
* matches tokens with single quotes ('ab'c d' matches 'ab'c d')
* performs a wildcard search at the end of a term ('abc*' matches 'abcd' and 'abcde')
* performs a wildcard search in the middle of a term ('a*d' matches 'abcd')
* performs a wildcard search at the beginning of a term ('*cd' matches 'abcd')
* preserves plus ( + ) character ('abc+' matches 'abc+' and 'abc', but not 'abccc')
* preserves minus ( - ) character ('abc-d' matches 'abc-d', 'abc -d', 'abc d' but not 'abc' or 'abcd')
* preserves minus ( - ) preceded by a space ('abc -d' matches 'abc -d', 'abc d' and 'abc-d', but not 'abc')
* preserves slashes without quotes ('ab/cd' should match 'ab/cd' and 'ab cd')
* matches tags with canonical punctuation ('yuri\!\!\!' on ice matches 'Yuri\!\!\! On Ice')
* matches tags without canonical punctuation ('yuri on ice' matches 'Yuri\!\!\! On Ice')
* matches unicode tags with unicode character ('Dave ♦ Sawbuck' matches 'Dave ♦ Sawbuck')"
* matches unicode tags without unicode character ('dave sawbuck' matches 'Dave ♦ Sawbuck')

(though note that in the last two cases, the diamond character is not indexed separately so you can't find the tag by searching for "♦")

column1: Creator sorting is broken for names starting with numbers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*The problem:*

Sorting a work list by creator using the "Sort by > Author" dropdown of the filters will not properly sort creator names (default pseuds or otherwise) that start with numbers.

*The cause:*

There is an issue in the "sorted_authors" and "sorted_pseuds" methods in the work class. If the first character of a pseud is a special character we remove it; unfortunately due to an error in the regex we're also removing the first character if it is a range of possible things, including numbers.

The offending bit is /^[\+-=_\?!'"\.\/]/

It should have the "\-" escaped so it's not trying to removing anything in the range from "+" to "=", but is instead removing "\-" as intended.

*How to test:*

1) Go to a large tag's work listing (for example, "Alternate Universe")
2) From the "Sort by" dropdown of the filters, choose "Author" and hit "Sort and Filter"
3) Look at the top of the list to see if the creator names with numbers are sorted correctly in order (for example, "007aardvark" should sort before "221b_wombat", which should sort before 666tasmanian_devil).

column1: Old Indexing: StatCounter indexing is broken.
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
The StatCounter indexing code in IndexSubqueue nests all of the stats one level too deep, so the stats that are used for sorting and searching works aren't updated when the StatCounter is reindexed.

*Steps for reproducing:*
# Find a work in a relatively small tag.
# Comment a bunch of times, enough to move up in the rankings if you sort by comments.
# Wait an hour or two for all of the background jobs to be run. Don't edit the work or any of its tags in the meantime, as that will trigger a reindex of the Work (which does properly update the stats).
# View the tag and sort by comments.

I went looking for some examples of this on archiveofourown.org, and found a couple of examples on [page 7 of the Time Loop tag, sorted by comments|http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Time%20Loop/works?commit=Sort+and+Filter&page=7&utf8=✓&work_search%5Bcomplete%5D=0&work_search%5Blanguage_id%5D=&work_search%5Bother_tag_names%5D=&work_search%5Bquery%5D=&work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=comments_count]. The sequence of comment counts, as of the time that I looked at it, was: 65, 65, 64, 63, 63, 62, 62, *64*, 61, 60, *80*, 60, 60, *66*, 59, 58, 58, 58, 57, 56. Of the three works that are out of sequence, one of them has comments from several hours ago, one of them hasn't been commented on since November, and one of them hasn't been commented on since October, so there should have been more than enough time for them to be reindexed.

column1: Old Indexing: Tag search by type doesn't work for newer tags.
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Tag search by type doesn't work for newer tags. The indexing code in IndexSubqueue sets _type equal to Tag.document_type (i.e. "Tag"), while the search code is expecting _type to contain the type of the tag (e.g. "Fandom"). So all tags indexed using IndexSubqueue disappear from the search when you pick a tag type.

*Steps for reproducing:*
# Create or find a new tag with a fairly unique name.
# Search for the tag using tag search with no type specified. See that the tag shows up in the results.
# Restrict the search to only include tags of your new tag's type.
# Notice that the new tag disappears from the search results when it shouldn't.

Even if you don't use a unique name, you can typically see missing tags just by picking a relationship tag from a fairly new fandom and trying to search for it with and without a tag type selected.

Interestingly, it looks like this bug can also cause a tag to show up twice in the search: once from being indexed using Tag.reindex_document, and once from being indexed using IndexSubqueue. This is distinct from the duplicate tag issue in AO3-2349. In fact, when I do [a search for "final fantasy tactics a2"|http://archiveofourown.org/tags/search?utf8=✓&query%5Bname%5D=final+fantasy+tactics+a2&query%5Btype%5D=], I see *three* versions of the tag: one with the unprintable characters at the end of the link, and two with no unprintable characters (resulting from this bug).

column1: Use ScheduledReindexJob and IndexQueue in cucumber tests.
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Currently, all of the automated cucumber tests involving search rely on:
# The code in lib/searchable.rb that performs synchronous indexing with reindex_document when in the test environment.
# The "all search indexes are updated" step, which deletes and recreates each index from scratch.

As a result, indexing/reindexing in the automated tests doesn't necessarily behave the same way as indexing/reindexing on the deployed version, which queues up items using IndexQueue and periodically runs ScheduledReindexJob to perform the actual indexing. It would be good to modify the tests to more accurately simulate this process, to catch more errors that might occur outside of the test environment.

This is a change that should only affect the tests, and shouldn't require manual QA.

column1: Make updating filter counts asynchronous
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We currently update the filter_counts table (which caches tag uses) in real time when users create new works or edit their tags. These are slow requests, and the counts don't really need up-to-the-minute accuracy, so we should handle this asynchronously instead, ideally adding the tag ids to a set and running a scheduled task hourly or every n hours.

*Testing*
# Pick a medium and go to its page.
# Pick a canonical fandom in that medium.
# Write down the current count associated with that fandom.
# Create a new work in that fandom.
# Wait 1 hour.
# Check the medium's page again and verify that the count has increased by 1.

You can also do similar tests with other actions that should change the count: e.g. deleting a work, adding or removing a canonical tag from an existing work, wrangling a tag, etc.

column1: ES5 BOT: Pseud index doesn't update when a work is updated.
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps to reproduce:*
# Log in as a user.
# Pick a canonical fandom that the user has never written in.
# Post a new work in that fandom.
# Wait for the pseud index to update.
# Search for the canonical fandom in people search, and keep refreshing until the people search is updated and you appear in the search results.

You'd expect to show up in the people search eventually. But because Work.update_pseud_index wraps the list of pseud IDs within another list (making the argument malformed), it won't be updated until something else triggers an update to the pseud index.

Even when the correct pseud IDs are passed in Work.update_pseud_index, there are several ways for a work to be updated that won't trigger an update to all of the relevant pseuds:
# Adding a pre-existing canonical fandom after the work is posted.
# Removing a canonical fandom from the work after it's been posted.
# Removing yourself as an author after the work is posted. (The value of authors_to_sort_on will update, which will cause all of the remaining authors on the work to have their pseuds reindexed -- but not the person trying to remove their name from the work.)
# Orphaning a work after it's been posted. (Just as when removing yourself as an author, the orphan_account will be updated, but not the user trying to orphan their work.)

All of these scenarios should cause the people search to update.

    range = {}

    range[:lte] = options[:date_to].to_date if options[:date_to].present?
    range[:format] = "date_optional_time"
{code}

Or we can follow AO3-5229 and set a limit on the year. I'm undecided...

ETA: we're going with clamping the year to 0-9999.

column147:
12/Jul/21 9:42 AM;557058:0ed2d036-cfdd-4793-9df9-3ec3e141a3cf;I assume “the nofollow update” is [AO3-4200|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4200]?

I personally see nothing in the PR ([https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3137/files|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3137/files] ) that could have introduced this change, so I have a hard time knowing what the old behavior might have been.

@Sarken I’d be happy about your input here.

On a technical side, the current behavior doesn’t technically add the “http://archiveofourown.org/…” prefix in the HTML at all, the browser will simply interpret urls without a protocol (http(s)://) as if that prefix was present. This is quite useful because users can leave links to other pages on AO3 without adding the prefix at all\!

For the case you describe, it’s hard to say what we could do to fix this issue. Optimistically adding a protocol prefix has several problems:

* It breaks relative links as described above (e.g. a user links to /works/31439690). This isn’t a very commonly known feature of HTML links, but it would probably still break some links for users.
* Adding “http://” or “https://” as protocol prefix is pure guesswork since we can’t tell which of these the URL actually supports. Adding the wrong one would break the link just as adding none at all would.

Overall, I think the current behavior is perhaps the least confusing, if at least because it literally follows what the user instructed it to do (even if that was nonsense).

I’m not familiar enough with the HTML cleaner to know if this is a viable option, but it might make sense to warn the user about their problematic link instead of trying to fix it ourselves. However, this seems like a major feature worth considering more.

The “nofollow“ change in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4200|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4200|smart-link] does not affect how relative links work, and I don’t think there’s any reasonable way for us to auto-correct links since relative links are totally valid. 31/Jan/18 6:29 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Part of this issue seems pretty straightforward to fix. The keys in BookmarkableQuery are of the form "bookmark_#\{type\}_count," but the QueryResult class is looking for keys of the form "#\{type\}_count," so it doesn't find the nested bookmark counts and falls back on using the bookmarkable counts, instead. The automated test added in the PR didn't catch the issue because the tests don't use the new search by default.

However, I played around with ElasticSearch because I was curious about what was being counted, and as far as I can tell, the bookmarkable tag aggregations count *all* bookmarks on all works matching the filters. This includes private bookmarks in all searches, bookmarks by all users in a search for a particular user's bookmarks, bookmarks missing a bookmark tag that the user selected, bookmarks hidden by an admin, etc. As long as there is at least one bookmark matching the search parameters, every other bookmark on that bookmarkable seems to be included in the count.

That part of the issue seems a bit trickier.

15/Mar/18 8:51 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;It should be fine to leave it the way it is in that case! 

Just to summarize the filter counts and filter behavior in case it's useful:

- In the work filters, the counts for all tags represent the number of times that exact tag has been used on a work. Selecting one of the tags for inclusion will return works tagged with that exact tag, its synonyms, and its subtags. Selecting one of the tags for exclusion will likewise exclude works tagged with that exact tag, its synonyms, and its subtags.
 
- In the bookmark filters, the counts for tags of all types *except* Bookmarker's Tags represent the number of times that exact tag has been used on a bookmarked item (i.e. a work, series, or external work). Selecting one of the tags for inclusion will return bookmarked items tagged with that exact tag, its synonyms, and its subtags. Selecting one of the tags for exclusion will likewise exclude bookmarked items tagged with that exact tag, its synonyms, and its subtags.

- In the bookmark filters, the counts for Bookmarker's Tags represent the number of times that exact tag has been used on bookmarks, *not* bookmarked items. Selecting one of the tags for inclusion will *only* return bookmarks tagged with that exact tag, *not* any of its syns or subtags. Selecting one of the tags for exclusion will *only* exclude bookmarks tagged with that exact tag, *not* any of its syns or subtags (once we merge https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3261).

column1: ES5 BOT: IndexSweeper fails for bookmarkable items.
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
The BookmarkableIndexer appends "-series" or "-work" or "-external_work" to the IDs of all of the items that it indexes. So when the IndexSweeper retrieves the IDs of any failures, those IDs will have the extra suffixes. When those IDs are passed back to a BookmarkableIndexer class, the batch function will call routing_info(id), which will call document_id(id), which will append the suffix again -- this time incorrectly.

This results in (a) incorrect IDs if a failure is followed by a successful reindex, and (b) the IndexSweeper viewing each iteration of failure as a separate document. So in the event of a permanent failure, the IndexSweeper and the AsyncIndexer will keep calling each other until the ID becomes so long that Elasticsearch throws an error.

*Testing*
This one is very difficult to test manually. I think you'd have to deliberately modify the code to produce an error, and then watch the failure stores. One way to consistently produce errors is to modify the line @batch << document(object) in Indexer.batch to read @batch << document(object).merge("_id" => "asdf"), since Elasticsearch doesn't like it when you try to embed the "_id" in your document.

column1: Support tickets should include rollout information
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We're going to be using [rollout|https://github.com/fetlife/rollout] to gradually, well, roll out Elasticsearch 6.0 to users. While this goes on, Support needs to know if a ticket is from a user who is on Elasticsearch 6.0 or 0.90. Therefore, we need to make sure that info gets submitted to the ticket tracker.

Support has already created a field on their side. It is called "Rollout" (so we can reuse it in the future) and it accepts up to 20 characters. When a support request is submitted, the field should receive either "ES 6.0" or "ES 0.90," depending on which version the user is on. This information should _not_ be editable or visible to the user -- basically, it should be like the user_agent or site_revision fields.

The report information is set here: https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/a124b745919786d353036ca6ef71c46fef04221e/app/models/feedback.rb#L54

If for some reason the field name needs to be changed, or the field needs to allow more characters, ping Support chairs CJ Record and Nary on Slack.

*To test:*
# Go to a works page and check if you have exclusion filters. If you do, you're on ES 6.0; if you don't, you're on 0.90
# Follow "Technical Support and Feedback" link in the footer
# Fill out the required information
# Submit
# Grab a Support staffer and ask them to confirm that:
## they received the ticket 
## the ticket contains the correct information in the "Rollout" field
## they received the email to the support-extra mailing list
## the email contains the rollout info _and_ the user agent info

It would probably be wise to check with each of the following:
* a logged in user who is on ES 6.0
* a logged out user who is on ES 0.90
* a logged out user

Please also make sure the IP address and user agent fields work correctly, since that code has been refactored.

# In an autocomplete field like Additional Tags, do one of the following:

## enter some text that uses the key in the same position as the QWERTY keyboard's comma key (e.g. ת on a [Hebrew keyboard|https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_keyboard#/media/File:Hebrew_keyboard_layout.png])

*What happens*
If you press the comma key on your non-QWERTY keyboard, a comma appears in the field and nothing else happens. You'd expect it to finalize the entry of the tag, making it appear over the field the same way pressing the comma key on a QWERTY keyboard does.

If you press the key that's in the same position as a QWERTY keyboard's comma, it finalizes entry of the tag, making it appear above the field. This effectively prevents you from using whatever letter/character is on that key. You'd expect to be able to use that letter/character normally. (If you're using a QWERTY keyboard, you can also see this behavior by trying to use the < character, which requires you to use the comma key in combination with the Shift key.)

*Notes*
The autocomplete JavaScript [uses the code attribute for all keyboard functionality|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1b70938c17edc6d59b06ba3f1f8ec5d01cabeaf5/public/javascripts/jquery.tokeninput.js#L63]. We probably need to considering using [the key attribute|https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2016/04/keyboardevent-keys-codes] instead, because we care about the character being inputted, not the physical key being pressed. KeyboardEvent.key has [good support on new browsers|https://caniuse.com/#search=keyboardevent.key], but it will likely break things for anyone using an unsupported browser.

column147:
06/Feb/18 1:33 PM;557058:85e7b59e-f3ad-4868-81c9-145d4251c741;It looks as if the cause of this behaviour is this line https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/models/search/work_query.rb#L210 which calls *split_query_text_phrases* https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/models/search/query.rb#L153-L160. This method only splits tokens on commas and then wraps each resulting phrase in quotes and prefixes it with e.g. {{tag:}}. So if you search for {{people doing things}}, it will generate a query string for Elasticsearch containing {{tag:\"people doing things\"}} - i.e. it requests an exact match on the phrase "people doing things".

"OK, so what if I enter commas?" you might ask. Well, unfortunately, though the UI will convincingly display each comma-separate token as if it were a tag, any commas in that field are stripped out by https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/models/work_search.rb#L286-L294 which is still being called by the new code to tidy up the search field inputs, but was originally designed as input to https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/models/work_search.rb#L286-L294 which used to just throw each individual word at ES without wrapping phrases in quotes.

I suppose we "just" need to give ES the individual words of the tags if we want the old behaviour back.
column148:
06/Feb/18 3:32 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;That sounds like what's causing "People Doing Things" to return no results. The combination of deleting commas and searching in phrases seems like a very bad idea -- that means that if I search for multiple non-canonical tags, even in different fields, it will only return works where all of the words from all of the non-canonical tags appear sequentially in the same order.

Interestingly, the automated test uses a single word search: "AU." So it would be unaffected by the phrase issue, but instead fails for a different reason: the definition of TaggableQuery.named_tags. Before, non-canonical tags were only used in the tag text search. In the new search, they're treated just the same way as canonical tags: their IDs are calculated and they're added to the list of filter_ids. (And non-canonical tag IDs are now added to the list of filter IDs in the indexing process.)

I'm not sure how much of this behavior should be fixed, vs. how much the docs/test should change. (I don't feel comfortable updating the docs, which is why I left the bug unclaimed.)

We can then examine whether there is a remaining issue with how we treat canonical vs non-canonical tags and open a new issue for that separately if necessary.

h2. What happens
testy2 is removed as co-creator of that chapter, but retains co-creator access to the work as a whole

h2. What should happen
If a co-creator who was added only to one or more chapters (and not as co-creator of the whole work) removes themselves from the last chapter for which they were credited, it should also remove them as a co-creator of the work and remove all associated edit permissions etc.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps to reproduce*
# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill out the required fields
# Under Relationships, enter either 
#* a canonical relationship tag and one of its synonyms, e.g. Lee Adama/Kara Thrace and Lee/Kara
#* two syns of the same canonical tag, e.g. Lee/Kara and Kara/Lee
# Post Without Preview
# Wait a few minutes for indexes to update 
# Hi, username > My Works
# In "Search within results," enter "otp: true" (minus quotes)
# Press "Sort and Filter"

I expect the work to appear in the listings. Even though it has more than one relationship tag, the wrangling system knows both tags mean the same thing.

It does not appear. It _does_ appear if you instead search for "otp: false" (again, minus quotes).
