*What happens*
I get a 500 error. If I go back to the edit page, the Fandom has saved, but not the MetaTag.

- Test Tag's Metatag's Metatag
-- Test Tag's Metatag
--- Test Tag
---- Test Tag's Subtag

*Notes* 
The error happens on [line 56 of the meta_tagging model|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/fb9d8018af57af394d08500908a11bd98dd1df6f/app/models/meta_tagging.rb#L56]: a no method error for update_attribute! because this method does not exist in Rails -- only update_attributes, update_attributes!, and update_attribute do.

column1: Series bookmarks do not appear on tag's bookmark page when a formerly canonical tag is synned to a new tag
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce
# Log in as a Tag Wrangler
# Post a new work in a new series, with a new tag:
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required information, using a new tag for the Fandom, e.g. "New Fandom Test Tag"
##* Note: It doesn't _have_ to be a new fandom tag, but it's easier/quicker for testing purposes
## Check "This work is part of a series"
## Fill in "Or create and use a new one:" with a name for your series, e.g. "New Test Series"
## Post Without Preview
# Canonize the tag:
## Go to the Edit page for your new tag, e.g. http://test.ao3.org/tags/New%20Fandom%20Tag/edit
## Check "Canonical"
## Press "Save changes"
# Make your work and series bookmarks:
## Hi, username! > My Works
## Follow the linked title of the work you just posted
## Press "Bookmark" to go to the bookmark form
## Press "Create" to save the bookmark
## Follow the link to the work's series
## Press "Bookmark Series" to open the bookmark form
## Press "Create" to save the bookmark
# Wait 10 or 15 minutes -- as long as it takes for the work and the bookmarks to appear on the work (http://test.ao3.org/tags/New%20Fandom%20Tag/works) and bookmark listings (http://test.ao3.org/tags/New%20Fandom%20Tag/bookmarks)
# Make your test tag a synonym of another tag:
## Go to the tag's edit page, e.g. http://test.ao3.org/tags/New%20Fandom%20Tag/edit
## Fill in "Synonym of" with another brand new tag, e.g. "Canonical New Fandom Test Tag"
## Press "Save changes"
# Wait 10, 15, or even 20 minutes while the wrangling change takes place

h1. What happens
The bookmark of the work correctly appears on the bookmark listing (http://test.ao3.org/tags/Canonical%20New%20Fandom%20Tag/bookmarks). The bookmark of the series does not.

h1. What should happen
All bookmarks should appear on the bookmark listing.

h1. Notes
Could be related:
* AO3-4540 (I suspect it's the same cause)
* AO3-5253 (Basically the same problem with external works)

Before I turned the canonical tag into a synonym, these were the filters on the series:

{code:java}
2.3.0 :004 > s_before = Series.find(63418)
 => #<Series id: 63418, created_at: "2018-02-20 00:58:36", updated_at: "2018-02-20 00:58:36", title: "Test Series", summary: nil, notes: nil, hidden_by_admin: false, restricted: false, complete: false, summary_sanitizer_version: 0, notes_sanitizer_version: 0> 
2.3.0 :006 > s_before.filter_ids
 => [10, 1218352, 14] 
{code}

And after I did the synning:

{code:java}
2.3.0 :011 > s_after = Series.find(63418)
 => #<Series id: 63418, created_at: "2018-02-20 00:58:36", updated_at: "2018-02-20 00:58:36", title: "Test Series", summary: nil, notes: nil, hidden_by_admin: false, restricted: false, complete: false, summary_sanitizer_version: 0, notes_sanitizer_version: 0> 
2.3.0 :013 > s_after.filter_ids
 => [10, 1218352, 14, 1218355] 
{code}

So the good news is the new filter_id (1218355) is getting added to the series -- but I suspect it's just trickling down to the series from the work update, since series tags come from the works -- so the series bookmark will indeed show up if the series bookmark gets reindexed. The bad news is the old filter_id (1218352) is still attached.

Part of the issue might be that [the reindex_taggables method|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e2c284a95ed1feb8d23ad33cad6ee2c4b2ec1174/app/models/tag.rb#L680] only reindexes works and bookmarks that use the tag. If the tag is on the bookmarkable (i.e. the series), the bookmark will not be reindexed.

Both the series and work bookmarks appear in the listing after synning. Fixed!

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Use a browser's "translate" feature on a page where we list languages in their local names and be amused how the browser bungles the translation. Or use a screen reader to let it read out the language names and be amused that it pronounces everything in an English accent.

Note: In practice, it turns out it doesn’t necessarily help with these things, even though it’s supposed to, so you have to check the attribute is present in the source.

The solution is to add a lang-attribute to the DOM element containing the localised language name to let the browser know what language this is in. So for the German language entry, the attribute should be {{lang="de"}} for example.

column1: Related Works page includes listings for works in anonymous and unrevealed collections
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
A user's Related Works page will include listings of works inspired by works in unrevealed and anonymous collections.

*Example:* 

[https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/coaldustcanary/related_works|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/coaldustcanary/related_works]

"Filth" ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1067371)|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1067371] is currently set as Unrevealed, but on my related works page, "Not at all filthy by testy5 " is listed as a related work. This was also the case when the collection was set to Anonymous.

*To replicate:*

# Log in as User A
# Post a work to an anonymous (or unrevealed) collection
# Log out
# Log in as User B
# Post a work inspired by the work from Step 2
# Go to the related works page for User A, i.e. https://test.archiveofourown.org/UserA/related_works

*What happens:*

The Related Works page for the creator of the anonymous/unrevealed work (User A) will list the work "inspired by" said work. This means everyone now knows that User A wrote the anonymous/unrevealed work.

*What should happen:*

This information should only be included if you are currently logged in _as_ User A. Otherwise, works inspired by User A’s anonymous or unrevealed works should be excluded.

*Notes:*

There’s a similar issue that occurs if User A writes an anonymous or unrevealed work that’s marked as inspired by one of User B’s works. Those works are currently included on User A’s related works page as “A work in an unrevealed or anonymous challenge,” with a link to the inspiring work. This means that if the related work is approved, it’s fairly straightforward to track down User A’s anonymous work. (Just follow the link to the inspiring work, and check the “Works inspired by this one:” section.)

Instead, anonymous/unrevealed works by User A that are inspired by a work by User B should not be included on User A’s related works page for anyone other than User A. (It’s okay if they occur on User B’s related works page, though, as long as they don’t reveal the association with User A.)

This should also apply for translations, as well as remixes.

column1: Fix intermittent test failure in pseud searches
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We have a few tests related to pseud indexing (for AO3-5326 and AO3-5327) [that does this|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f759e3dab530c9c7fdf3de38d270c32599bba2d2/spec/models/pseud_search_form_spec.rb#L64-L67]:
{code:ruby}
bookmark = create(:bookmark, bookmarkable_id: work.id)
run_all_indexing_jobs
result = PseudSearchForm.new(name: bookmark.pseud.name).search_results.first
expect(result).to eq bookmark.pseud
{code}

The last assertion often fails because:

- fields are faked in factories as random alphanumeric strings, then indexed by PseudIndexer with the "simple" analyzer (e.g. "le5kct26" is actually "le kct")
- PseudQuery [doesn't set the operator on name queries|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f759e3dab530c9c7fdf3de38d270c32599bba2d2/app/models/search/pseud_query.rb#L55], so "le kct" will match anything with "le" OR "kct"
- the query can return results in the wrong order (because of a small number of results on [multiple shards|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.2/consistent-scoring.html], see the tests for AO3-5265), so the pseud we want is not necessarily the first one

How to fix so the tests should pass more consistently:

- We set the pseud names ourselves instead of letting factories do it, less chance of some random name appearing in the desired results.
- We limit the number of shards to 1.

Since we're not testing search relevance/order, and the test just needs a pseud search result, I'm going with the first fix.

*How to test*: no manual testing required.

column1: ES6: Pseuds indexing ignores numbers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
As indicated in AO3-5358, pseuds are indexed using the *simple* mapping in Elasticsearch. This means that, for example, numbers and punctuation are ignored, such that {{testy2}} and {{testy3}} are both returned in a search on "testy2", and {{man}} or {{x-file}} will be returned for a query on {{x-man}}.

This is the problem that also occurred with the tag mapping (see AO3-5265). The purpose will be to change the behaviour so the following are true:

- a search for *testy2* should return *testy2* first, followed by the other *testy*s 
- a search for *x_file* should return *x_file* first, followed by any other combination of *x* and *file*

column151:
16/Mar/18 3:00 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;I have the pseuds "Hy-phen" and "phen hy," as well as a totally different pseud with "hyphen" in the name.

I people search for "hy-phen" in the "Search all fields" field.

The results include "phen hy," first and then "Hy-phen." The pseud with "hyphen" in the description is not in the results. 

To a user, it's a little unexpected to get the results in that order. You'd expect the exact match first.

To a coder, it makes sense: as far as Elasticsearch is concerned, the query "hy-phen" means "hy AND phen," and the pseuds are tokenized as "hy phen" and "phen hy," making them equally good matches for the query "hy AND phen." 

Considering a) how long Elasticsearch work has been ongoing and b) we're getting the correct results, just in a surprising order, we can live with this, just like we can live with the ordering issue described in point 1 in my previous comment.
column152: 16/Mar/18 7:05 AM;557058:85e7b59e-f3ad-4868-81c9-145d4251c741;Further to Sarken's comments, if we find that the ordering is something users complain about, we can open a new ticket for the ordering issue and consider what the expected behaviour should be. It's likely that any result-ordering fix would revolve around tweaking the query passed to Elasticsearch rather than how the strings are tokenised, so it's something we can address at any point without worrying about the overhead of reindexing.

column1: ES5 BOT: Add separate "Any field" and "Tag" fields for bookmarks and bookmarkables on bookmark search
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
On the [bookmark search form|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search], we have the fields "Any field" and "Tag" which can match either bookmarks or bookmarkables. During the ES6 upgrade, we switch to a parent-child indexing model for bookmarkable-bookmark (to avoid reindexing e.g. all bookmarks when a work is updated), which makes querying across bookmarks and bookmarkables complicated (it's unclear what should be AND'ed or OR'ed together), and leads to issues such as AO3-5301, AO3-5320.

We can avoid this problem by making it explicit to users what they want to match on. Add these fields on the bookmark search form, which correspond to new fields on bookmark filters in AO3-5355 :

- Any field on bookmarked item (form) = Search within results (filters)
- Any field on bookmark (form) = Search bookmarker's tags and notes (filters)
- Bookmarked item's tags (form) = Other work tags to include (filters)
- Bookmarker's tags (form) = Other bookmarker's tags to include (filters)

These should only be visible on the ES6-version of the form.

Help pop-ups will be updated separately.

*Page where the problem can be seen:*
https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/yuletide/bookmarks

*What happens:*
The sidebar says there are 67 bookmarks, but the page header says "1 - 20 of 64 Bookmarked Items in Yuletide." This is because the sidebar count includes:
* bookmarks, not bookmarkable items, and
* bookmarks of deleted works ([Yuletide 2013's|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/yuletide2013/bookmarks] count is off due to it containing 1 bookmark of a deleted item.)

The sidebar count should not include those things.

It's technically correct for the sidebar to count bookmarks -- it does, after all, say "Bookmarks (#)" -- but the discrepancy between that count and the one at the top of the page is probably going to make people think it's broken. We can always consider making the collection sidebar say "Bookmarked Items (#)" instead.

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Follow Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information, making sure to check "This collection is unrevealed"
# Press “Submit”
# Follow Post to Collection
# Fill in required information
# Press “Post”
# Follow Bookmark
# Press “Create”
# Log out
# Follow Search > Bookmarks
# Fill in "Any field on work" with something that matches the work you posted and bookmarked, e.g. General Audiences if you rated the work General Audiences
# To make this easier, fill in Bookmarker with the name of the account you bookmarked the work with
# Also to make this easier, choose "Date Bookmarked" for "Sort by"
# Press Search bookmarks

h2. What happens

The bookmark shows up in the search results, thus telling the world that the bookmarked item is rated General Audiences (or contains that phrase somewhere in the searchable info).

h2. What should happen

The bookmark should not appear in the search results because it is matching on hidden information.

It is okay for it to appear if the bookmarker name, tags, or notes match a search term entered in “Any field on bookmark” (_not_ “Any field on work”), since that information is on the bookmark itself and not hidden.

h2. Deploy notes

Needs a worker restart. Has a post deploy rake task that queues for reindexing: {{bundle exec rake After:reindex_unrevealed_bookmarkable}}

column1: Bookmarks: Language option missing from search and filter interface
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Example URLs*
Bookmark Search page: https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search
Bookmark tag page: https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Suits%20(TV)/bookmarks
User bookmark page: https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/testy/bookmarks
Collection bookmark page: https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/yuletide/bookmarks

*The problem*

We index bookmarks based on the bookmarkable item's language, making it possible to search for bookmarks of works in another language, e.g. Russian: 

* In Elasticsearch 0.90, you can do this by entering bookmarkable_language_id: 30 in "Any field" on the Bookmark Search page, or in "Search within results" on a tag, user, or collection bookmark page
* In Elasticsearch 6, you can do this by entering language_id: 30 in "Any field on work" on the Bookmark Search page, or in "Search within results" on a tag, user, or collection bookmark page

However, there's no way to select a language on either the filters or the search page.

*The solution*
On Elasticsearch 6 -- no need to implement it on 0.90 -- we should add a "Work language" select menu to both the filters and the search page. 

* On the filters, it should be between "Search bookmarker's tags and notes" and "Bookmark types" (to mirror its position of after the search field on work filters)
* On the search page, it should be between "Bookmarker's tags" and the checkbox for "Rec"
** If AO3-5374 is implemented, it can be before or after the field for selecting the type

There should also be automated tests for these fields.

*Notes*
Only works -- not series or external works -- have languages set, so if you specify a language, the results will only be works.

column1: ES5 BOT: Use whitelist, not blacklist, for indexing fields
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Problem:*

When we index a work document, we take a blacklisting approach -- that is, we use "except" to say "index every except these fields": https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/329b7d049861758074749a4b597f9dc681da87d0/app/models/search/work_indexer.rb#L48

This has the potential to go very wrong if we add a new column (say, idk, orphaner_ip_address) to the work table and forget to say "don't index this information."

Indexers for works and bookmarks are affected. Indexers for pseuds, tags, and bookmarkables are already using whitelists.

*Solution:*

Let's instead use "only" to say "index only these fields." 

*Testing note:* 

This is a code issue, not a reproducible bug. To test this, someone with database access to staging will need to get the JSON for a work *before* this code is deployed and things are reindexed. *After* things are reindexed, they should get the JSON for the same work. The JSON things should be identical.

column1: Submitting sign-ups or prompts errors if the only field on the form is Title, Description, or URL
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce.

h2. Prompt Meme

# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in Collection name
# Fill in Display title
# Choose Prompt Meme for Type of challenge, if any
# Submit
# Make sure Sign-up open? is checked
# Under Request Settings, check both Required and Allowed for Title
# Uncheck Allowed for Description
# Fill in 0 for Allowed for all tag types
# Submit
# Follow the Prompt Form link
# Fill in the Title field
# Submit

h2. Gift Exchange 

# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in Collection name
# Fill in Display title
# Choose Gift Exchange for Type of challenge, if any
# Submit
# Make sure Sign-up open? is checked
# Make sure the Allowed and Required fields for Number of offers per sign-up are both set to 1 (we can leave requests the way they are)
# For Offer Settings (again, we can leave requests they way they are)
## make sure Allowed is checked for Details/Description
## fill in 0 for Allowed for all tag types
# Submit
# Follow the Sign-up Form link
# Press Submit

h1. What happens

The page reloads with red error messages and no prompts (Prompt Meme) or requests or offers (Gift Exchange) visible. The error will look something like this, depending on the type of challenge you’re testing: 

{quote}There were some problems with this submission. Please correct the mistakes below.

Sorry! We couldn't save this challenge signup because:

You must submit between 1 and 5 requests to sign up for this challenge. You currently have 0.{quote}

In order for the sign-up to save, you have to edit the challenge settings to _allow_ at least one type of tag in addition to the text (i.e., Details/Description, Title, or URL) field. Allowing another type of text field won't cut it – it _has_ to be a tag. You do not actually have to fill in the tag field when you submit.

This error also happens for both types of challenges if you allow but do not require the text field in question. 

For a Gift Exchange,  you can also reproduce it by 

* setting up both requests and offers using the offer settings described above
* setting up just the requests using the offer settings above (and keeping the default offer settings)

h1. What should happen

The sign-up should be successfully submitted.

column1: Rerunning failed Resque tasks breaks assignments for gift exchanges hit by the stuck-in-a-matching-loop bug
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. The problem

Occasionally, a gift exchange's matching will get stuck in a loop and a database admin will have to ensure that it completes. All the failed runs for this exchange end up in the Resque failures list.

When someone goes to the Failed page on Resque and presses the Retry Failed Jobs button (e.g. because they want to send out failed subscription emails), it retries the failed matching jobs. *EDIT:* This might only happen when rerunning the tasks using `bundle exec rake resque:run_failures`, not when using the Retry Failed Jobs button.

If the exchange has already set assignments, this effectively unsends them by setting the ChallengeAssignment's sent_at to nil. The assignments remain visible on the challenge's assignments page (https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTION_NAME/assignments), but they disappear from the participants' assignments pages (https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/assignments). 

The means the challenge mods either have to purge assignments and rerun matching and recreate the assignments themselves or ask a database admin to fix things by setting the sent_at date. (For assignments that were _not_ automatically generated, such as pinch-hits or write-in recipients or givers, request_signup_id and offer_signup_id information is actually lost from the ChallengeAssignment objects and can only be restored if the challenge mods have kept a record.)

h1. The solution

Failed matching jobs should not be rerun, especially not if the challenge has successfully generated potential matches and/or sent assignments.

h1. Testing

Unfortunately, we do not currently know how to reproduce the failed matching loops that cause this issue.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Edit the work to add a new canonical tag

The series blurb is updated to include (or no longer include) the new tag. However, the bookmark of the series never appears on (or is never removed from) the bookmark listings for that tag, likely because the series is not reindexed. (See also AO3-3726, AO3-4540, AO3-5353.)

Bookmarks of the series should appear on the bookmark listings for the newly-added tag. (If you're removing a tag, the bookmark should disappear from the listings for the removed tag.)

column1: Backdated work's published_at date does not always override revised_at date, resulting in blurb and meta showing different dates
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Example URL:* [https://archiveofourown.org/works/14406267|https://archiveofourown.org/works/14406267] & [https://archiveofourown.org/users/testy/works|https://archiveofourown.org/users/testy/works]

h1. Steps to reproduce

Note: This can _only_ be reproduced if the time is after 00:00 UTC, but before 00:00 US Eastern. Thanks to daylight saving, this can be between 00:00-04:00 or 00:00-05:00 UTC depending on the time of year.

# Login
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required fields
# Check "Set a different publication date" but *do not change the pre-selected date*
# Post Without Preview
# Edit work
# Change publication date to e.g. 23 July 2015
# Post Without Preview

h1. What happens

The work meta on the top of the work uses the backdated date and says "Published: 2015-07-23." 

The date in the upper right of the blurb (located on the creator's works pages, tag listings, etc) says the day the work was posted, e.g. 23 Apr 2018. 

In work listings sorted by Date Updated, the work is sorted by 23 Apr 2018.

h1. What should happen

The work meta behavior is correct. 

The blurb, however, should use the backdated date. 

The work should be sorted in listings according to the backdated date.

h1. Notes 

This is *not* a caching or indexing issue. A look at a buggy work as it exists in MySQL shows:

{code:ruby}2.3.0 :014 > work_edited.revised_at
 => Sun, 22 Apr 2018 23:51:42 EDT -04:00 
2.3.0 :015 > work_edited.published_at
 => Thu, 23 Jul 2015{code}

For comparison, a backdated work that is *not* buggy looks like:

{code:ruby}2.3.0 :002 > w.revised_at
 => Mon, 22 Sep 2014 08:00:00 EDT -04:00 
2.3.0 :003 > w.published_at
 => Mon, 22 Sep 2014{code}

Note: revised_at is the date shown on work blurbs; published_at is the date shown in the meta. 

The work creator *cannot* correct this by editing the work to change the backdated date, or by turning backdating off and back on.

The issue arises from a {{revised_at}}/{{published_at}} mismatch, so I think it might also affect works that don't have {{backdate}} set yet. And I don’t think the {{revised_at < created_at}} check will catch the unbackdated works with broken dates.

If it weren’t for [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6189|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6189|smart-link] , it might work to have a SQL query checking {{HOUR(revised_at)}}, since the issue is basically “any work created while the server date and the Rails date didn’t match.” But we have no guarantees about what Rails time zone any given work may have been created in.

IDK, maybe the query needs a join on the chapters table, so that both {{revised_at}} and {{published_at}} can be used in the calculations? Or maybe it'd be simpler to rewrite the date code to be less brittle.

Once we have chapter IDs and the first {{published_at}}, joining the works table to get {{revised_at}} is simple.

If having a nice query is not possible, we can always use {{Work.find_each}} and just run through everything, check if there are date inconsistencies, and if so reset {{revised_at}}.

In either case, we should:

* get rid of the array tracking invalid chapter IDs - there might be too many which causes the task to crash, the most we should keep is a count;
* maybe(?) order the query results, like by work/chapter ID, and print the first one for each batch in the progress message, so we get a sense of where we’re at and if we need to go back, update the task, and restart.

column1: Make IndexSweeper send fewer commands to REDIS
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
IndexSweeper is currently rather inefficient: even if a batch of 1000 has no errors, it reads and writes all three failure stores once for each item in the batch, resulting in a total of 6000 REDIS commands per batch.

On top of that, each failure store is an array of all previous errors encoded as a JSON string. If each error takes 200 characters to encode in JSON, and each of the three failure stores has 1000 errors, then each error store is 200KB, and a single successful batch receives over 600MB of data and sends over 600MB of data, for a total of over 1.2GB. This only gets worse as the number of previous errors increases.

When a lot of Elasticsearch errors occur, this causes the REDIS server to be swamped with requests.

Ideally, the number of requests should be independent of the size of the batch. In addition, it would be nice if the amount of data transmitted/received was independent of the number of errors that have previously occurred (so that if the number of errors ever reaches millions, it won't require reading and writing a 200MB string).

*Testing:* Like all modifications to IndexSweeper, this change is not particularly feasible to test manually. (You'd need a consistent way to produce indexing errors, which either means finding a way to consistently produce errors on staging, or deliberately modifying the code to produce Elasticsearch errors.)

New Relic says the slowest SQL query within the last 7 days is the kudo find:

{code:sql}
SELECT `kudos`.* FROM `kudos` WHERE `kudos`.`commentable_id` = ? AND `kudos`.`commentable_type` = ? AND (pseud_id IS NOT ?) ORDER BY created_at DESC
{code}


We index the 3 columns in the WHERE, but not created_at. We should index that.

*Update*

From redsummernight in Slack: 
{quote}adding an index on the column created_at doesn't help
because the where clause on the other 3 columns requires using the other index 
so by the time we get to "order by" mysql decided that, hmm, let's just sort it now, index won't help{quote}

*Update 2*

We're going to try [the .any? alternative suggested below by ticking instant|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5415?focusedCommentId=353861&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels:comment-tabpanel#comment-353861] to see if that provides us some degree of relief while we explore the best way to remove the order clause altogether.

*Testing*

QA should make sure kudos work, e.g. the kudos-giver gets added to the list or the guest count goes up.

We'll want to keep an eye on New Relic once this is deployed to see if it helped.

02/Jun/18 6:36 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;(a) I don't think that benchmark does what it's supposed to -- calling .all doesn't seem to force the records to be retrieved, so it's just measuring the cost of building the query, not executing it. You might want to try it with .length instead, since that's the first method called in the kudos/kudos view.

(b) If the Ruby sorting is still too slow, there's a chance you might be able to speed this up with an index on (`commentable_id`,`commentable_type`,`created_at`). It's not a perfect solution, because you'd be losing the speed of filtering out the pseud_ids you don't want, but in most cases I think that would be about a x2 speed penalty, whereas the extra cost of sorting is xlg(number of kudos). (I'm also not completely certain that MySQL would choose the right index in these cases -- would require testing.)

(c) It might also help out to modify the cache block in the kudos/kudos view. Currently, even if there exists a cached fragment for the kudos list, it will still load all kudos from the database before displaying the cached HTML (without ever examining the kudos that it loaded). But if you swap the start of the cache block with the if statement that comes right before it, it will no longer do that. Alternatively, you could modify the if statement to use .any? instead of .length > 0. (That would add an extra SQL query when there's a cache miss, but it's a query that should be pretty snappy.)

(d) If all else fails, maybe it'd be faster to paginate the kudos instead of loading all of them at once.

column27:
We need some sort of popup that will appear every time we update the TOS and that will require users to agree to the new TOS before they can continue using the site. 

- It should contain the text in the "UPDATED SITEWIDE BANNER LANGUAGE" section of the OTW Language Additions document

- It should cover enough of the screen in order to prevent anyone from using the site without accepting the new TOS 

- It should not appear on the TOS page, the Report Abuse page, the DMCA page, or the Support page

- To accept the new TOS, a person needs to both a) check a checkbox and b) press a button to close the banner/popup. The checkbox should be labeled "I have read & understood the new Terms of Service and Privacy Policy" and the button should say "I agree/consent to its terms"
 
- The button should be disabled until the checkbox is checked
 
- When a logged out user accepts the new TOS, we should give them a cookie that prevents them from seeing the popup again in that browser unless they clear their cookies

- When a logged in user accepts the new TOS, we should record it in the database so that, as long as they are logged in, they never see the banner again for this version of the TOS

- If you have just created your account and have just logged in, you should not see the popup until the next version of the TOS

- If JavaScript is disabled, you should not see the popup and you should be able to navigate the site as usual

You'll need to use your browser's developer tools to confirm that the accepted_tos cookie is set to expire in 20 years. (In Safari, you can find this information in the Storage tab under Cookies.)

column27:
# Log in as a wrangler
# On the New Tag page, create a canonical tag and remember its type, e.g. Meta Character Tag 1. This will be your meta tag.
# Post a work with another tag of the same type, e.g. Sub Character Tag 1. This will be your sub tag.
# From the edit page for Sub Character Tag 1, canonize the tag
# Again from the edit page for Sub Character Tag 1, add Meta Character Tag 1 as a meta tag
# Bookmark the work you posted earlier
# Wait a few minutes
# Yay, both the work and the bookmark appear on Meta Character Tag 1's work and bookmark listings
# From the edit page for Sub Character Tag 1, decanonize the tag
# Wait a while

*What happens:*
Uh oh, the work and bookmark still appear on Meta Character Tag 1's work and bookmark listings

*What should happen instead:*
The work and bookmark should be removed from those listings.

*Testing notes:*

It wouldn't hurt to test bookmarks of works, series, and external works. Definitely check that a work/bookmark does _not_ get removed from the tag listing if it is also tagged with Meta Character Tag 1 or another tag that is subbed to Meta Character Tag 1.

Also, make sure to test this with the “Make tag non-canonical and unhook all associations” option as well. You’ll have to be logged in as an admin to use that.

*Coding notes:*
This happens because decanonizing a tag does not remove any filter taggings it inherited from meta tags.

This is the work when both Sub Character Tag 1 and Meta Character Tag 1 are canonical:

{code}2.3.0 :002 > taggings_before = FilterTagging.where(filterable_id: 1067612, filterable_type: "Work")

{code}
The filter tagging with filter_id 1218470 is Sub Character Tag 1. The inherited filter tagging with filter_id 1218467 is Meta Character Tag 1.

This is the work when Sub Character Tag 1 has been decanonized:

{code}2.3.0 :003 > taggings_after = FilterTagging.where(filterable_id: 1067612, filterable_type: "Work")
 => #<ActiveRecord::Relation [#<FilterTagging id: 19891958, filter_id: 9, filterable_id: 1067612, filterable_type: "Work", created_at: "2018-06-01 07:42:58", updated_at: "2018-06-01 07:42:58", inherited: false>, #<FilterTagging id: 19891961, filter_id: 6670, filterable_id: 1067612, filterable_type: "Work", created_at: "2018-06-01 07:42:58", updated_at: "2018-06-01 07:42:58", inherited: false>, #<FilterTagging id: 19891964, filter_id: 14, filterable_id: 1067612, filterable_type: "Work", created_at: "2018-06-01 07:42:58", updated_at: "2018-06-01 07:42:58", inherited: false>, #<FilterTagging id: 19891970, filter_id: 1218467, filterable_id: 1067612, filterable_type: "Work", created_at: "2018-06-01 07:46:35", updated_at: "2018-06-01 07:46:35", inherited: true>]>

28/Apr/20 11:20 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;I’m not 100% sure why it would take 3 hours for it to fix itself, but I do have a theory.

Judging by the timestamps on the comments, the delay occurred less than 8 hours after red started the {{Tag:reset_filters}} task from [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5667|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5667|smart-link]. The part of that task that fixes {{FilterTaggings}} was done in ~20 minutes, but the {{FilterUpdater}} also adds all works to the background reindexing queue (to catch any changes).

Reindexing takes longer than fixing filters, I’m pretty sure. (The code isn’t very optimized at all.) If the reindexing queue was still full when the sub tag was de-canonized, the {{FilterTaggings}} would have been removed almost immediately (because the {{utilities}} queue was empty), but the search results wouldn’t have been updated until the whole reindexing task finished.

I don’t know how long the full reindex would have taken, but if it was long enough, it could have caused the delay in this issue.

If further testing results in other cases where it takes 3 hours to resolve itself, I’ll definitely try to see if there’s a bug in queuing or caching that could have caused it. But in the meantime I’ll focus on the {{Tag:reset_filters}} task to see if there’s a better way to handle the reindexing.

column1: Users can get a cached version of the wrong type of search, resulting in 500 error
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
On production, we currently have some users on Elasticsearch 0.90.7 and others on 6.2. Users on 6.2 somewhat frequently encounter [a 500 error|https://rpm.newrelic.com/accounts/115892/applications/190034/traced_errors/2f519296-6ff5-11e8-a5fd-0242ac110009_0_14317?original_error_id=2f519296-6ff5-11e8-a5fd-0242ac110009_0_14317] resulting from the following when attempting to access a tag's works page, e.g. https://archiveofourown.org/tags/Derek%20Hale*s*Stiles%20Stilinski/works:

{code}
Error message
NoMethodError: undefined method `max_search_results_notice' for #<SearchResult:0x0055b2dcb2ce80>
{code}

SearchResult is the old Elasticsearch, while max_search_results_notice is the new, which tells us the user is getting cached results for the wrong version of Elasticsearch. Therefore, we need to use different cache keys for the different Elasticsearch versions.

This may also happen on bookmarks, but so far all reports we've received have been for works pages. Still, the code should be updated to be sure it doesn't start happening.

*Testing*
Unfortunately, this is not reproducible at will and does not appear to have happened on staging. To test, we'll have to deploy to production and keep an eye on New Relic to see if these errors stop, and we'll have to ask our production testers to make sure to let us know if they encounter 500 errors.

column1: Occasional 500 error when deleting works due to Net::SMTPFatalError: 550
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Support and Policy & Abuse have encountered several works that give 500 errors during the deletion process, regardless of whether the person deleting the work is an admin or a work creator. Database admins are similarly unable to delete the affected works using the destroy method on the command line -- they receive errors such as

{code}
Net::SMTPFatalError: 550 maximum allowed line length is 998 octets, got 1002

	from app/models/work.rb:211:in `block in before_destroy'
	from app/models/work.rb:203:in `each'
	from app/models/work.rb:203:in `before_destroy'
{code}

Replacing the content of the work or the beginning or end notes (it depends on the work) with new text enables deletion, but means the user does not receive a full copy of their work.

The error does not appear to be related to the length of the content or notes -- this error has even happened when attempting to delete a work that consisted solely of an image. It also does not appear to be related to the _specific_ content; that is, if you recreate a problematic work on staging, it will still delete.

Since this error is not reproducible on demand, any fix for this can't be tested beyond making sure it is possible to delete a work. We will have to deploy the fix and see if we stumble upon the error again. 

*Notes*

james_ discovered that this is due to the plain text part of the email having 7bit encoding. red found that [Mail's documentation on multipart emails|https://github.com/mikel/mail#writing-and-sending-a-multipartalternative-html-and-text-email] says:

bq. Mail assumes that if your text in the body is only us-ascii, that your transfer encoding is 7bit and it is text/plain. You can override this by explicitly declaring it.

*How to test*

- Post a work and delete it
- Post a work and have an admin delete it

In both cases, as the work's author, you should receive emails, with the HTML and plain text versions of the work attached. If you look at the raw email, you should see that the plain text attachment has base64 encoding, like this:

{code}
----==_mimepart_5b2b25fe3d906_773ffab1942599d
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8; filename="2k line.txt"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="2k line.txt"
{code}

*More notes*
Sarken has the URL of a work affected by this bug on production. Once this is deployed, we can delete that work to confirm the issue is fixed.

column1: Replace static text in meta tags with page-specific content
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We have fixed content in our meta description tag, which is about the AO3. It would be more useful for Work pages if this was replaced with content specific to the work’s content.

A side effect of having static content in meta tags is that Google ignores it for their search results and displays the first text on the actual page instead. But the first text on every AO3 page is actually the ToS popup text, and so that is what shows up for every single AO3 search result on Google right now. [Here is an example search|https://www.google.de/search?ei=9zA5W9jxI4K26AT817uYBQ&q=Berty+finding+the+words+site%3Aao3.org&oq=Berty+finding+the+words+site%3Aao3.org&gs_l=psy-ab.3...135711.138109.0.138341.18.10.0.0.0.0.337.860.2j1j1j1.5.0], where as of the creation of this issue, this is the case. Attached you’ll also find a screenshot.

If we have page-specific content in our meta tags, Google will hopefully use that to display in their search results. Therefore, this issue is to change the meta tags to the following:

{code:html}<meta name="title" content="[1]">
<meta name="description" content="[2]">{code}

\[1] We’re currently not using this tag. But it should be added and should contain the title of the work. Alternatively we could use the content from the title tag, which is already page specific.
\[2] The work’s summary.

We want to additionally use the twitter and og-specific meta tags (used by facebook and others), to enable link previews on these sites. 

The tags that need to be added are roughly:

{code:html}<!-- Open Graph / Facebook -->
<meta property="og:type" content="website">
<meta property="og:url" content="[url of this page]">
<meta property="og:title" content="">
<meta property="og:description" content="">
<meta property="og:image" content="">

<!-- Twitter -->
<meta property="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">
<meta property="twitter:url" content="[url of this page]">
<meta property="twitter:title" content="[1]">
<meta property="twitter:description" content="[2]">
<meta property="twitter:image" content="[3]">{code}

\[1] For the title, something like {{author: work title}}, would be the easy solution. {{work title by author}} would read nicer, but you’d have to do some Maths to not go over the max character length, which would cause the author name to be cut off.

\[2] For the description, tags in the order of {{fandoms, relationships, characters}} could work, or {{fandoms. summary}}. Again, some experiments with some example works versus the max length would probably help figure this out.

The pre-generated tweet text for the twitter share button on works pages displays {{title by author - fandoms}}, as further orientation.

\[3] For the preview image, our idea is to generate one image for each possible permutation of blurb icons upfront and then link to the static image matching the work’s blurb. Since our icon blocks are in a 1:1 format and these preview images are cropped/fitted to 16:9, we had the idea of generating these images in 16:9 and do something like \[ logo | icon block ], excuse the ascii design.

Official documentation: 

* [twitter cards docs|https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/twitter-for-websites/cards/overview/markup]
* [Open Graph Meta Tag Docs|https://developers.facebook.com/docs/sharing/webmasters/]

column1: Works incorrectly considered crossovers when Fandom A has two top-level metatags and the work uses Fandom A and one of those metatags (or one of Fandom A's syns)
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Fandoms with two top-level metatags count as being unrelated to all other fandoms, including their direct metatags.

This means if you have a work tagged with both "The Avengers (Marvel Movies)" and one of its metatags, e.g. "The Avengers (Marvel) - All Media Types", or one of its syns, e.g. "Avengers (Movieverse) - Fandom", it's considered a crossover, when it should not be.

*Testing*
# Log in as a wrangler
# Search > Tags > New Tag
# Create the following fandom tags:
#* Top Level Metatag 1, canonical
#* Top Level Metatag 2, canonical
#* Tag With Two Top-Level Metatags, canonical
#* Syn of Tag With Two Top-Level Metatags, not canonical
# Edit the tag "Tag With Two Top-Level Metatags" and:
#* Enter both "Top Level Metatag 1" and "Top Level Metatag 2" in its metatag field
#* Enter "Syn of Tag With Two Top Level Metatags" in its Subtags field
# Post a work with the fandoms "Tag With Two Top-Level Metatags" and "Top Level Metatag 1" (or "Top Level Metatag 2" -- doesn't matter)
# Post another work with the fandoms "Tag With Two Top-Level Metatags" and "Syn of Tag With Two Top Level Metatags"
# Go to the works listing for "Tag With Two Top-Level Metatags" and filter the list to "Show only crossovers"

You should not see the works in the results.

27/Jul/18 8:49 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;On the test servers, Captain America (Movies) has two first-class meta tags: Marvel, and Captain America - All Media Types. This means that Captain America's first-class meta tags aren't a subset of The Avengers's first-class meta tags, and vice versa. So according to the current definition of the crossover check, the fandoms count as "unrelated" (because each one has a meta tag that the other doesn't share) and so any work tagged with both is a crossover.

(For the record, Captain America - All Media Types is a subtag of Marvel in production, so I'm pretty sure those works only count as crossovers on staging.)

If you'd prefer, it's pretty straightforward to modify the crossover check so that two fandoms count as "related" as long as they share at least one meta tag, which seems like a fairly reasonable definition to me. column27:
If you are on a device that does not have the fonts Lucida Grande and Lucida Sans Unicode, but does have the font Arial Unicode MS, you will see certain things displayed in that font:
* Button elements, e.g. the words Ratings, Warnings, Fandoms in the filters on [works pages|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/1-800-WHERE-R-U%20Series%20-%20Meg%20Cabot/works]

* Button-style status indications, e.g. the word Unread on unread items in your inbox

With most other things on the site, if you don't have Lucida Grande and Lucida Sans Unicode, you see things in GNU Unifont, Verdana, Helvetica, or the sans-serif of your device's choosing. Therefore, the elements mentioned above look different, and that's weird. They should have the same font stack as the rest of the site.

*Testing*
Since we can't guarantee that you don't have certain fonts installed, the best way to test this is to use your browser's developer tools to look at the computed styles for the elements described above. In Safari 11.1.1, for example:

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce

I'm going to assume you're using iOS 11.4 and are unfamiliar with VoiceOver. If you're using a different version, you may need to Google for directions.

# In Safari, open a page with filters
# In iOS's Settings, tap General
# Tap Accessibility
# Tap VoiceOver
# Toggle VoiceOver on
#* *Note the instructions* about tapping once to select an item, twice to activate the selected item, and swiping with three fingers to scroll!
# Return to Safari
#* The easiest way to do this, rather than switching between apps, is probably to press the home button, tap Safari once to select it, and then tap it *very quickly* twice to open it. No, do it quicker -- by default, you have about 0.25s between tap 1 and tap 2, or else it will just act as selecting twice.
# Tap Filters once to select, then double tap very quickly to open
# Tap Fandoms (or another option) in the filters to select, then double tap quickly to expand the section
# Tap the *checkbox or radio button* (_not_ the text) to select it

h1. What happens
You'll notice the black outline extends beyond the grey of the filters, as in the screenshot below. Well, if you *double tap* the checkbox with the intention of checking it, sometimes it'll work, but other times it might close the filters or do something else unpleasant.

 !IMG_6812.PNG|thumbnail! 

h1. What should happen
The black outline should not extend beyond the grey of the filters, as in the screenshot below. The checkbox should be checked when you do the double tap.

 !IMG_6814.PNG|thumbnail! 

h1. Testing notes
This issue was caused by the fix for AO3-5370, so I'm going to try a CSS hack that will let us keep the fix in Safari 9. That means that in addition to testing the behavior in iOS with VoiceOver, you'll need to re-test AO3-5370 to make sure it remains fixed.

It wouldn't hurt to check that the filter behavior is unchanged in other browsers as well.

h1. Workaround
If you tap the text instead of the checkbox, everything works fine.

column147:
01/Dec/19 9:00 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;[https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.8/search-request-search-after.html|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.8/search-request-search-after.html]

{quote}Pagination of results can be done by using the {{from}} and {{size}} but the cost becomes prohibitive when the deep pagination is reached. The {{index.max_result_window}} which defaults to 10,000 is a safeguard, search requests take heap memory and time proportional to {{from + size}}. The Scroll api is recommended for efficient deep scrolling but scroll contexts are costly and it is not recommended to use it for real time user requests. The {{search_after}} parameter circumvents this problem by providing a live cursor. The idea is to use the results from the previous page to help the retrieval of the next page.{quote}

We use from + size with {{index.max_result_window}} set to 100k. Switching to cursor pagination would remove the limit and also improve ES performance as well.

The downside of {{search_after}} is that you cannot jump to a random page (e.g. you can't just request page 754). A few ways we can deal with random page jumping:

* Just don't allow random page jumping. Any listings will have "Previous" and "Next" buttons only, no more 1, 2, 3, etc. URL parameters like {{page=12}} will cease to have meanings. This is what the Tumblr dashboard does.
** [~accountid:557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0] noted we don't want this approach as it places even more emphasis on page 1 works (with the most kudos/comments/bookmarks, or most frequently updated).
* Allow random page jumping by chaining {{search_after}} queries. So if users ask for page 10, we have to get all of the first 10 pages. This approach would use less memory than from + size but will generate a crap ton of queries we ultimately discard. Not very viable.
* Maybe a mix? For the first 10k results (default {{index.max_result_window}}) just use from + size as usual. Then if users want to go beyond, switch to {{search_after}}. Example: [https://medium.com/@Benoit_Travers/elasticsearch-how-we-paginated-over-10-000-items-11198af5018c|https://medium.com/@Benoit_Travers/elasticsearch-how-we-paginated-over-10-000-items-11198af5018c]. Downside: complicated to implement.
* Why doesn't {{search_after}} let us specify a starting offset? The answer is unfortunately no: [https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/28068|https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/28068].

20/Apr/19 2:05 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;Notes from [~accountid:5caa93d79c21b237caab3305] (thank you!):
{quote}
I've looked through documentation for the new Zoho Desk API and while I do not have a PR, I have mapped out (almost) all the steps which would be required.

The only API call which is used in the Archive Of Our Own server is creating a Ticket, which is documented here: https://desk.zoho.com/DeskAPIDocument#Tickets#Tickets_Createaticket
The main changes -- besides the data being JSON, not XML -- is that the authentication token and the orgId (the equivalent to the "portal name" -- see "THE SLIGHTLY-MORE-COMPLEX PART" below) are passed as HEADERS, not in the URL path as it currently is.

*THE SIMPLE PARTS:*
First of all, many of the fields simply have the same, or just slightly different names:
The current "title" attribute should now be put as "Subject",
"email" stays as "email" (I'm pretty sure -- you may want to double-check this. Also see the stuff about "Contact"s below.)
and "description" as "description"
other things can be placed as "customFields":
"language",
"ip_address" and "url" for abuse reports,
"site_revision", "user_agent", "rollout" for support requests.

*THE SLIGHTLY-MORE-COMPLEX PART:*
What had previously been the "portal name" and the "department name" is now required to be the numerical identifiers representing those.
These can (probably?) just be added safely to the config.yml file and referred to from there.
These numerical identifiers can be gotten from the API:
the orgId (from the portal name) from https://desk.zoho.com/DeskAPIDocument#Organizations#Organizations_Getorganization
the departmentId (from the department name) from https://desk.zoho.com/DeskAPIDocument#Departments#Departments_Listdepartments


*THE COMPLICATED/PROBABLE DATABASE-CHANGES PART:*
Creating a ticket now requires that there is some Zoho-Desk-internal Contact object -- created separately -- that the ticket creator.
Managing these Contacts will require non-zero complexity.
Documentation: https://desk.zoho.com/DeskAPIDocument#Contacts

Creating a Contact is a separate API call, which requires a "lastName" set -- I think this could just be the username? (Although if I'm reading the code correctly, if an admin files an abuse report, no username is stored, I think?)

There doesn't seem to be a way to search Contacts, by, e.g., "lastName" or "email" or something, so if we wanted to not create a new Contact every single ticket, even for the same person, I think we'd have to store their contactId.

There may be other issues which come up when implementing this, as well.

Also, looking at the time, it seems like there's only four months left -- until early August -- before the old API shuts down entirely, so this seems relatively time-sensitive.

(I have a small few other notes as well, if someone takes this issue on and wants to contact me, but this is most of it and all I think I can summarize well.)
{quote}

We freaked out a little at the thought of maintaining the list of contacts ourselves, but luckily it turns out it was hiding in the Search section rather than Contacts: https://desk.zoho.com/DeskAPIDocument#Search

column1: Work search for words in different fields doesn't work
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
1. In the main search field or the top of the work search form, enter 'sarken closer', hoping to find sarken's works in The Closer fandom.
2. See none of those works in the search results despite the fact that they exist and are properly indexed.

What's happening is that the behavior of Elasticsearch queries [has changed from the old version|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.0/breaking_60_search_changes.html]: it used to split up words separated by spaces and look for them in any field. Now, it only returns records that have all of the words in the same field, which means it doesn't work if you're simultaneously looking for creator + tag, or tag + summary.

{quote}
The split_on_whitespace parameter for the query_string query has been removed. If provided, it will be ignored and issue a deprecation warning. The query_string query now splits on operator only.
{quote}

The workaround is to type "sarken AND closer" whenever you want to search multiple fields, but that leaves the default behavior of the search system fairly unintuitive and confusing to casual users.

Solution TBD.

28/Oct/25 2:02 PM;712020:1bcdb886-fc02-4abf-9f5e-df4ba8bb1ccd;I'm really getting into the weeds of this one, if anyone knows Elasticsearch better than I do, then I am all for feedback/discussion! Apologies for being terrible at explaining things but hope this makes some kind of sense.

I think the crux of the issue here is whatever solution fixes the stated problem will break the "field: value" style syntax for advanced searching. This may or may not be an acceptable tradeoff.

As far as I can tell, there are 2 ways of fixing this that give you more of a clean "word only" search style that searches across fields:

# The simple_query_string is what I started out with, works pretty well imo and is probably the easiest for now. "field: value"/"field:value" just get treated as invalid and therefore discarded, so you get nothing if using those as search terms.
# The multi_match cross_fields query might be the best way to go after a bit of tuning (harder, but the relevance payoff while searching might be worth it), but again, the "field: value" syntax is lost.

Now hypothetically speaking you could probably write some kind of parser before sending it to the query (for simple_query_string) to do some bool matching to try and match the parsing for the query_string ("field: value" syntax) but that seems like a lot of effort to potentially get it wrong.

Ultimately, if the "field: value" syntax would like to be maintained, I don't see a good way to fix this issue unless someone has an idea that I haven't considered yet, so open to ideas!

# Elasticsearch documentation is so, so horrible. Need to get that thought out of the way 😭 
# The {{split_queries_on_whitespace}} ONLY works on {{keyword}} types, not {{text}} types. Tried to do it out of curiosity and was hit with 
{noformat}Elastic::Transport::Transport::Errors::BadRequest: [400] {"error":{"root_cause":[{"type":"mapper_parsing_exception","reason":"unknown parameter [split_queries_on_whitespace] on mapper [title] of type [text]"}],"type":"mapper_parsing_exception","reason":"Failed to parse mapping: unknown parameter [split_queries_on_whitespace] on mapper [title] of type [text]","caused_by":{"type":"mapper_parsing_exception","reason":"unknown parameter [split_queries_on_whitespace] on mapper [title] of type [text]"}},"status":400} (Elastic::Transport::Transport::Errors::BadRequest){noformat}
# Just for fun, I changed title into keyword, as this seems like the only field this actually works with?:

{noformat}title: {
  type: "keyword",
  split_queries_on_whitespace: true
},{noformat}

# Gives me 0 results when searching for an exact match on title (using the “angst bunny” work)

!image-20251120-062903.png|width=575,alt="image-20251120-062903.png"!

It WILL work with quotes though:

!image-20251120-062944.png|width=508,alt="image-20251120-062944.png"!

So changing to keyword breaks more than it fixes, since title just becomes one giant token “angst bunny” and appears that {{split_queries_on_whitespace}} doesn’t really work with {{query_string}}. 


With the angst bunny example → parser turns this into: angst AND bunny → (title:angst OR creator:angst…) AND (title:bunny OR creator:bunny…)

So there’s only ever 1 word that gets matched with any given field, so split_queries_on_whitespace doesn’t really then do anything anyway (I think???)

It’s not very obvious this wouldn’t work just based off the docs, since this [https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/mapping-reference/keyword|https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/mapping-reference/keyword|smart-link] links [https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/query-dsl/full-text-queries|https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/query-dsl/full-text-queries|smart-link]  which literally include {{query_string query}}…. but see point 1 about that, lol. 


I think my conclusion has to be either say a) this is impossible in the current state to search across fields, or b) overhaul the general search system entirely.

This is just my 2 cents, but it might be worth looking into how many people really use {{field: value}} or other operators in the general search box. It might be more meaningful for the majority of users to have this cross-query syntax return results for what you would expect to come back with hits (the “sarken closer”/“title author” syntax), even if that necessarily returns a bit too many results than expected or means users who are used to the old system would have to switch. (Hopefully though, this would be a lot easier for everyone). Perhaps the query_string syntax can be maintained still in some form and available to users, if they so wish to use it.

Understandable if this isn’t a priority, but thought I’d throw that out there.

column1: Missing inherited MetaTaggings break crossover check
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
In production, some tags, such as [Guardians of the Galaxy (Movies)|https://archiveofourown.org/tags/Guardians%20of%20the%20Galaxy%20(Movies)/works] are missing their inherited meta tags. Until these meta tags are fixed, tags like Guardians of the Galaxy will be treated as having 0 first-class meta tags, resulting in a lot of false negatives for the crossover check. (Because currently, we check whether one fandom's first-class meta tags are a subset of the other's.)

The crossover check should iteratively and/or recursively compute the missing inherited meta-tags to fix the check (at least until the meta-taggings table is fixed).

*Testing Notes:*

1. To create a fandom with a missing inherited meta tag, create four canonical fandom tags. I'll call them Fandom A, Fandom B, Fandom C, and Fandom D.
2. Edit Fandom A and add *sub* tags Fandom B and Fandom C.
3. Edit Fandom D and add *meta* tags Fandom B and Fandom C.
4. Edit Fandom C and remove Fandom A from its meta tags.
5. Keep refreshing the edit page until Fandom A disappears, then remove Fandom D from its sub-tags.
5. At this point, Fandom D should have Fandom B as a direct meta-tag. Because of the meta-tag issue, however, it should be missing the inherited meta tag Fandom A. You can check this by creating a work with Fandom D, and checking whether it shows up when you add Fandom A to "Other tags to include."
6. Try tagging a work with Fandom D and another unrelated fandom. The work should be marked as a crossover, but as a result of this bug it won't be.

column1: Run unwrangled bins through elasticsearch
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
There's currently not a good direct way to query which tags are unwrangled for which fandoms and how many of them there are, and the joins we use now are hard on the database. To make the system more efficient, we want to cache that data in Elasticsearch, making it easier to query.

h2. Testing
*Note: Until this comment is removed, this list should be considered a work in progress.*

*Note: AO3-2270 will also be in this release. Any comments regarding unwrangled tags on works tagged with fandom* _*syns*_ *(as opposed to canonical fandom tags) should go on that issue.*

* On the edit pages for unwrangled tags, the list of Suggested Fandoms should be correct.
** Suggestions will only come from the first 100 uses of the tag. For example, if the unwrangled character tag “Sharon Raydor” is used on 100 works tagged with the fandom “The Closer,” and is then used on 1 work tagged with “Major Crimes (TV),” only “The Closer” will appear in the list of suggested fandoms. Also, “The Closer” should only appear once, not 100 times.
* Creating a new work/draft with (or editing an existing work/draft to include) a new character, relationship, or freeform tag should place that tag in the appropriate unwrangled bin for any canonical fandoms listed on the work. This should happen within a few minutes of the tag being added to the work.
* When a new character, relationship, or freeform tag is added to a work in one of your fandoms, the number of unwrangled tags listed on your wrangling page should increase appropriately within about 4 hours.
* If you wrangle an unwrangled tag, the number of unwrangled tags listed on your wrangling page should decrease appropriately within a few minutes. The tag should also disappear from your fandom’s unwrangled bin within a few minutes.
* Unwrangled tag bins should only include unwrangled tags.
* Sorting unwrangled tag bins by tag name, date created, and number of taggings should work correctly.

column1: Use a GET parameter and localStorage to determine whether a guest should be shown a TOS/GDPR prompt
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We prompt users to agree to the TOS any time they visit a page, unless they have already agreed to it while logged in or with cookies enabled (AO3-5416). There is no way to avoid the TOS popup if accounts are not available (people who browse using incognito/private mode) or cookies don't work.

We would like to use localStorage instead of cookies to determine whether the TOS prompt should be shown to guests.

We will also skip the TOS prompt if the URL has {{?tos=yes}} at the end. (We don't add these parameters to the URL automatically after you press "I agree/consent to its terms" because we don't want people accidentally sharing links with them. We want it to be something a user has to manually add so we can be relatively sure they actually agreed to the TOS and didn't just follow a link that happened to have the {{?tos=yes}} params.)

*Testing instructions*

Part 1:
- Log out.
- Go to https://test.archiveofourown.org and the TOS prompt should appear. Check the box and press the button to accept the TOS. 
- Navigate to another page and make sure it doesn’t reappear.

Part 2:
- Open a private / incognito browser session.
- Go to https://test.archiveofourown.org and the TOS prompt should appear. Don't press the button yet.
- Go to https://test.archiveofourown.org?tos=yes and the TOS prompt should not appear.
- Navigate to another page and make sure it doesn’t reappear.
- Close your private / incognito browser session and open a new one.
- Go to https://test.archiveofourown.org/tos and make sure the TOS prompt does not appear.

Part 3:
- Browse logged out and accept the TOS prompt.
- Have a registered user that has not accepted the TOS (by asking a site admin to reset your account's accepted_tos_version, since accounts have to accept the TOS upon registration).
- Log in as this user. Check that the TOS prompt appears. Don't press the button yet.
- Go to https://test.archiveofourown.org?tos=yes. Check that the TOS prompt still appears.
- Accept the prompt, navigate to another page and make sure it doesn’t reappear.

column1: Marvel Is Broken: The Missing FilterTagging Reason
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a wrangler
# Create a canonical fandom tag "Metatag" (note: it doesn't have to be a fandom, but all tags must be canonical and of the same type)
# Create a canonical fandom tag "Subtag A" and add "Metatag" as its metatag
# Create a canonical fandom tag "Subtag of Subtag A" and add "Subtag A" as its metatag
# Create a canonical fandom tag "Subtag B" and add "Metatag" as its metatag
# Post a work that uses both "Subtag B" and "Subtag of Subtag A"
# Wait for listings to update and confirm the work appears in the listings for "Metatag," "Subtag A," and "Subtag of Subtag A."
# Edit the tag "Subtag of Subtag A" to remove "Subtag A" as a metatag

h1. What happens

The work posted in step 6 should continue to be in the work listings for "Metatag" because it still has "Subtag B."

h1. What happens

It is no longer included in the listings.

h1. Notes

This is affecting a bunch of Marvel Cinematic Universe works. Info from ticking instant:

{quote}ticking instant [17:49]
I was poking around the Avengers tag to try to see how the new crossover code was doing, and I noticed that there's nearly 20,000 works tagged with "The Avengers (Marvel Movies)" that don't seem to have their inherited "Marvel" filter.

This isn't part of the previous bug, since "The Avengers (Marvel Movies)" still seems to have "Marvel" as a meta tag. (I checked a newly-posted work.)

It turns out that there's actually yet another bug related to removing meta tags, this one affecting the FilterTaggings instead of the MetaTaggings.

If you have an overarching meta tag (like "Marvel") with two sub tags (like "Thor - All Media Types" and "The Avengers (Marvel Movies)"), and a subtag of the first sub tag (like "Thor (Movies)"), and you delete the MetaTagging between "Thor - All Media Types" and "Thor (Movies)", then any work tagged with both "Thor (Movies)" and "The Avengers (Marvel Movies)" will have the "Marvel" filter removed.

As far as I can tell, this has happened a bunch of times with Marvel tags, including: "Iron Man (Movies)", "Thor (Movies)", "Guardians of the Galaxy (Movies)", "The Incredible Hulk (2008)", and even a couple of comics tags as well.

Between the two bugs, there are over 40,000 works in the "Marvel Cinematic Universe" tag that are missing the "Marvel" meta tag.{quote}

Note from Tag Wrangling about the structure of the Marvel tags:

{quote}
The tag structure was:

- Marvel
-- Marvel Cinematic Universe
--- Thor (Marvel Movies)
--- The Avengers (Marvel Movies)
-- Thor - All Media Types
--- Thor (Marvel Movies)

and is now:

- Marvel 
-- Marvel Cinematic Universe
--- Thor (Marvel Movies) (with Thor - All Media Types synned to it)
--- The Avengers (Marvel Movies){quote}

This often happens alongside AO3-5508 in production, as seen in Marvel fandoms. The issues can, however, occur separately. (According to ticking, there are over 40,000 works in the "Marvel Cinematic Universe" tag that are missing the "Marvel" metatag, and 5508 accounts for about 13,000 of those.)

This is not super high priority as we are eyeing a rewrite of this code. However, it's good to have these things logged.

column1: Marvel Is Broken 2: The Inherited Metatag Reason
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce
# Create four canonical fandom tags. I'll call them Fandom A, Fandom B, Fandom C, and Fandom D.
# *Edit Fandom A* and add subtags Fandom B and Fandom C.
# *Edit Fandom D* and add metatags Fandom B and Fandom C.
# *Edit Fandom C* and remove Fandom A from its metatags.
# Keep refreshing the edit page until Fandom A disappears, then remove Fandom D from its subtags.
# Post *a work with Fandom D*.
# Go to *the works page for Fandom D* and wait for the work to appear.
# In the "Other tags to include" field of the filters, enter "Fandom A" and press "Sort and Filter."

h1. What happens
The work does not appear.

Note that if you instead entered “Fandom B” in the field, the work would appear. This is because Fandom D has Fandom B as a direct metatag, but it is missing the inherited metatag Fandom A.

You can also test this by checking the work listings for Fandom A and Fandom B. The work with Fandom D will appear on the page for Fandom B, but not on the page for Fandom A.

h1. What should happen
The work should appear. Fandom D should have Fandom A as an inherited metatag.

h1. Notes
This often happens alongside [AO3-5507|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5507] in production, as seen in Marvel fandoms. The issues can, however, occur separately. (According to ticking, there are over 40,000 works in the "Marvel Cinematic Universe" tag that are missing the "Marvel" metatag, and this bug counts for about 13,000 of those.)

This is not super high priority as we are eyeing a rewrite of this code. However, it's good to have these things logged.

This issue was responsible for [AO3-5484|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5484] .

column1: Store the user id of the original creator of a work
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
To help with abuse of the orphaning feature, we'd like to store the user ID of a work’s original poster on the work so that admins can view it and misbehaving users can be dealt with:

* the ID should be visible on work pages only to admins with the superadmin or policy_and_abuse role
* the ID should not be in the search index
* the ID should be scrubbed from orphan works after 72 hours

It can go in the work meta, above the IP Address. Usernames can consist of only numbers, so it’s necessary to emphasize that the ID, _not_ the name, is the main piece of information being presented. It could look like this:

{quote}Original Creator ID: user ID (username){quote}

If the account is deleted and the username is no longer accessible, it should just display the user ID. This would happen if:

* someone posts a work, orphans it, and deletes their account
* someone posts a work, invites a co-creator (who accepts the invitation), and then deletes their account

(Note: This was previously intended to also help with a different sort of abuse of the co-creator feature, but we’ve changed that behavior.)

*Testing*

{color:#bf2600}*Before merging*{color}*, post two works and orphan one of them.*{color:#bf2600} {color}This should be done within the 72-hour window.

Once this is in QA:

# Post a new work, then orphan it.
# View the work as a super- or policy and abuse admin. Make sure there’s a new field in the meta with the original creator’s user ID and username.
# Delete the creator’s account.
# View the work again as one of the correct admins, and make sure the original creator’s user ID is present (without a username this time).
# After 72 hours, view the work as an admin again and make sure the original creator’s information is no longer shown.

*Deploy notes*

column1: Limit the number of password resets
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We want to limit the number of password resets without getting too much in the way. 

We want to implement this in a way similar to [Devise Lockable|https://github.com/heartcombo/devise/blob/5d5636f03ac19e8188d99c044d4b5e90124313af/lib/devise/models/lockable.rb], including making this a concern module. Unlike Lockable, we won’t distinguish between successful and failed attempts.

Add config values for how many resets a user is allowed to request ({{ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_LIMIT}}) before they must wait a given period of time ({{ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_COOLDOWN_HOURS}}), e.g. 12 hours after 4 resets. 

(Note: You’re welcome to come up with better names for these; it was just easier to write the issue if we had names to reference instead of constantly needing to express the concept.)

Add a {{resets_requested}} integer column to the {{users}} table that records how many resets the user has requested. Ensure this field is indexed. 

We’ll use the existing {{reset_password_sent_at}} [column|https://github.com/heartcombo/devise/blob/5d5636f03ac19e8188d99c044d4b5e90124313af/lib/devise/models/recoverable.rb#L28] when we need to reference when a reset was last sent. 

When someone makes a password reset request for an account, increase {{resets_requested}} by one and inform the person how many reset requests remain. The info on remaining resets can be added to the current flash message, so it reads:

{quote}Check your email for instructions on how to reset your password. You may reset your password {{#{ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_LIMIT - user.resets_requested}}} more times. After that, you will need to wait {{#{ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_COOLDOWN_HOURS}}} hours before requesting another reset.{quote}

Even unsuccessful attempts should increase {{resets_requested}}.

If {{user.reset_password_sent_at > ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_COOLDOWN_HOURS.hours.ago}} or {{user.resets_requested <= ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_LIMIT}}, send a password reset.

If the password cannot be reset, an error flash message should be shown.

{quote}You cannot reset your password at this time. More resets will become available at #{(time of last reset + ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_PERIOD) in user's time zone}.{quote}

If a reset is requested and {{user.reset_password_sent_at > ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_COOLDOWN_HOURS.hours.ago}}, the {{user.resets_requested}} should be set back to 1 and a reset should be sent.

*Testing*

{{PASSWORD_RESET_COOLDOWN_HOURS}} is set to 12 hours and {{PASSWORD_RESET_LIMIT}} is set to 3

* Request a password reset and ensure the success message is correct and you receive the email. 
* Repeat X times, until you have no resets left. Ensure the error message is correct and you do not receive an email.
* When X hours pass, request a password reset and ensure the success message is correct and you receive the email.
