column1: Block password resets for certain users
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*History*

In April 2018, we hot fixed the mailer so it would bail and not send password resets to certain users. However, that was right smack dab in the middle of the Elasticsearch upgrade, so it was never permanently committed.

*Desired changes*

Allow Policy & Abuse to prevent password resets from being sent to users who are receiving them erroneously. 

When you try to reset the password for a user whose account is protected in this manner:

* you should get an error message that says, “Password resets are disabled for that user. For more information, please contact Policy & Abuse,” with a link to the abuse form, and
* the user should not receive an email

Policy & Abuse admins should be able to log in, go to the Manage Users > Find Users page, and search for a user. 

In the search results table, there should be a new role: “Protected User.”

Checking this corresponding checkbox for a user and pressing “Update” should lead to the behavior described in the bullet points above. (The change should also be logged – please refer to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6137|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6137|smart-link] for that.)

The box should stay checked on subsequent searches to indicate the user has the “Protected User” role.

Unchecking the box should return the account’s password reset behavior to normal, and subsequent searches should show the box unchecked.

*Testing notes*

Before testing  can begin, a database admin will need to run a rake task to create the role: {{bundle exec rake defaults:create_roles}}. (If you’re setting up your very own instance of the otwarchive code, this rake task will also handle creation of other roles.)

When searching for a user to update their role, please make sure there are no duplicate roles listed in either the search results table or the “Role” search field, i.e. “Tag Wrangler” should only appear once in each location.

It should be possible to search for users who have the “Protected User” role.

It should be possible to add and remove “Protected user” role for a user. This behavior will be available to any admin who can change an account role – this means admins with the role open_doors, policy_and_abuse, tag_wrangling, and superadmins. It shouldn’t be used by anyone other than policy_and_abuse and usage will be logged (again, see AO3-6137).

When a user is protected, make sure to try requesting password resets by both username and email address.

Please also make sure that a protected user can still log in and can still change their password.

Also, please confirm that password resets still work for users who have not been protected.

column1: Possible to reuse an invitation after the account that initially used the invitation is deleted
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce
Note that this also works with an invitation you've received from another user.

# Follow the "Get Invited\!" link from the homepage
# Request an invitation by filling in the "Email" field (with an email address you have access to) and pressing "Add me to the list"
# Wait for your invitation to come
# Follow the signup link in the email
# Fill in all the fields and press "Create Account" to create an account
# Wait for the confirmation email
# Follow the "activate your account" link in the email
# Log in using the account you just created
# Hi, username\! > My Dashboard > Profile > Delete My Account
# Choose "OK" in the popup to confirm account deletion
# Go back to your invitation email
# Follow the signup link in the email
# Fill in all the fields and press "Create Account"

h2. What happens
Your account is successfully created.

h2. What should happen
Following the signup link in the email should result in you being redirected to the homepage with an error saying, "This invitation has already been used to create an account, sorry\!"

This is [the same error message that is supposed to appear when you follow a signup link that has been used by an existing account|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/96f4004dd7d265555f2b7a824201fc0ecae66afe/app/controllers/users_controller.rb#L351-L353], but there seems to be a bug preventing it from actually appearing.

h2. Notes
If an invitation was used for an account that has been purged as 14 days of being unactivated, the invitation *will* be reusable.

If you’re looking at the invitation’s show page:

* when an account gets *purged*, the invitation's "Redeemed at" and "Redeemed by" will be reset to blank, indicating the invitation can be reused
* when an account is *deleted by the user*, the invitation's "Redeemed by" will be reset to blank, but the "Redeemed _at_" will still be present, indicating the invitation cannot be reused

Also, on the admin search results page for invitations, if the "copy and use" link is available, the invitation is definitely usable (the link is only displayed if there's no "Redeemed at" info).

column1: Collections: Occasional 500 error when revealing or de-anoning due to lingering CollectionItem for deleted Work
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Details and steps to reproduce
If you're running an anonymous or unrevealed collection and you reveal or de-anon all the works by unchecking the unrevealed/anonymous option in Collection Settings, it occasionally gives a 500 error. (Some of the works may be revealed or de-anoned upon reloading the collection's works list.)

This happens because someone deleted a work that was in the collection, but for some reason, the {{CollectionItem}} associated with that {{Work}} object still exists. A database admin can delete the {{CollectionItem}} and the challenge owner can then successfully reveal or de-anon the collection.

These steps will not always reproduce the bug, but here is the process:

# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information
# Check either “This collection is unrevealed” or “This collection is anonymous” (or both\!)
# Press “Submit”
# Follow the “Post to Collection” link
# Fill in required information (the collection info will already be filled in because you used the “Post to Collection” link)
# Post Without Preview (or Preview and then Post – it doesn’t actually matter)
# Return to the collection via the link at the top of the work
# Repeat steps 6-8
# Follow the “Edit” link on the top of your work
# Follow the “Delete” link on the top of the work
# Choose “OK” to confirm deletion
# Return to your collection
# Follow the “Collection Settings” link in the dashboard
# Uncheck “This collection is unrevealed” and/or “This collection is anonymous”
# Press “Update”

h1. Fixing
Ideally, we would fix whatever causes the {{CollectionItem}} to linger even after its work is deleted.

However, since the cause of that may be difficult to track down, we can settle for making it so unrevealing or de-anoning a collection doesn't error when it encounters a {{CollectionItem}} without a {{Work}}.

Here, have a convenient link to the methods related to revealing works/creators: [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/d049ce6a46933d56ec9e5fff93c62c437c5493d8/app/models/collection.rb#L447-L472]

h1. Notes
Note that [AO3-5544|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5544] can also lead to some works in a collection remaining unrevealed, but in that case, no error occurs when updating the collection settings.

h1. Testing
Because this is not something we can currently reproduce on demand to test manually, we will likely need to create an automated test for this scenario and trust that if it passes, the issue is fixed.
column147:
15/Nov/18 2:44 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;This bug can manifest even if every collection item is properly cleaned up in the same transaction as its work.

All of the collection items are loaded right at the start of the {{.each}} loop in {{Collection.reveal_collection_items}}, but the item associated with each collection item is only loaded during each individual collection item’s callbacks. So if someone deletes their work while reveals are running in the background, or if the draft purging code purges a draft in the collection while reveals are running in the background, this bug will happen.

If there are unassociated {{CollectionItem}}‌s floating around, it'd be good to prevent that, but handling missing items is necessary regardless. (Luckily, that’s basically the same issue as AO3-5089, which already has a pull request.)

column1: Collections: Works occasionally not marked unrevealed and anonymous upon posting directly to an unrevealed or anonymous collection
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Overview and steps to reproduce
If you have an anonymous, unrevealed collection (or, quite likely, a collection that is only one of those) and someone posts a work to said collection, the work and its creator may still be visible to all who encounter said work.

These steps will not always reproduce the bug, but here is the process:

# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information
# Check both “This collection is unrevealed” and “This collection is anonymous”
# Press “Submit”
# Follow the “Post to Collection” link
# Fill in required information (the collection info will already be filled in because you used the “Post to Collection” link)
# Post Without Preview

h1. Details
This is a fascinating situation where the Work is incorrect ({{in_anon_collection: false, in_unrevealed_collection: false}}), but the CollectionItem is correct ({{anonymous: true, unrevealed: true}}):

{code}2.3.0 :001 > w = Work.find(000)
=> #<Work id: 000, expected_number_of_chapters: 1, created_at: "2017-11-17 20:20:18", updated_at: "2017-11-17 20:40:41", major_version: 1, minor_version: 1, posted: true, language_id: 1, restricted: false, word_count: 7498, hidden_by_admin: false, delta: false, revised_at: "2017-11-17 20:20:58", backdate: false, endnotes: "", imported_from_url: nil, hit_count_old: 0, last_visitor_old: nil, complete: true, summary_sanitizer_version: 1, notes_sanitizer_version: 1, endnotes_sanitizer_version: 1, work_skin_id: nil, in_anon_collection: false, in_unrevealed_collection: false, anon_commenting_disabled: false, spam: false, spam_checked_at: "2017-11-17 20:40:41", moderated_commenting_enabled: false>

2.3.0 :002 > c_i = CollectionItem.where(item_type: "Work", item_id: 000)
=> #<ActiveRecord::Relation [#<CollectionItem id: 000, collection_id: 105699, item_id: 000, item_type: "Work", user_approval_status: 1, collection_approval_status: 0, created_at: "2017-11-17 20:20:28", updated_at: "2017-11-17 20:20:28", anonymous: true, unrevealed: true>]>{code}
Please note that the {{Work}} and {{CollectionItem}} IDs have been changed to {{000}} and some work fields ({{title}}, {{summary}}, {{notes}}, {{authors_to_sort_on}}, {{title_to_sort_on}}, {{ip_address}}) removed for privacy, as they are not relevant.

We confirmed that this work \-\- and at least one other work affected by this issue \-\- belonged only to one anonymous, unrevealed collection.

We note that the {{Work}} and {{CollectionItem}} were created at the exact same time ({{created_at: "2017-11-17 20:20:28"}}), although this is not in itself unusual \-\- it happens on works that are properly marked unrevealed and anonymous as well.

We suspect a race condition. 😭

{{CollectionItem.update_work}} is one of the few {{after_commit}} callbacks we have that tries to read data that was just written in the previous commit. Because it's an {{after_commit}} callback, not an {{after_save}}, the database queries to look up {{user_approved_collection_items}} (in {{update_anon_unrevealed}}, which is called by {{CollectionItem.update_work}}) occur _outside_ of the transaction, which in theory would allow them them be routed to the read-only SQL servers, which have some chance of lagging behind the master SQL server by a transaction or two. (h/t ticking instant for the discovery and explanation.)

h1. Testing
Because this cannot be reproduced at will, it is unlikely the fix can be tested. All we can do is take several shots at posting to an unrevealed, anonymous collection to confirm the correct behavior still happens and watch for any new reports of this bug after the fix is deployed.

h1. Steps to reproduce
Note: We're using a character tag here and simulating the process of performing a suffix swap. However, this problem could occur with any type of tag and when making any sort of edit to the tag name.

# Log in as a wrangler
# Post a work with a new character tag like "Somebody Who Once Told Me \- Character"
# Edit the tag you just made to canonize it and put it in a fandom, e.g. Testing
# Create a tag set that is accepting nominations for character tags
# Nominate the tag you just canonized (do not simply add the tag to the tag set – this bug is with nominations specifically)
# Log out
# Log in as an admin
# Go to the edit page for your tag, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Somebody%20Who%20Once%20Told%20Me%20\-%20Character/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Somebody%20Who%20Once%20Told%20Me%20-%20Character/edit]
# Edit the "Name" field to remove the " \- Character" bit (and press "Save changes")
# Log out of your admin account
# Log back in as the tag wrangler
# Attempt to access your tag nomination, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/496/nominations/6703], or your tag set's page for reviewing nominations, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/496/nominations/]



h1. What should happen
Those pages should load. The nominated tag should still be exactly as the nominator wrote it ("Somebody Who Once Told Me \- Character").



h1. What happens instead
500 error\! For the nominations review page, the error might not happen immediately, depending on the number of nominations (because the broken nomination might not be randomly selected for display).

It is still {{tagname: "Somebody Who Once Told Me \- Character", canonical: true, exists: true, parent: true}} when those last three things should be false, and so we error when looking up the tag object in the {{nomination_tag_information(nominated_tag)}} method of the tag sets helper: [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/9e5741ddcaacc9cc8ca9fe367bf4921fb99c78af/app/helpers/tag_sets_helper.rb#L66]

column1: Draft deletion task sometimes deletes chapters but leaves work itself behind
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Sometimes, if a user has a draft that is more than 30 days old, the draft deletion task will delete the chapter(s) but leave the Work object behind. 

Not only does this leave the draft blurb visible on the user's drafts page, causing confusion (the user gets a 500 error when attempting to open or edit the draft), but if the work was in a collection, it can also cause 500 errors for moderators attempting to reveal or de-anon works (or, I believe, access the Manage Items page).

It's possible this is also related to tags used solely on drafts still showing up in the wrangling bins even when they are more than a month old.

Unfortunately, this is not something we can reproduce on demand, but it appears to be happening with increasing frequency. 

We will add more details when/if we get them.
column147:
24/Nov/18 7:48 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Currently, the draft deletion task deletes all the chapters first, and then deletes the works. This has a couple of effects:

(a) If the task encounters an error partway through deleting the works, this means that all of the works that it failed to delete will have no chapters. If it's an intermittent error, then the issue should be cleaned up the next time the draft deletion task is run. But if it's a persistent error, then every single draft could linger without chapters until someone intervenes.

(b) Even if it runs without a single error, if the draft deletion task takes a long time, then each of the works will spend some amount of time with missing chapters, potentially resulting in temporary issues like the one described in the bug report.

The solution is to stop deleting the chapters first, and instead allow the work's callbacks to handle chapter deletion. Using callbacks ensures that the chapter deletion and the work deletion occur in the same transaction, so that there's much less danger of running into works without chapters.

It's hard to test for this issue specifically, but the PR that I wrote rewrites the draft deletion task. So for manual testing, it'd be good to do the following:
# Make a draft (preferably with a bunch of interesting associations, like series and collections).
# Use the rails console to update the draft's {{created_at}} date to over a month ago.
# Run the draft deletion task.

If that results in the draft being deleted, the code should be good to go.

# Check “This collection is unrevealed”
# Press “Submit”
# Follow the “Post to Collection” link
# Fill in required information (the collection info will already be filled in because you used the “Post to Collection” link)
# Post Without Preview
# Repeat previous 3 steps until you have your desired number of works
# Return to the collection, e.g. by following the link in the work meta
# Follow the “Collection Settings” link
# Uncheck "This collection is unrevealed"
# Press "Update"

h1. What happens
Most of the works are revealed, but not all of them.

h1. What should happen
All of the works should be revealed.

h1. Notes
The {{CollectionItem}} for the work correctly has its {{unrevealed}} column updated to {{false}}. However, the corresponding {{Work}} does not get its {{in_unrevealed_collection}} column updated to {{false}}. It's _not_ a case of the work belonging to multiple unrevealed collections, as you can see from the following example (identifying data removed):

{quote}2.3.0 :007 > work = Work.find(000)
=> \#<Work id: 000, expected_number_of_chapters: 1, created_at: "2018-10-01 18:06:16", updated_at: "2018-10-19 01:59:30", major_version: 1, minor_version: 2, posted: true, language_id: 1, restricted: false, word_count: 0, hidden_by_admin: false, delta: false, revised_at: "2018-10-01 18:07:07", backdate: false, imported_from_url: nil, hit_count_old: 0, last_visitor_old: nil, complete: true, summary_sanitizer_version: 1, notes_sanitizer_version: 1, endnotes_sanitizer_version: 1, work_skin_id: nil, in_anon_collection: false, in_unrevealed_collection: true, anon_commenting_disabled: false, spam: false, spam_checked_at: "2018-10-01 18:10:38", moderated_commenting_enabled: false>

2.3.0 :008 > work.collection_items
=> \#<ActiveRecord::Associations::CollectionProxy \[\#<CollectionItem id: 000, collection_id: 000, item_id: 000, item_type: "Work", user_approval_status: 1, collection_approval_status: 1, created_at: "2018-10-01 18:06:17", updated_at: "2018-10-01 22:40:14", anonymous: false, unrevealed: false>\]>

{quote}
Quite possibly a race condition and quite possibly related to [AO3-5533|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5533].

{{CollectionItem.update_work}} is one of the few {{after_commit}} callbacks we have that tries to read data that was just written in the previous commit. Because it's an {{after_commit}} callback, not an {{after_save}}, the database queries to look up {{user_approved_collection_items}} (in {{update_anon_unrevealed}}, which is called by {{CollectionItem.update_work}}) occur _outside_ of the transaction, which in theory would allow them them be routed to the read-only SQL servers, which have some chance of lagging behind the master SQL server by a transaction or two. (h/t ticking instant for the discovery and explanation.)

[AO3-5532|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5532] can also cause some works in a collection to stay unrevealed, but the major difference is _that_ involves a 500 error when updating the collection settings. This does not have an error.

This can probably happen with anonymous works, too, but we’re not sure.

h1. Testing
Because this cannot be reproduced at will, it is unlikely the fix can be tested. All we can do is take several shots at posting to and then revealing an unrevealed collection to confirm the correct behavior still happens and watch for any new reports of this bug after the fix is deployed.

column1: Automate gem updates with Dependabot
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Right now we get notified of vulnerabilities by gem_security.sh, which fails builds. This makes it difficult to see other test failures.

If we use [Dependabot|https://dependabot.com/], we will get notified of gem vulnerabilities by pull requests that modified Gemfile/Gemfile.lock. The new workflow would be like:

- The bot open pull requests for gem updates. The bot can be configured to use the necessary labels: "Gem Updates" and "Awaiting Reviews".
- We create JIRA issues and edit the issue IDs into the bot's PR titles. After that, the workflow goes on as normal. As long as the issue is in JIRA and the PR is open, we won't forget about the update.

To switch to the bot, we need to:

- Modify gem_security.sh to stop "exit 1".
- Modify the Gemfile to use the Ruby version explicitly: the bot cannot resolve File.read.
- Sign up for an account on the bot site (any staffer can do it).
- Set the bot to run daily, and only include security updates.
- On the first PR by the bot, set the default labels for future PRs.

19/Dec/18 8:59 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;From a discussion with ticking instant:

- Devise automatically logs users out when they [change passwords|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/5cf864c5d48637c8bea9dc9223ebceb086ca44ff/app/controllers/users_controller.rb#L67-L71], we don't need to do anything special.
- The configuration {{config.sign_in_after_reset_password}} would apply if we were using Recoverable (specifically, to make it so that when you visit the link that Devise sends and modify your password, you don't have to sign in), but since Recoverable isn't [one of the modules for Users|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/5cf864c5d48637c8bea9dc9223ebceb086ca44ff/app/models/user.rb#L6-L12], it does nothing at the moment.
- We do password resets differently: when users request a reset, we emails them a temporary password (reset_password_token, instead of the usual password column) they can use to log in. This doesn't go through Devise. We [explicitly log users out as soon as a password reset is requested|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/87f62a26b7ddef58935e7c486f3bf2087468b6cc/app/controllers/passwords_controller.rb#L19-L21].

So everything works as intended:

- Users get logged out (of only the current session) when requesting a password reset
- Users get logged out (of all sessions) when changing password.

We don't have to change anything further for this issue.

column27:
[R.I.P Paperclip 2007-2018|https://robots.thoughtbot.com/closing-the-trombone].

Once we're on Rails 5.2, we should migrate from Paperclip to the recommended replacement, [Active Storage|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/v5.2/active_storage_overview.html].

*Testing*

# Before this is deployed, some testers should upload new icons for their default pseuds.
# After this is deployed, if you did Step 1, please confirm the icon is still present.
# Regardless of whether you did Step 1 and 2, you can test the following:
## Upload a new pseud icon
## Reset your pseud icon to the default
## Upload a collection profile picture
## Create a skin with a preview image

*Deploy Instructions*

This needs to be put on 1 appserver before being deployed everywhere. Then, run the ansible on that server with branch [https://github.com/OTWSystems/ansible/tree/feat/active-storage-config|https://github.com/OTWSystems/ansible/tree/feat/active-storage-config|smart-link]. Next, migrate to add the required tables:

{noformat}VERSION=20240323013245 rails db:migrate:up{noformat}

After that is done, start a screen session and run

{noformat}rake After:migrate_collection_icons
rake After:migrate_pseud_icons
rake After:migrate_skin_icons{noformat}

 (yes, this lives in after because we need to do it both before and after, and the second is the most important). This task will likely take quite some time. Once it is done, we can run the deploy as normal (and then as soon as possible afterwards apply the Ansible to push out the required configs).

Finally, re-run the After task to catch any icons uploaded on old servers during the deploy.

21/Mar/20 3:42 PM;557058:ec29aa28-e2ac-43d5-8086-db7b2491f462;ActiveStorage is good if you want to attach media (images, video) to a model. It’s super easy to set up and Rails does all the nitty gritty. You then get some additional stuff for free, like generating thumbnails for video files, or generating variants of images in additonal sizes. Also things like generating a preview image for a PDF, for example. Uploading to s3/other cloud storage is also provided functionality.

But if you want to do things like edit the uploaded file (convert a video file to a different format and use that instead of the original, for example) or generally use it for non-media files, the documentation gets a lot more sparse and there’s also not a lot of tutorials/blog posts for that. My use case was uploading an XML file, running code that adjusts that XML file, and override the original file with the changed one. I got it to work, but it was a lot harder than expected and I don’t feel confident that my solution is actually any good.

While researching my problem, the recommendations I’ve seen is to use Shrine if you have complex requirements. [Shrine on github|https://github.com/shrinerb/shrine]. It covers a lot more use cases and is still maintained. I don’t have any personal experience with it.

There’s also a maintained fork of paperclip: [kt-paperclip|https://github.com/kreeti/kt-paperclip]. Again, have not tried it myself. But I would expect it to be backwards-compatible with paperclip?

For our current requirements ActiveStorage would be the easy, fast and sufficient solution. But once we get to media hosting, it might produce more work than going with Shrine from the start. And I don’t know if it’s possible/sensible to use both solutions at once. But if we trust the maintainer to be in it for the long run, kt-paperclip might actually be a drop-in replacement? (Without having verified it, just going by the assumption that a fork tries to maintain compatibility.)

column1: Comment pagination sometimes jumps back to top of page on works, always does so on news posts
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
You'll need a work and a news post with two or more pages of comments, and you'll need to load those comments *without* JavaScript.

For a news post, the URL will look like: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/\#\#\#?show_comments=true#comments|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/###?show_comments=true#comments]

For a single chapter work, the URL will look like: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/\#\#\#?show_comments=true#comments|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/###?show_comments=true#comments]

For a multi chapter work, the URL will look like: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/\#\#\#?show_comments=true&view_full_work=true#comments|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/###?show_comments=true&view_full_work=true#comments]

h1. What should happen
When you use the pagination to navigate between pages of comments, the page that is loaded should have a comments anchor on the end of its URL, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/\#\#\#?page=2&show_comments=true#comments|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/###?page=2&show_comments=true#comments], which should position the comment form at the top of the screen (or the kudos section, if you’re using a work).

h1. What does happen
In reality, this never appears to happen with news posts. It sometimes appears to happen with works.

Tested while logged in, with preferences set to show full work by default and not to warn for adult content. It seems more likely to keep the anchor on works rated Explicit, Mature, or Not Rated, but I am not 100% sure that is the key. redsummernight notes that if they access a work while logged out and have to navigate past the adult content warning, the comments anchor is lost on the pagination (i.e. if you start at [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/704022?show_comments=true&view_full_work=true#comments], following “Proceed” takes you to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/704022?show_comments=true&view_adult=true&view_full_work=true#comments], and then the anchor disappears when following one of the pagination links.)

Just to reiterate, this only applies when loading comments via the URL parameters, not AJAX. That has its own issues ( [AO3-5204|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5204] ).

This table was retrieved with an index scan, which is like a full table scan, except it only hits the index (not the actual table). This is usually not great for performance.

column1: Fix performance issue in definition of approved_collections.
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Currently, when you call {{Work.find(id).approved_collections}} on a work that has at least one approved collection, it generates an extra database query:

{code:java}2.3.4 :004 > Work.find(5).approved_collections
  Work Load (1.0ms)  SELECT  `works`.* FROM `works` WHERE `works`.`id` = 5 LIMIT 1
  ↳ (irb):4:in `irb_binding'
  Collection Load (0.5ms)  SELECT  `collections`.* FROM `collections` INNER JOIN `collection_items` ON `collections`.`id` = `collection_items`.`collection_id` WHERE `collection_items`.`item_id` = 5 AND `collection_items`.`item_type` = 'Work' AND `collection_items`.`user_approval_status` = 1 AND `collection_items`.`collection_approval_status` = 1 LIMIT 11
  CollectionItem Load (0.4ms)  SELECT `collection_items`.* FROM `collection_items` WHERE `collection_items`.`collection_id` IN (1, 3){code}

The first query, of course, is the work being loaded from {{Work.find(5)}}. The second query loads the {{approved_collections}}, just as desired. But the third query loads every single CollectionItem in one of the work's approved collections (not just the work's CollectionItems). This means that if you have a single work {{w}} in a collection with thousands of collection items, calling {{w.approved_collections}} will load every one of those thousands of CollectionItems.

This shouldn't happen. The third query is the result of a mistake in the definition of {{approved_collections}}, and should disappear when the definition is fixed.

Note that this also affects {{user_approved_collections}} and {{rejected_collections}}.

*Testing instructions*

# Go into the rails console.
# Make sure that {{ActiveRecord::Base.logger.level}} is set low enough that you see SQL queries.
# Find a work with at least one approved collection.
# Call {{Work.find(id).approved_collections}}, and make sure that it results in exactly two database queries.

column1: Prompt Meme: Posting a work that fulfills multiple prompts doesn't notify all prompters.
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps:*

# Start a prompt meme, or pick an existing one that's open to new prompts.
# Log in as a user with an email address that you have access to.
# Create a new prompt in the prompt meme.
# Log in as a second user (with a different email address that you have access to).
# Create another new prompt in the same prompt meme.
# Log in as a third user.
# Claim both prompts.
# Open the "New Work" form.
# Check the boxes for both prompts under "Open Claims."
# Fill in the rest of the form.
# Post Without Preview
# Check the email associated with both prompters.

*What Should Happen:* Both prompters are notified about the work that was posted for their prompt.

*What Actually Happens:* Only one prompter gets an email.

The {{UserMailer#prompter_notification}} method takes only the work as an argument, and tries to loop through the work’s claims and call {{mail()}} for each one. However, calling {{mail()}} doesn’t actually send a message; it just sets the variable {{message}}, which is later used to send a single email when {{deliver}} is called. The loop needs to be moved out of the {{UserMailer}} and into the places that call {{prompter_notification}}.

*Update April 2026:*

This bug was fixed as part of [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/5238|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/5238|smart-link] . However, an automated test for this would still be nice to have. So let’s use this issue to add that.

column1: Migrate kudos to BIGINT, add uniqueness constraint, and clean up duplicate kudos
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We need to migrate the primary key on the kudos table to BIGINT and add a uniqueness constraint to kill the duplicate kudos bug once and for all. Also, we need to clean up existing double kudos.

Note that the clean up cannot be run until we have a post warning users about it. If we do it without a warning, there may be panic in the streets when people see their kudos numbers drop.

h2. Testing
Make sure you can still leave kudos, logged in and logged out, and that you cannot kudos the same work twice. 

To test the clean up, you could find some works that already have duplicate (triplicate, etc) kudos, but it’s probably easiest if someone with database access inserts duplicate kudos on a few works before this change is deployed to staging, and then we can double check that they get cleaned up.
column147:
09/Mar/19 2:03 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;Add a Rails migration to change the primary key type, clean up duplicates, and add the unique constraint. The migrations will be used in development and CI environments.

On test and production sites, we will use pt-online-schema-change (as we did for AO3-4056), which handles the key type change and unique constraint addition; we get the duplicate clean up for free.

If the user has already left multiple kudos on a single work by switching their default pseud, then they may be unable to delete either pseud (since deleting a pseud tries to transfer all kudos over to the default).

07/Jan/20 11:29 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;Instead of fixing the issue with switching pseuds, we could change kudos to be tied to users instead of pseuds ([~accountid:557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b]). So the plan becomes (each step can be in a separate release):

- Migration: add a user_id column to the kudos table, indexed but not (yet) unique, unused.
-- Should we use a foreign key constraint here? User deletion will guarantee kudos deletions.
--- No, because the kudos [should stick around as guest kudos|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/8506d487cfd11d33d78f5c276c5da5d81f9ae6e9/app/models/user.rb#L137].
- Add code to save user ids for new non-guest kudos, and scrub user ids from kudos when users are deleted.
-- Also add a task to fill in user ids for old non-guest kudos.
- Change all kudos displays to use users instead of pseuds. Remove code that attaches pseuds to kudos / updates kudos when default pseuds change.
-- The kudos mailer should start using user names as well ([~accountid:557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6]). Since kudos emails don't link to the kudos givers (yet, AO3-3154), it should be fine if we have a mix of pseuds and users in RedisMailQueue during the transition.
-- After this step the pseud_id column should be unused.
- Downtime! Migrate primary key to bigint, add unique constraints (commentable + user_id, commentable + ip_address), in the process removing kudos duplicates.
- Remove unused column pseud_id.

column1: Rejecting a work from an unrevealed or anonymous collection leaves the work unrevealed or anonymous
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce
# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information and check either “This collection is anonymous” or “This collection is unrevealed.” You could even go wild and check both.
# Press “Submit”
# Follow “Post to Collection” to open the posting form with the collection info filled in
# Fill in required information
# Press “Post Without Preview”
# Return to your collection
# Manage Items > Approved
# From the select menu for the work that currently says “Approved,” choose “Rejected”
# Press “Submit”

h1. What happens
The work is moved to the rejected page, but it remains unrevealed and anonymous.

h1. What should happen
The work and its creator should be revealed.

column148:
12/May/20 4:26 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;This seems like it might pose some difficulties for maintainers, particularly those of moderated collections. If the creator deliberately submitted their work to the unrevealed/anonymous collection, that means that they intended for the work to be unrevealed/anonymous (at least for a period of time). So maintainers might hesitate to reject works from unrevealed/anonymous collections.

Unfortunately, if maintainers don’t want to reject outright and reveal/de-anon the work, that leaves them with no way to communicate to the creator that they have seen the work, but don’t think the work in its current state belongs in the collection.

column1: Unwrangled tag count doesn't decrease when tag is wrangled to a different fandom
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce
# Log in as a tag wrangler.
# Post a work in one of your assigned fandoms, and on that work, include at least two brand new tags. We'll assume they are freeforms called Tag A and Tag B.
# Go to your wrangling page ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers/USERS]) and follow the appropriate link to see these unwrangled tags. In the case of our example, you'd be going to the unwrangled freeform page for your fandom ([https://archiveofourown.org/tags/FANDOM/wrangle?show=freeforms&status=unwrangled]).
# In the Tag Name column of the table, check the box next to Tag A.
# In the "Wrangle to Fandom(s)" field, enter the name of your fandom (or choose it from the autocomplete).
# Press one of the "Wrangle" buttons.
# Return to your wrangling page and note that the number of unwrangled tags for your fandom has decreased.
# Again, follow the appropriate link to see the remaining unwrangled tag you created.
# In the Tag Name column of the table, check the box next to Tag B.
# In the "Wrangle to Fandom(s)" field, enter the name of some other fandom, e.g. No Fandom.
# Press one of the "Wrangle" buttons.
# Return to your wrangling page.

h1. What should happen
The number of unwrangled tags for your fandom should decrease.

h1. What happens instead
The number of unwrangled tags for your fandom is the same.

h1. Notes
Wrangling a tag to a fandom currently updates the unwrangled tag count for the fandom the tag was wrangled _to_. This happens because the fandom tag's updated_at date is changed, which [changes the cache key|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/5c29fc05e5f56019855970763b50f2efff928f4c/app/models/tag.rb#L1252].

Instead, it should update the unwrangled tag count of the tag's _suggested fandoms_ (pre_fandom_ids in Elasticsearch), since those are the counts that are actually affected when the tag is wrangled. It would probably make sense to do this with a callback in CommonTagging.

column1: Restore string columns' empty default values removed by the UTF8MB4 upgrade
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
In AO3-4056, we [converted the database to UTF8MB4 encoding|https://railsmachine.com/articles/2017/05/19/converting-a-rails-database-to-utf8mb4.html].

The second stage conversion script does this:
{code:ruby}
default = (column.default.blank?) ? '' : "DEFAULT \"#{column.default}\""
{code}

This means columns with {{DEFAULT ''}} lose that attribute. Let's add them back:

- archive_faqs: slug
- collections: icon_alt_text, icon_comment_text
- invite_requests: simplified_email
- languages: sortable_name
- pseuds: icon_alt_text, icon_comment_text
- skins: icon_alt_text
- taggings: tagger_type, taggable_type
- tags: name, sortable_name

Note that the conversion script would work correctly if we replaced instances of {{column.default.blank?}} with {{column.default.nil?}}.

column1: Rename Warning class
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Our current code uses a class named Warning for Archive warning [+tags+|https://archiveofourown.org/faq/tags?language_id=en#whatisatag]. This class will need to be renamed ArchiveWarning to avoid conflicts with newer versions of Ruby. We would like this change to be made in a separate pull request prior to upgrading Ruby.
 
 Unfortunately, there are numerous places in our code where we use the tag class names to create user-facing text. For example, we call tag_type.classify.pluralize to create [headings in this tag set partial|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/46e9d9b713ba54dc6e6beb14e50255196c2465cc/app/views/tag_set_nominations/_show_by_tag_type.html.erb#L3]. In this case, renaming the Warning class would have the unwanted side effect of changing the user-facing text from "Warnings" to "ArchiveWarnings". 
 
 Fortunately, [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5123#icft=AO3-5123|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5123#icft=AO3-5123|smart-link] ([pull request|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3013/files]) has a solution for dealing with situations where the preferred display text does _not_ match the class name. Much like [the label_name for the Freeform class|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3013/files#diff-eb166e301667da04821038f1e54effc5R5] was set to "Additional Tags", we'd like to set the label_name for the ArchiveWarning class to "Warnings". Then we'd like to use this method in our views as much as possible.
 
 It's also important to ensure that class names used in the HTML don't get changed from warning/warnings to archivewarning/archivewarnings/archive_warning/archive_warnings/etc. The existing class names get used a lot by Archive users who create site skins (e.g. some people want to hide things related to warnings, whereas other users want to highlight warnings).
 
 *Reference*
 
 A [+branch+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/compare/master...sarken:AO3-5037_ruby_rename_warning?expand=1] containing an initial pass at this is available on GitHub. 
 
 There is also an [earlier pull request|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3526] that predates the introduction of the label_name method.
 
 *Testing notes*
 
 This affects the CSS classes used on warning-related areas, so please create a site skin with the following CSS and use it while testing:
 
 {code}.Warning,
 .Warnings,
 .Archive_Warning,
 .Archive_Warnings,
 .ArchiveWarning,
 .ArchiveWarnings,
 .Archive,
 .Archives,
 .archive_warning,
 .archive_warnings,
 .archivewarning,
 .archivewarnings,
 .archive,
 .archives {
 background: hotpink !important;
 font-size: 1.5em;
 outline: 5px solid hotpink !important;
 }{code}
 
 If you see anything highlighted or outlined in pink, please comment with a screenshot. (Feel free to change it to some other color that is more noticeable to you, but make sure to leave the \!important.)
 
 *Testing notes II*
 
While wearing the hotpink site skin:
 
- Viewing works
-- Links to Warnings on work metas and work blurbs work.
-- Work blurbs show the correct symbols for Warnings.
-- Share a work: embed code should have warnings.
-- Tag RSS feed: links to Warnings show up and work.
-- Download a work (any format): links to Warnings show up and work.
-- Turn on/off preference: "Hide warnings (you can still choose to show them)." Check that this option behaves correctly on work metas (top of each work) and work blurbs (in search results). The links "Show warnings"/"Hide warnings" should work.

- Bookmark filters
-- Include every tag type using checkboxes (checkboxes remain checked after "Sort and Filter")
-- Exclude every tag type using checkboxes (checkboxes remain checked after "Sort and Filter")
-- Warnings are aggregated correctly on the filters (breakdown: CCNA has how many, NAWA has how many, etc., should be sensible numbers).

- Work filters
-- Include every tag type using checkboxes (checkboxes remain checked after "Sort and Filter")
-- Exclude every tag type using checkboxes (checkboxes remain checked after "Sort and Filter")
-- Warnings are aggregated correctly on the filters (breakdown: CCNA has how many, NAWA has how many, etc., should be sensible numbers).

- Posting and editing works
-- Post a work without a warning. Expect the "Warning is missing" error. With and without preview.
-- Post a work with warnings. Warnings should show. With and without preview.
-- Edit a work's warnings ("Edit"). With and without preview.
-- Edit a work's warnings ("Edit Tags"). With and without preview.
-- Edit a work's warnings ("Edit Tags", as admin). With and without preview.
-- Edit/orphan/delete multiple works. The section "Your edits will be applied to all of the following works:" has the correct warnings, links work.

- Importing works
-- Import a work without specifying warnings. Expect the work to have "Choose Not To Use Archive Warnings".
-- Import a work while specifying warnings. Expect the work to have the specified warnings.
-- Import a work with "Warnings: Underage" in the body, and without specifying warnings on the import form. Expect the work to have the "Underage" warning.
-- Import a work with "Warnings: WTF" in the body, and without specifying warnings on the import form. Expect the work to have the "Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings" warning, but not a "WTF" warning.
-- (Open Doors) Import a work with different warnings through the API

- Other bookmarkable types
-- Series have the right warnings (warnings from all the works in it).
-- Bookmark an external work with various kinds of tags: the tags should show up. External works don't have warnings however.
-- Bookmark search: search for bookmarked items of a specific type (Work/Series/External Work) that have certain warnings.

- Tag wrangling
-- Quick: wrangle as you would normally. Anything looks misspelled?
-- Edit a tag: "Category" shows tag type (singular). "Warning" for warnings.
-- Edit a tag: Expect "This is the official name for the Warning".
-- Edit a tag: Cannot change name of warnings.
-- New tag: Options spelled correctly? (Note: Need to be logged in as admin to see Warning option.)

- Subscriptions
-- Subscription emails show warnings for new chapters of subbed works.
-- Subscription emails show warnings for new works of subbed series.
-- Subscription emails show warnings for new works/chapters of subbed users.

- Tag sets and challenges
-- Create a tag set with canonical warnings.
-- Create a tag set with noncanonical warnings (these exist because of an unrelated bugs, e.g. "IT HAS WAY TOO MUCH SEX RUN FOR YOUR LIFE" on staging).
-- Add a warning to an existing tag set.
-- Remove a warning from an existing tag set.
-- With a prompt meme using a tag set, expect the sign-up form to have only the warnings from the tag set, and that you can select them.
-- Include warnings on gift exchange sign-ups, run matching and expect matches. Also participants can expect to receive emails containing their assignment, including warning tags.
-- Include warnings on gift exchange sign-ups (where the exchange uses a tag set containing warnings), run matching and expect matches.
-- In a gift exchange, enable Optional Tags (set count as warnings) in request and offers.

*Steps to reproduce*
# Log in as a wrangler
# Find yourself an unwrangled tag, e.g. by going to the freeform bin: https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=freeforms
# Follow the "Edit" link for the unwrangled tag you want to work with
# Check the "Unwrangleable" box, but do not enter anything in the "Fandoms" field
# Press "Save changes"

*What happens*
The tag is marked unwrangleable! It has also disappeared from any and all bins because there is no fandom attached.

*What should happen*
You should get an error message that says, "Sorry, you can't mark a tag unwrangleable until it has a fandom."

If the tag you're editing is a fandom, the Unwrangleable section of the form should just... not be there, because fandoms are never supposed to be marked unwrangleable. (For thoroughness, we probably want to add a backend check rather than just relying on the checkbox not appearing in the view. If you need an error message, that one can be, "Sorry, you can't mark a fandom unwrangleable.")

column1: Tag connections are lost when canonical tags are synned, aka the Tag Drop bug
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps to reproduce*

Log in as an admin. On the edit page of a canonical tag, use the "Synonym of" field to syn that canonical tag to another tag, existing or not. This bug is intermittent, so it may take several tries to trigger it.

*What happens*

Periodically, all the connections from the old canonical tag are not transferred to the new tag. This includes metatags, subtags, synonyms, and other child tags. It's most obvious with fandom and character tags, which tend to have a lot of child tags. With fandom tags, this results in all the child tags and synonyms appearing in the mass bins again, as they have lost their fandom connection.

*What should happen*

All tag connections from the canonical should be transferred to the tag it is synned to, whether that tag is newly created or existed before.

Because this bug does not always happen, testing should be conducted on many tags.
column147:
08/Feb/19 6:37 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Setting {{syn_string=}} to a valid merger results in an async call to transfer the associations:

{code}        if new_merger && self.errors.empty?
          self.canonical = false
          self.merger_id = new_merger.id
          async(:add_merger_associations){code}
([Source|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/96935fb4a4bd73575e4ddcaee96b8b31d9e8ad2b/app/models/tag.rb#L1174-L1177])

However, that action also triggers another async call in a {{before_update}} hook in the Tag class:

{code}    if self.canonical_changed? && !self.canonical?
      self.async(:remove_canonical_associations){code}
([Source|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/96935fb4a4bd73575e4ddcaee96b8b31d9e8ad2b/app/models/tag.rb#L1082-L1083])

Since setting the synonym also sets canonical to false at the same time, as soon as the tag is saved this callback will queue up a call to {{remove_canonical_associations}} (which does exactly what you’d think).

So effectively you have dueling asynchronous function calls. If {{add_merger_associations}} acts first, the associations are transferred properly. If {{remove_canonical_associations}} acts first, the associations are deleted instead of transferring.

(The call to {{add_merger_associations}} is enqueued first, so technically it should be run first, if only by a narrow margin. But it also takes more time to run, so if both functions start at roughly same time, {{remove_canonical_associations}} is more likely to finish first.)
column148: 08/Feb/19 11:17 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;This can also result from stale data. The call to {{add_merger_associations}} only works if the merger can be read from the database at the beginning of {{add_merger_associations}}, but it’s added to the Resque queue before anything is even written to the database.

column1: Add images to EPUB, MOBI, and AZW3 downloads
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
On production, if you download an EPUB and open it in Apple Books, the image will display as long as you are connected to the internet.

However, with the Calibre-based code, the image does not display if you are online. In fact, the code for the image is stripped out.

Let's stick the images in the EPUB file so they always display, regardless of your internet connectivity. Heck, let's make them work in MOBI and AZW3, too. (PDF already has them, and we can’t really do this for HTML, since that is a single file, not a container. However, HTML should continue to display images as long as you are connected to the internet.)

Ideally, when you open a file with a large image, the image will be resized so it does not extend past the edges of the page. This seems to be default behavior in many programs (Kindle app on Mac OS, Apple Books/iBooks on Mac OS and iOS, Kobo Reader on iOS) but we'll add {{max-width: 100%}} to our CSS in hopes of helping programs where it is not the default (Bluefire Reader on iOS is the only known problem at this time).

*How to test*: Download some works with images! Make sure they display even when you're not online!

column1: Works cannot be edited due to missing creatorships, usually after transferring the work to a different account
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Occasionally, we hear from users who cannot edit their works. Some users report a 500 error. Others say when they try to save their edits with or without previewing, the page refreshes the Edit Work page. The URL in the browser bar is for the work, but the page they see is the Edit Work page, and the edits are not saved. (Note: this is consistent with other errors when posting, e.g. if you disable JavaScript and attempt to remove the work title. The difference is other errors have a useful error message.) Still others receive the following error:

{quote}Sorry\! We couldn't save this work because:
translation missing: en.activerecord.errors.models.work.attributes.base.base{quote}

99 times out of 100, this turns out to be caused by the first chapter of the work (which can be a single or multi-chapter work) not having a Creatorship. The work generally does have a creatorship:

{quote}2.3.4 :010 > w = Work.find(000)
=> #<Work id: 000...
2.3.4 :011 > w.creatorships
=> #<ActiveRecord::Associations::CollectionProxy \[#<Creatorship id: 61349501, creation_id: 000, creation_type: "Work", pseud_id: ...
2.3.4 :012 > w.chapters.first.creatorships
=> #<ActiveRecord::Associations::CollectionProxy \[]>{quote}

This often – but possibly not always – happens when the user has transferred the work to a different account. This is done by adding the second account as a co-creator and then removing the first creator.

One report (Zoho ticket 212046) specifically says this happened after mass editing multiple single-chapter fics to switch accounts. Could this be related to AO3-3915?

*Notes*

The changes in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5658|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5658|smart-link] should prevent any further instances of missing creatorships. However, there will still be some existing works work missing creatorships. 

When editing works with missing creatorships:

# If you press Preview and then Update to edit the work, it works fine, and silently fixes the broken creatorships.
#  If you press Post Without Preview to edit the work, it will generate a pair of confusing error messages, but otherwise resolve itself:

{quote}Sorry\! We couldn't save this work because:
* Chapters creatorships pseud has already been taken
* Invalid chapter: Chapter must have at least one creator.{quote}

*Testing notes*

A database admin will need to break some works' creatorships for this to be tested.

*How to reproduce:*

# Press “Yes, link me!” to confirm the link between the works
# Go to the parent work from step 3
# Download > EPUB, AZW3, HTML, or PDF

*What happens:*

The title of the work inspired by the downloaded work overlaps the words "Works inspired by this one."

I've attached images of the HTML, AZW3, PDF, and EPUB downloads to illustrate. MOBI just has somewhat awkward positioning of the text, but when testing the fix, we should check that it looks okay there, too.

It’s also a good idea to check that there are no issues when there are multiple child works.

*What should happen instead:*

The text shouldn't do that.

To fix it, we'll want to override the following style for the afterword section:

{code:java}.meta dd { margin: -1em 0 0 10em; }{code}

This should probably be fine:

{code:java}.afterword .meta dd { margin: 1em 0 0 1em; }{code}

column1: Possible to delete only posted chapter of a work, preventing everyone from accessing the work except in full work mode
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Currently, the only posted chapter of a work with at least one draft chapter can be deleted.

*Steps:*

# Create work with single chapter.
# Add at least one draft chapter.
# Delete the posted chapter.

*What happens:* 

Posted chapter is deleted, and draft chapter posts by default. Behavior of work and access to work becomes a bit buggy.

If there were multiple unposted draft chapters, chapter 2 typically posts, and chapter 3 fills now-empty chapter 1 position. Because new chapter 1 is a draft, direct link to work results in "Sorry, you don't have permission to access the page you were trying to reach. Please log in." redirect for non-creators. Posted chapter 2 can be accessed from the work's /navigate page. 

*What should happen:*

Creators should be prevented from deleting the only posted chapter, with error message, "Sorry, you can't delete the only posted chapter of a work. Please post another chapter first. You can also choose to delete the work."

*Testing note*

To keep the code a little simpler, we dropped the word “posted” from the requested error message. If this is too confusing, let us know!

column1: Edit Work page doesn't offer options for interacting with draft chapters if the work has only one posted chapter
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps to reproduce*

# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required information
# Press "Post Without Preview"
# Follow "Add Chapter"
# Fill in required information
# Press "Preview"
# Press "Save Without Posting" to save draft chapter
# Follow "Edit Work"

*What should happen*

To make sure users know they have multiple chapters and can access them, it should behave like editing a work with multiple posted chapters:

* Next to the "Add Chapter" button at the top of the form should be options to edit chapters, e.g. {{Edit Chapter: \[1\] \[2 (Draft)\] \[3 (Draft)\]}}, where the brackets indicate button-style text.
* Next to that should be a Manage Chapters link
** [AO3-4313|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4313] exists for resolving the issue of things not working properly if a user reorders their work so the first chapter is a draft.
** [AO3-3846|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3846] exists for making draft chapters visible on the reordering page.
* The Work Text section should not be displayed. Instead, the user should have to go to the relevant Edit Chapter page to edit a chapter’s text.

*What happens instead*

The options aren't there, making it easy to forget you have draft chapters and hard to get to them if you remember.

*Notes*

It appears this is related to caching.

* In the edit page navigation, we [only display the edit and manage links if @chapters|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/80c950525269715a85ebe63a58c234a2822fdac9/app/views/works/edit.html.erb#L10-L20].
* Ditto [the Work Text section on the edit form|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/80c950525269715a85ebe63a58c234a2822fdac9/app/views/works/_standard_form.html.erb#L286-L323].
* In the controller action, [@chapters is set to equal all chapters if number_of_chapters > 1|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/80c950525269715a85ebe63a58c234a2822fdac9/app/controllers/works_controller.rb#L341]
* _However_, [number_of_chapters is cached|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3463d1a8f9b349bd3f827098d43c10c786777f9b/app/models/work.rb#L752-L757].
* [The cache does not appear to be updated when a new draft chapter is added|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3463d1a8f9b349bd3f827098d43c10c786777f9b/app/models/work.rb#L622-L625].

column1: Use Calibre to generate PDF downloads
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We initially stuck with wkhtmltopdf for making PDF downloads [because Calibre needed xvfb installed|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/0da96bee3ca1587403ec5b73e8d3c2d192e7b0c6/app/models/download_writer.rb#L68-L79]. 

However! In the five years between the original Calibre pull request being submitted and it being deployed, Calibre stopped requiring xvfb for PDF generation.

Ergo, we would like to use Calibre for PDFs.

We're keeping this separate for the original move to Calibre (AO3-3880) because we learned this after putting up a post declaring we'd still be using wkhtmltopdf so changes to PDFs would be minimal. We can weigh whether this change needs a post once we get some previews.

*Testing*

When testing, we'll want to make sure PDFs look good in general, and especially in non-Latin languages and with images. 

It would be a good idea to download works like this on staging and production and compare them to see the scope of the changes:

* works with images (it would be especially good to know if they keep {{alt}} text, unlike current PDFs)
* works with embedded audio or video (using embeds from e.g., YouTube and Soundcloud as well as using the {{video}} and {{audio}} HTML tags)
* multi-chapter works, with work and chapter notes and chapter summaries 
* single chapter works, also ideally with notes and summaries 
* works that use a different alphabet than English, e.g. works in Chinese, Russian, and Hebrew

column1: Limit referrer information sent to other sites
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When you follow a link from the Archive to another site or go to a page with the Twitter widget (e.g. a work), a header like the following is sent to that site:

{code:java}Provisional headers are shown
DNT: 1
Referer: https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/0000/chapters/000?view_adult=true
Upgrade-Insecure-Requests: 1
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/72.0.3626.109 Safari/537.36{code}

The header contains the URL of the page you're coming from (or, in the case of Twitter, the page the widget is being loaded on – in other words, Twitter can tell what work you're accessing, and if you're logged in, that information is likely associated with your Twitter account).

To prevent this, we'd like to update [config/application.rb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/config/application.rb] to set the {{Referrer-Policy}} to {{same-origin}}, as described in [Setting HTTP security headers in Rails|https://www.marksayson.com/blog/setting_http_security_headers_in_rails/].

To test, open your browser’s developer tools and check the response headers after navigating from one Archive page to another. The {{Referrer-Policy}} should say {{same-origin}}. (You may need to consult Google for instructions specific to your browser.)

When testing, we should also make sure the Twitter share widget on works is still functional, and we should also check that New Relic still contains referrer information.

column1: Challenge assignment generation gets stuck, displaying "Assignments Generating" message forever
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Occasionally, challenge assignment generation will error and stop running, which results in the moderators seeing [the "Assignments Generating" message on the matching page|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/da6033ca608510b201324f4ab88cb92d8d04f78c/app/views/potential_matches/index.html.erb#L20-L24] basically forever.

The mod sees this message is because the progress key for assignment generation still exists. Therefore, a database admin has to delete the progress key ({{REDIS_GENERAL.del(ChallengeAssignment.progress_key(collection))}}), which will return the page to [its original state|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/da6033ca608510b201324f4ab88cb92d8d04f78c/app/views/potential_matches/index.html.erb#L25-L40] and allow the mods to try again.

Instead of making the moderators contact Support so a database admin can do this, when assignment generation errors, we should automatically return the matching page to its original state and add a red flash-style error message at the top that says, "Sorry, there was an error while generating assignments. Please try again."

Refer to AO3-3969 for the same thing, but with potential matches. It might make sense to do the two issues together.

column1: Caching on work index pages doesn't check for include_work_search or exclude_work_search
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps to Reproduce:*
# Log in (to avoid nginx's cache, since it may complicate the results).
# Visit the following URL for all Marvel works tagged with "Hurt/Comfort":
https://test.archiveofourown.org/works?include_work_search%5Bfreeform_ids%5D%5B%5D=2379&tag_id=Marvel
# Visit the main Marvel listing:
https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Marvel/works

*What Should Happen:* Visiting the first URL should show the first page of a search with a total of around 3,000 works, and should only display works that are tagged with a synonym or subtag of "Hurt/Comfort." Visiting the second URL should show the first page of a search with a total of around 50,000 works, and should include works that aren't tagged with "Hurt/Comfort."

*What Actually Happens:* Both pages show exactly the same search results. If the {{include_work_search}} version is cached, then the second URL will have the wrong number of results. If the plain version is cached, then the first URL will have the wrong number of results.

(I think in theory it might be possible to get the right results if the second page view is perfectly timed to match the 20 minute expiration for the search results cache, but otherwise both results will be the same -- and one of them will be wrong.)

*Explanation:* Currently, {{WorksController#index}} decides whether to cache the search results by checking {{params\[:work_search\]}} to ensure that the user hasn't refined their search in any way. But since the Elasticsearch upgrade, search parameters are split between {{params\[:work_search\]}}, {{params\[:include_work_search\]}}, and {{params\[:exclude_work_search\]}}.

In normal use, any query that sets {{params\[:include_work_search\]}} or {{params\[:exclude_work_search\]}} will also set {{params\[:work_search\]}}, so this isn't an issue.

However, if someone tries to edit the URL to eliminate blank parameters, they may end up with a search that sets only {{params\[:include_work_search\]}} and/or {{params\[:exclude_work_search\]}}, without also setting {{params\[:work_search\]}}. That kind of search is cached using the same cache key as a blank search. As a result, if one person visits the page with extra search params and one person doesn't, the results that both receive will depend on who visits the page first.

Either {{WorksController#index}} should also check both {{params\[:include_work_search\]}} and {{params\[:exclude_work_search\]}}, or the work search parameters should be refactored so that they all fall under {{params\[:work_search\]}}.

column1: Remove unused code from Bookmark model
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
There are a number of functions in {{app/models/bookmark.rb}} that were originally used to calculate information about the bookmarkable for use in indexing/search. But now that bookmark search uses {{BookmarkedWorkIndexer}}, {{BookmarkedExternalWorkIndexer}}, and {{BookmarkedSeriesIndexer}} to index information about the bookmarkables, those functions are unused.

The following functions have information about the bookmarkable alone:

* bookmarkable_pseud_names
* bookmarkable_pseud_ids
* bookmarkable_collection_ids
* bookmarkable_title
* bookmarkable_posted
* bookmarkable_restricted
* bookmarkable_hidden
* bookmarkable_complete
* bookmarkable_language_id

(Note that bookmarkable_date should *not* be deleted, because it's still used by the {{BookmarkIndexer}}.)

In addition, the following functions were formerly used to calculate information about the bookmark's tags and the bookmarkable's tags:

* tag
* tag_ids
* filters
* filters_for_facets
* filter_names
* filter_ids
* fandom_ids
* character_ids
* relationship_ids
* freeform_ids
* rating_ids
* warning_ids
* category_ids

All of these functions are currently unused, and should be deleted (to improve code coverage and make it easier to follow the flow of control in the parts of the class that are being used).

*Testing Instructions:* As long as the PR passes automated tests, I'm not sure any manual testing is required. (Since these functions were only used in indexing, the indexing in the automated tests would fail if any critical functions were missing.) But if you wanted to be thorough, you could try creating a bookmark on a brand new work and ensure it can be found with bookmark search.

column1: Tag Set nominations aren't updated when the nominating pseud is deleted
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Tag Set nominations are tied to pseuds, but when the pseud in question is deleted (not the user as a whole, just the pseud), the nominations are untouched (meaning that they still exist in the database, and still point to a pseud that no longer exists).

This doesn't appear to cause any 500 errors, but it does remove all association between the user and their previous nominations, allowing the user to nominate tags to the same tag set multiple times.

*Steps to reproduce:*

# Log in as User A.
# Go to Browse > Tags > Tag Sets > New Tag Set.
# Check the "Currently taking nominations?" box.
# Make sure that at least one of the numbers in the "Nomination Limits" section is non-zero.
# Fill in the rest of the fields as desired and press "Submit" to create the tagset.
# Log in as User B.
# Go to My Preferences > Manage My Pseuds > New Pseud.
# Fill in the fields as desired and press "Create" to create a new pseud.
# View the tag set created by User A and click "Nominate."
# Select the pseud that you just created.
# Nominate tags as desired, and then press "Submit."
# Go to My Preferences > Manage My Pseuds.
# Find the pseud that you just created/nominated for, and press the "Delete" button.
# View the tag set again and click "Nominate."
# Nominate different tags from before and press "Submit."
# Log in as User A.
# View nominations for the tag set, and note that both of User B's nominations are visible.

*What should happen:* When User B views the tag set the second time, they should see the "My Nominations" button, not the "Nominate" button. (Note that the button in the list of tag sets always has the label "Nominate," regardless of whether you've nominated before. But if you click on it it should redirect to the nominations that you previously submitted, not to a page that allows you to enter new nominations.)

*How to fix it:* Either tag set nominations should be associated with the user instead of the pseud (since it's not like anyone other than the nominating user can see which pseud they used), or the pseud_id on tag nominations should be updated to the default pseud whenever a pseud is deleted.

column27:

#* The invitation should disappear from the invitations page.
#* The creation's byline should list A.
#* The creation should appear in A's work/series listings after a few minutes.
#* User A should be able to edit the creation.
# If User A rejects the invitation, then:
#* The invitation should disappear from the invitations page.
#* The creation's byline should not list A.
#* When User B edits the creation:
#** They should no longer see User A listed as being invited.
#** They should be permitted to re-invite User A to the same creation.
# If an archivist tries to add User A as a co-creator, then:
#* User A should be added as a co-creator, not just invited.
#* User A should immediately be listed as a co-creator on the creation.
#* The creation should appear in User A's listings.
#* User A should receive an email telling them that they're listed as a co-creator.

*If User A has the preference option disabled (the default), then:*
# User A should not see a "Creator Invitations" link in their dashboard sidebar.
# If User B tries to add User A as a co-creator, then:
#* User B should see an error message saying that's not allowed.
#* User A should not receive an email.
#* The creation should not appear in any searches or listings related to User A.
# If A and B are already listed as co-creators on a work, then:
#* User B should be able to edit the work.
#* User B should be able to add User A to any chapter of that work.
#* However, they should not be able to add User A to a chapter of another work.
#* User B should be able to add the work to a series, thus adding User A to the series.
#* User B shouldn't be able to add User A to any other series.
# If User A had an invitation from User B before they disabled co-creators, then:
#* User A should not see "Creator Invitations" link in their dashboard sidebar.
#* However, when User A views the work, they should see a notice about an invitation.
#* The notice should link to their "Creator Invitations" page.
#* User A should be able to accept/reject the invitation as normal.
#* User B should be able to edit the creation.
# If an archivist tries to add User A as a co-creator, then:
#* They shouldn't get an error.
#* User A should immediately be listed as a co-creator on the creation.
#* The creation should appear in User A's listings.
#* User A should receive an email telling them that they're listed as a co-creator.

*Miscellaneous Notes:*
# Manually adding orphan_account as a co-creator will result in the invitation being automatically accepted.
# It's possible to both be listed as a co-creator and invited to be a co-creator simultaneously, if you have multiple pseuds that are invited to the same work and only accept one invitation. However, when you edit the creation, the invitation will silently disappear. (I'm not sure if this behavior is desirable, but it occurs because you implicitly rejected the invitation by not selecting the invited pseud from the "Creator/Pseud(s)" box while editing. # Try using the Edit Multiple Works page to change which of your pseuds are listed in the byline.
# Try using the Edit Multiple Works page to remove yourself as co-creator.
# Try deleting a user who has co-created some works.
