column1: Rewrite FilterTagging and MetaTagging code
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
There are a number of bugs with the current MetaTagging and FilterTagging code. Rather than making the current code more complex to try to fix these bugs, it would be good to rewrite the code to make the MetaTagging and FilterTagging calculations more straightforward. It would also be good to introduce more tools to handle these types of issues in the future.

There are a couple of general issues that need to be addressed in any rewrite, and a few other changes that would also be good to make:

h3. Calling asynchronous functions before the data is committed

Most of the functions that update FilterTaggings access information about tags from the database – such as checking the current merger and whether it's canonical. But most of those asynchronous functions are called in {{before_save}} or {{before_update}} callbacks, which means that if the transaction takes a while to commit, the data won't be available at the time that the asynchronous function runs.

(The worst example of this is {{syn_string=}}, which calls {{async(:add_merger_associations)}}. Thanks to the way that the TagsController is set up, this means that when the asynchronous job is enqueued, the transaction hasn't even *started* yet, much less been committed.)

Unfortunately, the fix for this is more tricky than just making all of the callbacks occur {{after_commit}}, because the asynchronous function calls are based on which fields have changed. If a single tag object is saved more than once in the same transaction, any {{after_commit}} callback will only be able to check the most recent changes. (And if you have multiple copies of the same Tag object floating around, you're not even guaranteed to see the most recent changes, or any changes at all.) You can see an example of this type of issue if you run the following in the console:

{code:ruby}Fandom.last.update(canonical: false)
Tag.after_commit do |record|
  raise "BROKEN" unless record.saved_change_to_canonical?
end
Tag.transaction do
  Fandom.last.touch
  Fandom.last.update(canonical: true)
end{code}

I'm not sure if there are any transactions that result in the same tag being saved and/or touched more than once, but it would be good to prevent that sort of bug from occurring in the future, given how difficult it can be to diagnose.

So instead of changing to {{after_commit}}, a better way to handle this is to use the {{after_commit_everywhere}} gem to ensure that each async call occurs after the data is committed.

h3. Computing changes instead of calculating from scratch

Currently, the computations for FilterTaggings and MetaTaggings are split up into multiple functions. When updating FilterTaggings, there's one function for when a new synonym is added, one for when a synonym is deleted, one for when a meta tag is added, and one for when a meta tag is deleted. There's a similar set up for inherited MetaTaggings: one function for when a direct MetaTagging is added, and one function for when a direct MetaTagging is deleted. Effectively, the current code is all about trying to figure out how the change in the tag should be mapped to a change in the filters and inherited meta tags.

The issue with this occurs when there are multiple changes to the tag in quick succession. When a synonym is unhooked from a canonical, the {{remove_filter_taggings}} function looks up the list of meta tags of the former canonical and checks whether the filters for those meta tags should still be listed on the works tagged with the synonym. However, if one of the meta tags of the former canonical is removed in the time after {{remove_filter_taggings}} is enqueued but before it runs, then it won't delete filters for that meta tag. (This is the cause of AO3-5432.)

In some ways, this the opposite of the first issue. The function {{remove_filter_taggings}} is accessing data that's too new – if it had the list of meta tags at the time that the function was originally enqueued, it would be able to correctly figure out which meta tags to remove. 

In general, in order to make these sorts of sequential changes work properly, you'd need all of the asynchronous functions to run in exactly the right order, and each function would need to store a bunch of information about the state of the tags at the time that it was enqueued. Unfortunately, Resque isn't really built around the idea of having jobs occur in the right order – the whole point of having multiple workers for the same queue is so that more jobs can be run in parallel. And when a job fails, Resque assumes that it can be rerun later, regardless of what that might do to the order. As far as I can tell, these sorts of incremental changes make concurrency issues almost inevitable when using Resque.

A cleaner way to address this is to recompute which MetaTaggings/FilterTaggings should exist from scratch each time. (This is the way that {{ExternalWork#check_filter_taggings}} works, though it's currently a little buggy.) Inherited MetaTaggings can be computed from direct MetaTaggings using a simple breadth-first search. FilterTaggings can be computed from Taggings, Tags, and MetaTaggings. This approach means that there's no danger of breaking the MetaTaggings/FilterTaggings by performing operations in the wrong order. As long as the information retrieved from the database is correct, the MetaTaggings/FilterTaggings will be correct.

This also has the benefit of making it very easy to add tools to help fix issues in the event that something does go wrong. The same code can be used in a rake task to fix all MetaTaggings/FilterTaggings, or in a troubleshooting feature available to admins/tag wranglers.

h3. Other issues to address

*Tools for fixing existing problems.* There are several meta tag trees and a large number of works that have already been affected by these issues. There should be some rake tasks for fixing filters.

*Tools for fixing future problems.* There still could be future issues if the database suffers from replication delays or if the servers crash at an inconvenient time. It would be good to add tools in the admin/tag wrangling interface – like the "Reindex Work" and "Reindex Tag" buttons – to fix the filters for just one tag or just one work, instead of having to run an entire rake task.

*Unify the Work and ExternalWork code.* Currently, Works and ExternalWorks each have their own version of the code for calculating filters. This results in inconsistencies (such as [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5433#icft=AO3-5433|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5433#icft=AO3-5433|smart-link]) and duplicated code. The filter code in those classes should be refactored to DRY it up and reduce inconsistencies.

*Don't reindex bookmarks when wrangling.* The Elasticsearch upgrade moved all filter information into the BookmarkedWorkIndexer. This means that bookmarks don't have any information that would change after wrangling, so there's no need to reindex them when a tag becomes canonical/non-canonical. This results in the current wrangling code doing more work than it needs to.

*Reindex everything when changing the tag name or type.* There is, however, a case where the bookmarks do need to be reindexed: when the name of the tag has changed. That kind of change actually requires a lot of reindexing that's currently not performed.

----

h2. Testing Instructions

This is supposed to be an extensive rewrite of the underpinnings of tag wrangling, so it would be good to have a tag wrangler or two put it through its paces and see whether there's any unexpected behavior.

In addition, there are some specific tests that should probably be run:

h3. Troubleshooting Tests

There will be some new troubleshooting features to make it easier to handle errors when they do occur. These features will need to be tested to make sure that they do what they're supposed to:

(/) *Fix Meta Tags:* (2/2 testers)

# Find a pre-existing tag with incorrect inherited meta tags.
# Alternatively, if you have a tag A that's the subtag of B, which is in turn the subtag of C, you can delete the inherited meta taggings for the tag A by calling:
{code:ruby}tag.meta_taggings.where(direct: false).destroy_all{code}
Note, however, that this won't affect the filters of pre-existing works in the sub tag. If you want a work with broken filters for testing, create a new work with the sub tag.
# Log in as an admin or a tag wrangler.
# Click on the "Troubleshoot" button on the tag show page.
# Check "Fix Meta Tags."
# Press "Troubleshoot."
# Wait 10 minutes, and check to see if the sub tag's works appear in/disappear from the works index of the meta tag. (Or, if you have access to the console, reload the meta tagging list and make sure that it looks right.)

(/) *Fix Tag Filters:* (2/2 testers)

# Find a pre-existing tag with missing filters, or filters that failed to be deleted.
# Alternatively, you can create one in the console by calling:
{code:ruby}tag.direct_filter_taggings.each do |ft|
  ft.destroy
  ft.filterable.enqueue_to_index
end{code}
Note that due to some peculiarities in the way that the Elasticsearch indexing works, a work with missing filters can still show up in the tags if the work is directly tagged with the canonical. So if you're constructing a tag with broken filters, you probably want a tag that has at least one synonym.
# Log in as an admin.
# Visit the tag's show page and click on the "Troubleshoot" button.
# Check "Fix Tag Filters."
# Press "Troubleshoot."
# Wait 10 minutes, and check to see if the work's filters are behaving properly.

(/) *Fix Work Filters:* (2/2 testers)

# Find a pre-existing work with missing filters, or filters that failed to be deleted.
# Alternatively, you can create one in the console by adding a filter tagging with:
{code:ruby}work.filters << tag
work.enqueue_to_index{code}
# Log in as an admin or a tag wrangler.
# Click on the "Troubleshoot" button on the work page.
# Check "Fix Work Filters."
# Press "Troubleshoot."
# Wait 10 minutes, and check to see if the work's filters are behaving properly.

h3. Scaling Tests

Because the new code will recalculate filter taggings each time, it will end up performing some extra work when wrangling. It would be good to make sure that the wrangling time for large tags is acceptable.

(/) *Adding a Synonym:* (2/2 testers)

# Log in as an admin or a tag wrangler.
# Find a fandom tag with at least 10,000 works.
# Set its synonym to a brand new fandom.
# Check back over the next few minutes and/or hours to see how long it takes all of the fandom's works to move over to the new tag name.

(/) *Adding and Removing a Meta Tag:* (2/2 testers)

# Log in as an admin or tag wrangler.
# Find a freeform tag with a large number of subtags, such as "Alternate Universe"
# Add a new meta tag.
# Check back over the next few minutes and/or hours to see how long it takes all of the tag's works to appear in the meta tag's listings.
# Remove the new meta tag.
# See how long it takes all of the tag's works to appear in the meta tag's listings.

(/) *Making C the direct subtag of A instead of the direct subtag of B:* (2/2 testers)

# Pick three canonical tags of the same type, with works under each.
# Wrangle them into a chain, so that A is the metatag of B, and B is the metatag of C.
# Wait until the works of C show up under both B and A to make sure that this worked.
# Edit tag C.
# Check the box to remove B as a metatag.
# Fill in the name of A in the "Add MetaTag" box.
# Press "Save changes."
# Look at the MetaTags section on the edit page to make sure the changes went through.
# View the tag, and check the "Metatags" section to make sure the changes are reflected there.
# Wait about 10-20 minutes.
# Check the works pages for each of the tags to make sure that A has works from all three tags, but B and C each have works only from their own tag.

h3. Work Blurb Tests

(/) *Renaming check:* (2/2 testers)

# Pick a tag and a work in that tag.
# View the work blurb.
# Modify the tag name.
# View the work blurb and ensure it's updated.

(/) *Type change check:* (2/2 testers)

# Pick a tag and a work in that tag.
# View the work blurb.
# Log into the rails console, and modify the type of the tag. You might want to switch it to or from a fandom, so that the type change is obvious.
# View the work blurb and ensure that the tags are displayed correctly.

h3. Included Issues

Ideally, the rewrite should fix all of the following issues:

[https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830#icft=AO3-3830|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830#icft=AO3-3830|smart-link]

Many of these are intermittent, so it's difficult to tell if the bug is fixed or just not appearing at the moment, but it'd be good to try each of them once or twice to make sure that the intermittent issues haven't become worse.

----

h2. Post-deploy

Staging:

* (/) Run migration {{20200423205608_add_unique_index_to_filter_taggings}}.
* (/) After the migration is finished, run task to fix meta tags: {{bundle exec rake Tag:reset_meta_tags}}
* (/) After meta tags are fixed, run task to queue fixes for filters: {{bundle exec rake Tag:reset_filters}}
* (/) After the filter fixes are queued, run task to actually process the {{reindex_world}} queue: {{bundle exec rake search:run_world_index_queue}}. We're done when this queue is empty.

Beta:

* (/) Run migration {{20200423205608_add_unique_index_to_filter_taggings}}.
* (/) After the migration is finished, run task to fix meta tags: {{bundle exec rake Tag:reset_meta_tags}}
* (/) After meta tags are fixed, run task to queue fixes for filters: {{bundle exec rake Tag:reset_filters}}
* (/) After the filter fixes are queued, run task to actually process the {{reindex_world}} queue: {{bundle exec rake search:run_world_index_queue}}. We're done when this queue is empty.

When determining whether to display the "Fandom" sort button, the challenge request summary can end up loading all prompts in the collection: {code:ruby}<% if @show_request_fandom_tags %> <% @collection.prompts.each do |f| %> <% if f.tag_groups.include?("Fandom") %>
  • <%= sort_link ts("Fandom #{@collection.challenge.request_restriction.allowed("fandom")}"), :fandom %>
    • <% break %> <% end %> <% end %> <% end %>{code} [(Source)|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/8f266b291397f9b05996495ad0c6516041342fc1/app/views/challenge/shared/_challenge_requests.html.erb#L8-L15] Even if it breaks out of the loop early – which it likely will in most cases – it still has to retrieve all prompts (including offers, and the full description for each prompt) from the database. It seems likely that this could slow down the requests summary, particularly if the challenge has a lot of prompts. column1: Syntax error when rescuing ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique errors for users
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column147:
13/Apr/20 11:11 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;The switch to Devise means that the {{UsersController}} no longer creates new users, so this is broken in multiple ways now.

It might still be possible to get an {{ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique}} error in the {{UsersController}}, but it would occur when updating the user’s login or the user’s email, and would only happen if someone else created or edited an account to have the same value(s) at exactly the wrong time (which would be much less likely to happen). The code in {{UsersController}} should probably be either deleted, or modified to reflect the fact that the {{ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique}} occurs on different actions now.

If users are still experiencing this error on account creation (are they?), we should probably rescue {{ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique}} in {{Users::RegistrationsController}}, which is where the {{User}} object is created and saved.
column148: 25/May/22 7:42 AM;557058:045245cb-4c5b-4691-b41f-82c2b91416c7;On the question of whether users are still experiencing this on account creation, yes they are (as of a report sent in on May 25, 2022).  The user reported filling in the fields to set up a new account, pressing Create, and getting a 500 error.  When they contacted Support about this, I looked up their info and found they already had an existing account with the same email address from 2017.
column149:
25/May/22 9:33 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;That actually doesn’t sound like the same issue. The code for rescuing {{RecordNotUnique}} is intended to handle cases where the HTTP request for account creation is sent twice in quick succession (either because the user clicks the button twice, or because something went wrong with the first request). This causes the first request to succeed, and the second request to fail with {{RecordNotUnique}} because the Ruby-side validation for a unique username/email didn’t see the account created in the first request. It’s a race condition caused by two near-simultaneous requests to do the same thing, and the {{rescue_from}} block is intended to make the results of the second request match the results of the first request.

But if the Ruby-side validation for a unique username/email didn’t see an account with the exact same email address created _5 years prior_, that’s not a race condition, that’s something else entirely. Did you check with someone in Systems to see if they had more details about the error?
column150:

h4. ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique

Mysql2::Error: Duplicate entry '<EMAIL>' for key 'index_users_on_email'

There’s a dozen of these errors for Users::RegistrationsController#create in the past week, and no other errors for the registrations controller.

If the user entered the exact same email with the exact same case, though, I’m stumped.

(Either way, I think it needs a new issue. I don’t think we want to show a confirmation screen when someone tries to sign up with an email from a 5-year-old account.)

column1: Creator can't edit a gift work if the recipient has deleted their account after refusing the gift
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
# Create an account you don't mind deleting. This will be the gift recipient.
# Log in to a different account.
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required information and enter the user from step 1 as a gift recipient.
# Post the work.
# Log out.
# Log in as the user from step 1.
# Hi, username\! > My Dashboard > Gifts
# Refuse the gift you received.
# Delete your account.
# Log back in as the creator of the gift work.
# Edit the work.

*What should happen*
You should be able to save the changes.

*What actually happens*
When you attempt to save the edits, you get a 500 error. This is because the Gift object still exists. (As a result, if you log in as an admin and view the work, you'll see "Refused As Gift:" displayed in the work meta, but it will be blank.)

Because the Gift is basically useless, we should make sure it gets deleted when the recipient deletes their account.

*Note*
Editing works fine if:

* the gift is accepted instead of refused
* the pseud is deleted instead of the user

column1: When orphan_account is a co-creator on a multi-chapter work, subscription emails are sent when the other co-creator posts a chapter that does not list orphan_account as a creator
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard
# Make sure you are *not* subscribed to your own account (in other words, press "Unsubscribe" if it appears)
# Go to the orphan_account's dashboard
# Press "Subscribe"
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required information
# Check "Add co-creators?"
# Enter "orphan_account (orphan_account)"
# Press "Post Without Preview"
# Have a database admin send subscription notifications (bundle exec rake notifications:deliver_subscriptions) *or* wait for them to send (note that notifications will not be sent for the work you just posted)
# Follow "Add Chapter"
# Fill in required information
# Do *not* add orphan_account as a co-creator on the chapter
# Press "Post Without Preview"
# Have a database admin send subscription notifications (bundle exec rake notifications:deliver_subscriptions) *or* wait for them to send

h1. What happens

You get a subscription email because you are subscribed to orphan_account.

h1. What should happen

In an ideal world where [AO3-3620|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3620] was fixed, getting a subscription email would actually be the desired result! (I _think_. If you're subscribed to User A, who has co-created a work with User B, and User B posts a chapter to that work *without* User A as a co-creator, should you get an email? I assume yes.)

However, assuming we are *not* in that ideal world, following the steps above should result in no email being sent. We like things equally broken.

We mostly want this fixed because people are confused why they’re getting these emails. They always turn out to be subscribed to the orphan_account, but they’re not used to getting emails due to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3620|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3620|smart-link].

h1. Notes

We [check if orphan_account is a co-creator on the creation|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3d47d6e252b6cb69a2bdfb3c58de0ea503a35b6d/app/mailers/user_mailer.rb#L104], but I think we need to check if orphan_account is a co-creator on the *work* in the event the creation is a *chapter*.

Also note this doesn't happen with series – that is, people who are subscribed to orphan_account do not get an email if someone posts a work to a series orphan_account has co-created.

column1: Drop filterable_type column for common_taggings
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When running {{consistency_fail}} to check for uniqueness constraints enforced in the codebase but not backed by the database, one of the results shows a missing index for CommonTaggings:
{code}
CommonTagging        common_taggings (common_tag_id, filterable_id)
{code}
There is, however, a very similar uniqueness constraint that is enforced by the database:
{code}
  add_index "common_taggings", ["common_tag_id", "filterable_type", "filterable_id"], :name => "index_common_tags", :unique => true
{code}
The difference is the {{filterable_type}} column, which is used to allow {{CommonTagging#filterable}} to be polymorphic. However, in practice, {{CommonTagging#filterable}} is always a Tag, so the {{filterable_type}} column serves no practical purpose. It would be nice to get rid of the column entirely, to reflect the fact that the {{CommonTagging}} class is used to define relationships between tags.

Any PR for this issue should handle these things:
# A migration to drop the {{filterable_type}} column for {{common_taggings}}, and if necessary adjust the unique index.
# Updating the {{CommonTagging}} class so that the {{filterable}} association has {{class_name: "Tag"}} instead of {{polymorphic: true}}.
# Updating any associations that are {{through: :common_taggings}}, since switching away from polymorphic means that {{source_type: 'Tag'}} is no longer needed.
# Modifying all other classes so that there are no more references to {{common_taggings.filterable_type}}.

*Testing Instructions:* Any user can check the following:

column1: Allow users to search for works and bookmarks by language short name
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
This issue applies to the following search fields:

* "Work Search" in the header
* "Search within results" in the work filters
* "Any Field" on the work search page
* "Any field on work" on the bookmark search page
* "Search within results" in the bookmark filters

Currently, if you'd like to search by language using any of the above fields, you need to use the syntax {{language_id: 1}}, where the number corresponds to the id of the Language in the database.

To make this more user-friendly, we'd like to make it so you can enter either {{language_id: en}} (where {{en}} is the Language short name) _or_ {{language_id: 1}} to get all English works. (The latter is necessary to avoid breaking bookmarked searches.)

We’ll need to reindex all works so the {{language_id}} field uses the short name. This is necessary to avoid [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5104#icft=AO3-5104|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5104#icft=AO3-5104|smart-link] and allow users to search for works in multiple languages, e.g. {{language_id: en OR language_id: zh}} to get works in either English or Chinese.

Note that if you use the old numerical id ({{language_id: 1}}) in your search, you should see the new short name ({{language_id: en}}) in the search field after performing your search.

*How to test*:

# Check that the language dropdown still works as expected in the bookmark search page and on the bookmark filters.
# Check that the field "Search within results" in work filters work by using the language_id hidden search operator.

# Repeat 3 for "Any Field" on the work search page.
# Repeat 3 for "Any field on work" on the bookmark search page.
# Repeat 3 for "Search within results" in the bookmark filters.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
The {{BulletproofMailer}} class in {{lib/bulletproof_mailer.rb}} was originally introduced to allow emails to be cancelled by calling {{abort_delivery}}, which throws an error and prevents an email from being sent. But [as redsummernight points out|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3591#discussion_r300818589], this workaround is no longer necessary in the current version of Rails.

To modernize the handling of aborted emails and clean up the codebase, it would be nice to make the following changes:
# Update {{UserMailer}} to extend {{ActionMailer::Base}} instead of {{BulletMailer::Base}}.
# Update {{UserMailer#batch_subscription_notification}} to use {{return}} instead of {{abort_delivery}}.
# Delete {{lib/bulletproof_mailer.rb}}.

*Testing Instructions:* We need to make sure that subscription notifications can be cancelled. Specifically:
# Log in as User A.
# Subscribe to User B.
# Log in as User B.
# Post a new work.
# Immediately after posting, edit the work and add it to an Anonymous collection.
# Wait for subscription notifications to be sent, and make sure that User A didn't receive an email.
# Check Resque to make sure that the subscription notification didn't produce a failed job.

column1: Tag Sets: When adding a non-canonical character/relationship and its canonical fandom to the same tag set, don't automatically associate them
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When added to a tag set alongside their (canonical) fandom, non-canonical characters and relationships appear to be nested inside the canonical fandom, not in the "Unassociated Characters & Relationships" section.

But when the tag set is used in a challenge and the “Fandom only?” option is selected, the non-canonical characters and relationships are not actually associated with the fandom:

* The non-canonical characters and relationships do not appear in the autocomplete when the user selects their canonical fandom, which contributes to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3511|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3511|smart-link].
* The non-canonical characters and relationships cannot be used on prompts even if they’re entered by hand (except in cases of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|smart-link]). 

We want to make the display of tag sets consistent with the way that that the challenges handle these non-canonical character and relationship tags – that is, tag sets that contain both a non-canonical character/relationship and its canonical parent fandom should not automatically consider that character/relationship to be associated with the fandom.

In order to prevent older tag sets from suddenly having a lot of missing associations, we’d also like to have a rake task for recreating all of the relevant {{CommonTagging}}s as {{TagSetAssociation}}s.

h1. Testing Instructions

# Pick a non-canonical character/relationship tag that has a canonical fandom associated with this. (You might try looking at synonyms of canonical tags.)
# Pick a canonical character/relationship tag in the same fandom.
# Adding tags to a tag set, and manually associating them:
## Create a new tag set.
## Add all three tags to the tag set: the canonical fandom, the canonical character/relationship, and the non-canonical character/relationship. Save changes.
## View the tag set, and make sure that the canonical character/relationship is nested under the canonical fandom, while the non-canonical character/relationship is under the “Unassociated Characters & Relationships” section.
## Edit the tag set, and under the “Tag Associations” section, add an association between the non-canonical character/relationship and the canonical fandom.
## View the tag set, and make sure that both characters/relationships are now nested under the canonical fandom.
# Nominating tags for a tag set in the canonical fandom:
## Create a tag set, and set the nomination numbers to 1 fandoms, 2 characters/relationships.
## Nominate the canonical character/relationship and the non-canonical character/relationship under the canonical fandom.
## Go to “Review Nominations” for the tag set and approve all three nominations.
## Check that canonical character is nested under the canonical fandom, but the non-canonical character/relationship is listed under “Unassociated Characters & Relationships.”
## Go to “Review Associations” for the tag set and make sure that the association between the non-canonical character/relationship and the canonical fandom is listed there.
# Nominating tags for a tag set in a different fandom:
## Create a tag set, and set the nomination numbers to 2 fandoms, 1 character/relationship.
## Nominate the canonical character/relationship under the canonical fandom.
## Nominate the non-canonical character/relationship under a different fandom (canonical or not).
## Go to “Review Nominations” for the tag set and approve all four nominations.
## Check that the canonical character is nested under the canonical fandom, but the non-canonical character/relationship is listed under “Unassociated Characters & Relationships.”
## Go to “Review Associations” for the tag set and make sure that the association between the non-canonical character/relationship and the new fandom you picked is listed there.
# Checking the rake task: (Already tested ✅)
## Create a tag set.
## Add all three tags to the tag set: the canonical fandom, the canonical character/relationship, and the non-canonical character/relationship. Save changes.
## View the tag set, and make sure that the non-canonical character/relationship is listed in the “Unassociated Characters & Relationships” section, while the canonical character/relationship is listed under the fandom.
## Run the rake task.
## View the tag set again, and make sure that the character/relationship is no longer listed in the “Unassociated Characters & Relationships” section, but is instead listed under the canonical fandom.
## Edit the tag set and scroll down to the “Tag Associations” section to make sure that there is exactly one association there: the one connecting the non-canonical character/relationship to the fandom.

h1. Deploy notes

Run rake task following the testing steps in step 6.

*Steps to Reproduce:*
# Log in.
# Create and post a new work.
# Open the edit form for the work in two windows (or tabs).
# In the first window, set the total chapter count to 2 and press Preview.
# Leave the preview open and switch to the other window.
# Go to Add Chapter, fill in a chapter body, and post.
# Go to Add Chapter, fill in a chapter body, and post.
# Switch back to the window previewing the work with chapter count 2 and press Update.
# Note that your chapter count is listed as 3/2.

Normally the expected number of chapters is set through the {{wip_length}}, which overrides the expected chapter count and sets it to {{?}} if the user tries to set the expected count lower than the actual count. But the hidden field on the preview page uses {{expected_number_of_chapters}} instead of {{wip_length}}, and {{expected_number_of_chapters}} has no safeguards.

column1: Links to chapter end notes should always link to the same page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
# Post a work.
# Add a chapter with chapter notes at the end; after posting, you are redirected to the new chapter 2.
# Follow "Entire Work".
# Under chapter 2, follow the link in "(See the end of the chapter for notes.)"

*What happens*
You arrive at chapter 2's end notes, but on the chapter 2 page, not on the entire work page.

*What should happen*
You arrive at chapter 2's end notes on the entire work page.

*Notes*
There can be even more weirdness depending on whether the user has the "Show the whole work by default" preference set.

The easiest way to fix this is to make the chapter end notes links [contain only the fragments and not the full paths|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/9461903/generate-link-to-without-path-only-anchor].

Since chapter contents are cached, we need to bump [the version of the cache key|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/854a4926c67c0419b10b1a4fe2165d8ccb8e9d87/app/views/chapters/_chapter.html.erb#L14].

column1: Possible to create a tag with no name using Hangul filler characters
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
It’s possible to create a tag using spaces, e.g. the fandom tag https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/%E3%85%A4 on [this work|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1070027], which consists solely of the [Hangul filler Unicode character|https://unicodelookup.com/#%E3%85%A4/1]. You can try copying the character here: {{ㅤ}}. (There is also a [halfwidth Hangul filler character|https://www.compart.com/en/unicode/U+FFA0] you can do this with. I am not sure if the bug is the same with the Hangul Choseong filler and/or the Hangul Jungseong filler.)

h2. Notes

For future reference, a way to figure out what a character is based on the encoded URL:

* Paste the encoded URL into [this decoder|https://meyerweb.com/eric/tools/dencoder/] and press “Decode”
* Copy and paste the character into the search bar on [Unicode Lookup|https://unicodelookup.com]

h2. Update

Upon further investigation, this appears to be a font issue. The character displays as a blank space in some fonts, e.g. the one used in the work meta (the dots are just the bottom border styling on tag links), but as a visible character in others, e.g. the one on the blurb:

!character_as_space (15eaca4e-3986-4d81-af6c-98d22e109ebf).png|width=500!

!character_visible (5a152245-965c-4736-b8de-63d23f0cedea).png|width=500!

Both screenshots are from macOS; on iOS, which has different fonts, both instances of the tag appear as spaces.

column1: User.orphan_account fails to create the user on a new database
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
On a new database, we attempt to create the orphan_account user if doesn't exist.

https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/854a4926c67c0419b10b1a4fe2165d8ccb8e9d87/app/models/user.rb#L547-L553

This fails because the new user is missing a host of required information (email, password, age check, TOS check), which means in tests we need the extra step of faking orphan_account, e.g. for Cucumber tests:

https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/854a4926c67c0419b10b1a4fe2165d8ccb8e9d87/features/step_definitions/user_steps.rb#L11-L14

(This is not a problem on production or staging, which already has the orphan_account user.

*Possible fix*: orphan_account doesn't actually need to be valid, so we could just skip validations when creating it. Then we can remove the extra setup steps in tests.
{code:ruby}
orphan_account = User.find_or_initialize_by(login: "orphan_account")
orphan_account.save(validate: false)
{code}

*How to test*: check if we can still orphan works.

I don't have a JIRA account so here are my notes:

News posts and FAQs work great (yay\! \\o/). The {{blockquote}} tag automatically adds the line to the right side of the text, and if I change it to {{blockquote dir="ltr"}} it aligns the text to the left and moves the line to be on the left side of the text.

Works are where things aren't working smoothly. What I did was copy a work in Hebrew into the rich text editor and add a blockquote to some part of it using the quote button. It appears okay on the editor itself (I'll attach pics), but when posting the line is on the left side of the text (though the text is indeed indented on the right side). In order for the line to be on the right side, I need to go to the HTML editor and manually add {{dir="rtl"}} to the {{blockquoate}} tag. I will note that when the text of the blockquote is highlighted in the rich text editor, the direction button of the editor does recognize the text as RTL. It just doesn't add the direction attribute to the tag.

(Also tested English text inside the work, and for English everything is okay at the moment)

Pics following

What the RTE shows

*Overview*

If you post a work that is inspired by another work on the Archive, and that inspiring work is deleted, it will be removed from your Related Works page... but the count in the dashboard will not go down and the RelatedWork object will continue to exist in the database.

*Steps to reproduce*

# First, create a work (the parent work) that will be listed as the inspiration for another work
## Log in as User A
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required information
## Press "Post Without Preview"
## Note the URL of this work
## Log out as User A
# Now create a work that will cite the previous as its inspiration
## Log in as User B 
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required inform
## Check "This work is a remix, a translation, a podfic, or was inspired by another work"
## Paste the URL of the parent work in the "URL" field
## Press "Post Without Preview"
## Hi, username! > My Dashboard
## Make note of how many Related Works your dashboard sidebar says you have
## Log out
# Delete the parent work
## Log in as User A
## Go to the work you posted
## Edit > Delete Work
## Confirm that you want to delete said work

*What should happen*

User B's Related Work count should decrease by 1.

*What happens instead*

The count does not decrease by 1. It stays the same.

*Notes*

Work B is (correctly) no longer listed on your Related Works page; it's just the count in the sidebar that is wrong. We should probably make sure we delete the {{RelatedWork}} object because it doesn't serve much purpose once the deleted item is gone.

Also note that that the edit page for Work B no longer shows the related work, so it can’t be fixed by the user. A database admin needs to delete the {{RelatedWork}} to fix the count.

column1: Gift Exchange: Simultaneously updating the Giver and Write-in Giver for a Potential Assignment breaks anonymity by causing the Giver's name to appear on the Write-In Giver's My Assignments page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps to reproduce*

# Log in
# Create a collection with a gift exchange challenge
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required information and choose "Gift Exchange" for "Type of challenge, if any"
## Submit
## On the exchange settings form, check "Sign-up open?"
## Submit
# Sign up for the exchange as three different users (it’s easiest if one of them is the collection owner)
## Follow the "Sign-up Form" link in the collection sidebar
## Since we accepted the default settings, we don't even need to fill anything in – just press "Submit"
# If you're not already logged in as the collection owner, log back in with that account
# Run matching
## On your collection's sidebar, follow  the "Challenge Settings" link
## Uncheck "Sign-up open?"
## Press "Update"
## From the sidebar, follow the "Matching" link
## Press "Generate Potential Matches"
## You'll get a pop-up warning you matches will be random; choose "OK"
## Wait briefly for matching to finish and refresh the page to see potential matches
# Copy each name from the Giver field into the Write-In Giver field in the next column
# Use the red *×* to clear each Giver
# Replace the original Giver with the _other_ collection participant who is neither the Write-In Giver nor the Recipient
# Press “Save Assignment Changes”
# Press “Send Assignments”

*What happens*

When a participant follows the "My Assignments" link on the collection dashboard, they will find two assignments: theirs and someone else's. 

The someone else's is actually their pinch-hit, but it displays the actual assignee's name.

*What should happen*

It should display "their_name* (pinch hitter)".

*Notes*

While just fixing the name that displays is an okay fix for now, the problem is deeper.

When the challenge moderator fills in both the Giver and Write-In Giver fields as described, the ChallengeAssignment objects all end up with both an offer_signup_id and a pinch_hitter_id. 

This means that if the Write-In Giver (pinch-hitter) goes to fill the assignment, the assignment does not get marked as fulfilled on their assignments page (or, indeed, on the moderator’s view of assignments).

Usually, when a mod assigns a pinch-hitter through other means, a brand new ChallengeAssignment is created with a pinch_hitter_id (rather than adding a pinch_hitter_id to the existing ChallengeAssignment).

Ideally, we should fix this issue with the ChallengeAssignment, but in the meantime, we should at least make sure the write-in giver (pinch-hitter) doesn’t see the actual assignee’s name (and email due to AO3-5733).

column1: Floating comment box in Inbox jumps to bottom of page when focusing the textarea in Chrome
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
This issue is limited to the latest version of Desktop Chrome (v77, as of writing), it's not a change on our part, we think it's a change to Chrome's layout rendering engine.

*Steps to replicate*

# Log in and go to your inbox
# Make sure you have some comments in your Inbox
# Click the "Reply" button to a comment
# The floating comment box appears, click into the textarea

*What happens*

* The box disappears from view, and will reappear depending on where you move your cursor, but trying to interact with any of the form fields will make it disappear again.
* You will find the comment box when you scroll all the way to the bottom of the page, that's where it will stay even if you interact with it.
* When you click "Reply" to make the box first show up, and click into the textarea, the box disappears, but you have put focus on the textarea. If you start typing, even though you don't see the box, the browser will jump to the bottom of the page to the textarea so that you can see what you're typing.
* When you click "Reply" to make the box first show up, then drag the box, that will ensure it stays put.

*What should happen*
The box should stay at the position where it was first initiated, even when focusing form elements inside of it.

*Notes*
One current theory is that this jumping happens because the box is created inside a container that is absolute positioned but doesn't have a top/right/bottom/left value applied. Once you set a top/left value by dragging the box, it will stay positioned there.

The floating box is used in two other places, the issue doesn't occur there. For the bookmarks form, because the top/left value is overwritten. For the comment box on the "Unread Messages" section on the homepage, because it gets rendered at the bottom of the container anyway (aka the place where it would jump to).

column1: Upgrade to Rails 5.2
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
In order to stay current with Rails, we want to upgrade to Rails 5.2. A lot of the work here involves upgrades to associated gems and fixes for deprecated features that will be removed in Rails 6.

Upgrading to the most recent version of Rails 5.2 (later than 5.2.4.3) will fix the following vulnerabilities:

* [CVE-2020-5267|https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rubyonrails-security/55reWMM_Pg8]: Possible XSS vulnerability in ActionView; we can remove the monkey-patch added in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5898|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5898|smart-link]
* [CVE-2020-8165|https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rubyonrails-security/bv6fW4S0Y1c]: Potentially unintended unmarshalling of user-provided objects in MemCacheStore and RedisCacheStore
* [CVE-2020-8167|https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rubyonrails-security/x9DixQDG9a0]: CSRF Vulnerability in rails-ujs
* [CVE-2020-8164|https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rubyonrails-security/f6ioe4sdpbY]: Possible Strong Parameters Bypass in ActionPack
* [CVE-2020-8166|https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rubyonrails-security/NOjKiGeXUgw]: Ability to forge per-form CSRF tokens given a global CSRF token
* [CVE-2020-15169|https://groups.google.com/g/rubyonrails-security/c/b-C9kSGXYrc]: Potential Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Action View’s translation helpers.

Testing a significant Rails upgrade usually involves a full regression.

*Deploy notes*

We will need to completely clear the cache ({{Rails.cache.clear}}) because 5.1 and 5.2 caches are incompatible (https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/34853).

* work share code

* comment links in work blurbs - make sure the URL has {{?view_full_work=true}} if there’s more than one chapter (and doesn’t have it if there’s only one chapter)

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Our current method for updating public site skins is "comment on the issue with the changes."

This is a bad system for a number of reasons.

We want to put the CSS for the three public site skins we support (Reversi, Snow Blue, and Low Vision Default) in the repository. This will let us open pull requests and track changes.

Note that the changes will still need to be copied to production by an admin to actually become live, but at least we'll have readable diffs for reviewing and a history of the changes in case something breaks.

h1. Steps to reproduce
# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required fields, and in your work text, include a rather large image
# Post
# On a screen that is not as big as your image, view the work

h1. What happens
The image is too wide to fit on the screen. It scrolls sideways. Meh.

h1. What should happen instead
The image should have a maximum width of 100% of the container size. (Note that the container isn't the same width as the screen.

h1. Notes
This needs an announcement first, which is in progress.

h1. Testing notes
Test on images that have width and height attributes set, just width, and just height.

This will apply to any user- (or admin-) inserted images, so it wouldn't hurt to test large images in comments or admin posts as well.

column147:
19/Oct/19 6:45 PM;557058:bb48f715-7c87-43a5-81b8-a60c77a4c45b;I’ve opened a WIP PR here: [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3661|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3661|smart-link] 


The intent is that a new developer could:

# Install git + docker (and nothing else)
# Clone the repo
# Setup some config files (database.yml, local.yml, redis.yml)
# Run some init commands (or a single script)
# Have the app running locally



Some questions/observations so far:

* Some documentation needs to accompany the docker bits.  I think the wiki makes sense to hold it (analogous to the Vagrant section).  Is the wiki open for public editing?
* Gem mysql2 needs to be upgraded to 0.5.2 (latest) otherwise server crashes on startup with error “uninitialized constant Mysql2::Client::LONG_PASSWORD“.  This probably deserves to be in its own PR.
* [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/config/environments/development.rb#L9|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/config/environments/development.rb#L9|smart-link] is forcing localhost for memcache location in development mode which won’t work in a docker-compose environment.  I replaced with local.yml lookup, but I think it should probably default to localhost if not defined.  This might also warrant its own PR.
* Tests currently don’t work within the container.  I did not investigate this thoroughly yet, but based on the error output, my theory is the tests expect redis at localhost (which is not the case with docker-compose).

column1: Add options for prefers-color-scheme media queries when making site skins
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
{{prefers-color-scheme}} media queries allow you to set CSS that is only applied if you are using your device's dark or light color theme option: [https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-color-scheme|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-color-scheme]

In the Advanced section of the skins form, we should add two checkboxes to the @media section: one for prefers-color-scheme: dark and one for prefers-color-scheme: light.

High priority because this provides users a way to make Android’s automatically-generated dark color theme a bit less unpleasant.

h1. Testing

First, ensure that the checkboxes are there.

Second, make sure they work. For example, you might want to paste in the CSS from Reversi, check the option for prefers-color-scheme: dark, and apply the skin. If you switch your device to dark mode, Reversi should be applied.

Third, make sure they work when combined with _other_ media queries. So you might want to do the steps above _and_ also check the media query for max-width: 42em. If you do that, you should see Reversi applied when the device is in dark mode or when the screen/browser window is narrow. (Our media queries are set up to behave as “or” not “and” at the moment.)

column1: Update Sanitize gem to resolve issue with invalid closing tags on track and source elements
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When using the {{<track>}} and {{<source>}} elements inside an {{<audio>}} or {{<video>}} element, closing {{</track>}} and {{</source>}} tags are automatically added. Furthermore, the closing tag {{</embed>}} for {{<embed>}} is also automatically added. Updating the Sanitize gem appears to fix this, so let's do that!

h2. What happens

Example input into the Work Text field in HTML mode:

{code:html}<video>
<source src="some url" type="video/mp4">
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url">
</video>

<audio>
<source src="some url" type="audio/mp3">
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url">
</audio>

<embed type="application/x-shockwave-flash" src="http://www.google.com/reader/ui/123-audio-player.swf">{code}

Example output:

{code:html}<video>
<source src="some url" type="video/mp4"></source>
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url"></track>
</video>

<audio>
<source src="some url" type="audio/mp3"></source>
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url"></track>
</audio>

<embed type="application/x-shockwave-flash" src="http://www.google.com/reader/ui/123-audio-player.swf"></embed>{code}

However, if you run the resultant code through the W3 Validator, it gives a "Stray end tags" error about {{</track>}}, {{</source>}} and {{</embed>}}.

h2. What should happen

So the desired output would be:

{code:html}<video>
<source src="some url" type="video/mp4">
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url">
</video>

<audio>
<source src="some url" type="audio/mp3">
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url">
</audio>

<embed type="application/x-shockwave-flash" src="http://www.google.com/reader/ui/123-audio-player.swf">{code}



In addition to testing the above, please also do all tests on [https://wiki.transformativeworks.org/mediawiki/HTML_Tag_Regression|https://wiki.transformativeworks.org/mediawiki/HTML_Tag_Regression]. The file attached to this issue does not have to be tested.

column1: Gift Exchange: Possible for assignment generation to create multiple assignments for a single user
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. The problem

sarken Oct 7th at 19:58
I'm doing a smoke test of gift exchanges following the Ruby update and I wanted to double check that this is normal. I ran matching (set to random) on an exchange, and the generated assignments included two for the same giver/recipient combo.

!multiple_assignments.png|width=200,height=183!

ticking instant (AO3 Contributor) 23:26
That definitely shouldn't happen. There are a whole bunch of checks to try to make sure that no one has more than one assignment (either as a recipient or a giver). (edited) 

The ChallengeSignup fields assigned_as_request and assigned_as_offer are supposed to be set whenever an assignment is created, and there are a lot of lines of the form next if request_signup.assigned_as_request and similar.

ticking instant (AO3 Contributor) 23:40
(That said, there's a chance that it might not be caused by the Ruby update, since I think stale data could also produce behavior like that. Have you checked that variable for measuring replication health recently? I just searched chat and I think the command was SHOW STATUS LIKE 'wsrep_local_recv_queue_avg';.)

ticking instant (AO3 Contributor) 17:13
It might be a matter of degree, if it is stale data. There were issues before where the assigned_as_request value was available when the assignment was not, because they were committed in different transactions. This issue would arise if the new value of assigned_as_request and the new assignment were unavailable. So if wsrep_local_recv_queue_avg has been trending upwards, this might be the next stage of it: accidentally double-assigning users.

(In theory, it could manifest as two different assignments for the same user, as well.)

ticking instant (AO3 Contributor) 22:41
A couple years back, I was playing around with rewriting the assignment generation code to (a) try to reduce the number of database queries, and (b) return a maximum matching instead of a maximal matching. One of the side effects of having fewer queries is that it ought to be less susceptible to stale data issues. I can try to dust off the code, if you'd like.

*tl;dr:* Sometimes one user gets multiple assignments in a gift exchange.

h1. Testing

This is a stale data issue, so it's not reproducible at will. Create a gift exchange, get multiple sign-ups, run matching, and ensure everything looks normal and there are no instances of duplicate assignments. Repeat a few times.

column27:
For support tickets, we currently have an "approved" column that saves whether the ticket has been marked as ham (true) or spam (false). We don't do this for abuse reports, and there's no real reason to do it here. We can just run the report through the spam checker and send or reject it based on the results without saving said results to the database.

*How to test the Support form*: make sure you can still send a Support ticket. Also try sending one with the email field set to akismet-guaranteed-spam@example.com, and make sure that ticket still gets rejected as spam.

*How to test the migration*:
1. Run the migration.
2. Copy the commands that it prints to a file.
3. Run the pt-online-schema-change command (but no SQL commands).
4. Submit a new support request.
5. Count the number of rows in feedbacks.
6. Run the SQL commands to swap the tables and drop the old table.
7. Count the number of rows in feedbacks, and make sure it's the same as before.
8. Double-check to make sure that the approved column has been dropped.

After much sobbing of blood and gnashing of teeth, we have determined the actual issues folks are reporting following the TinyMCE upgrade\!

*Spellcheck doesn't work:* 

Although words are underlined with red squiggles in some browsers (others aren't getting squiggles), you cannot right click on the underlined word to see and/or accept the browser's suggestions. If you right click, you only get TinyMCE's context menu.

Additionally, the default Safari context menu includes a spellcheck option when right clicking on text. TinyMCE's context menu does not contain that option, ergo it is missing.

*Paste option is missing/not working:* 

Baffling\! Right clicking in the previous RTE never provided a paste option. But sure, let's add the useless Paste option to TinyMCE's context menu, since at least that will tell people to use the keyboard shortcuts.

Yeah, well. Turns out if you right clicked on a _word_, it provided the option to paste.

So\! We're going to disable TinyMCE's godforsaken context menu (the next version enabled it by default) and all the normal browser behavior should be back.

column1: Allow skipping Codeship tests using commit messages
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Occasionally we find ourselves needing to deploy to staging quickly, and we know the pending changes are covered by any part of the test suite, so we don't really want to wait a few hours for Codeship to run all the tests (e.g. RTE changes). Codeship lets you [skip builds|https://documentation.codeship.com/general/projects/skipping-builds/] by including {{\[skip ci]}} in the commit message, but that will skip the staging deploy as well.

We can update the Codeship scripts to skip just the setup and test pipelines when the commit message contains {{\[skip codeship tests]}}.

Along the way, some QoL updates:

- Skip installing Redis 3.2.1, as Codeship's version is now later (4.0.9).
- Skip installing MySQL 5.7.22, as Codeship's version is now later (5.7.27).
- Use Codeship's script for [installing and starting Elasticsearch|https://documentation.codeship.com/basic/services/elasticsearch/].
- Remove code for resetting coverage in the retry script, as we no longer generate coverage on Codeship.
- Generate just the test database using {{rake db:create}} instead of {{rake db:create:all}}.
- Split up {{prepare_codeship.sh}}. This script is run twice (once for specs, once for features) but most of it only needs to be run once (installing dependencies etc.).
- Remove unused things from the script directory.

In embed_sanitizer.rb, I added a method to allow the new {{allow}} attribute on embeds from YouTube:

{code:ruby}def optional_iframe_attributes
  if source == :youtube
    %w[allow]
  else
    []
  end
end{code}

And I of course updated {{sanitize_embed}} to include that:

{code:ruby}def sanitize_embed
  Sanitize.clean_node!(
    node,
    elements: %w[embed iframe],
    attributes: {
      'embed' => %w[
        allowfullscreen height src type width
      ] + optional_embed_attributes,
      'iframe' => %w[
        allowfullscreen frameborder height src title
        class type width
      ] + optional_iframe_attributes
    }
  )

  if node_name == 'embed'
    disable_scripts(node)
    node['flashvars'] = "" unless allows_flashvars?
  end
  { node_whitelist: [node, parent] }
end{code}

And I threw in an automated test, which was passing, so I assumed all was great:

{code:ruby}it "keeps allow attribute on youtube embeds" do
  html = '<iframe src="<https://www.youtube.com/embed/yPQfcG-eimk"> allow="accelerometer; autoplay; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"></iframe>'
  result = sanitize_value(field, html)
  expect(result).to include(html)
end{code}

But when I actually gave the code a whirl on my development environment, I still got a “Video unavailable” error even when all of the HTML was present and accounted for. 😭 The only difference between what I pasted (the code from this issue) and the output was the {{allowfullscreen}} attribute was written as {{allowfullscreen=""}} in the sanitized version:

{code:html}<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/yPQfcG-eimk" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen=""></iframe>{code}

ETA: The exact code, with or without the{{=""}} works on Dreamwidth, so maybe it has to do with my dev environment being insecure?

ETA 2: Disabling cross-origin restrictions in Safari shows that is indeed the source of the problem. (h/t to bingeling\!) I’ve pushed the changes but I suspect we might want to whitelist certain values for {{allow}} so I haven’t submitted a pull request yet. [Here is a list of possibilities.|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Feature-Policy#Directives] If anyone wants to figure out what we need, feel free to grab my branch and start from there.

column151:
14/Dec/19 1:48 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;*redsummernight* 04:21

I think I cracked it

it's not the allow attribute, it's our new Referrer-Policy from [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5632|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5632|smart-link] 

we set it to "same-origin" meaning we don't tell YT "this is from AO3"; some videos have embedding restrictions (whitelist or blacklist certain domains), so they won't play if no referrer is set, to be on the safe side

doesn't matter how old a video is

the quickest fix is to add {{referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"}} to YT's iframes; not sure if that's the best referrerpolicy option, and not sure if editing every iframe element is a good idea or if there's a more global site setting we should use

but it's a start

column27:
This action labels PRs based on the paths that are modified in the PR:
[https://github.com/actions/labeler/blob/master/README.md|https://github.com/actions/labeler/blob/master/README.md]

While it cannot use labels that depend on a PR's review status ("Reviewed: Action Needed") or priority, it can help us with:

* Awaiting Review (all incoming PRs)
* Gem Updates (touching Gemfile, Gemfile.lock)
* Has Migrations (touching db/migrate)

If there are false matches (e.g. we do edit those files, but only comments) we can always manually edit out the wrong labels.

These two labels are only possible with [exclusion matching|https://github.com/actions/labeler/issues/9]:

* Scope: i18n Only (touching config/locales and nothing else)
* Scope: Tests Only (touching only test/, features/, factories/, spec/ and nothing else)

column1: Fix inconsistencies in "Series Updated" dates
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
The "Series Updated" date ({{series.revised_at}}, used on series blurbs and for the "Date Updated" sort option on bookmark searches) is defined as:

* {{max(revised_at)}} of any visible works; visible = unhidden + posted + (if logged out) unrestricted
* {{series.updated_at}} (when the series's summary/title was last updated), if no works are visible

As of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6304|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6304|smart-link], we now index two versions of certain fields – one for logged in users and one for guests. We can do the same for {{updated_at}} and {{revised_at}}.

We should still keep {{series.updated_at}} as the fallback for the case where all works in a series are drafts (unposted) or hidden.

*How to test*: Check that on a bookmark search/listing, sorted by "Date Updated":

* Adding a new work to a series will bump the series to the top of the list (either logged in or not).
* Adding a new restricted work to a series will make the series restricted and also bump it to the top of the list.
* Editing the title of an old series will not bump it to the top of the list (either logged in or not).
* Editing the title of an old series with all works restricted will not bump it to the top of the list.

*Note*: We will need to reindex all bookmarked series. Add a new task in [search.rake|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/lib/tasks/search.rake] to do just this:

{code:ruby}BookmarkedSeriesIndexer.index_from_db{code}

(there is already a task to reindex all bookmarkables, but that would be overkill in this case)
column147:
21/Apr/21 9:33 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;{quote}a series is restricted if any work in it is restricted, and logged out users just don't see restricted series at all{quote}

Isn’t that the opposite of how it works? [The comment on the computation|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/app/models/series.rb#L131-L132] says that a series becomes unrestricted if any work in the series is unrestricted. (So a series is only restricted if all works in the series are restricted.)
column148:
09/Apr/22 4:42 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;{quote}Isn’t that the opposite of how it works?{quote}

Yeah, good catch. I’ll remove the second reason.
column149:
02/Dec/22 2:08 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;{quote}{{max(updated_at)}} of any visible works; visible = unhidden + posted + (if logged out) unrestricted{quote}

This seems like something we should change – using the {{updated_at}}, I mean. That changes if you edit anything about the work, e.g., the title or the restricted status, and it’s causing quite a few tickets.

What’s happening is a lot of users are locking down their works due to speculation about content scraping. When they lock their works, which changes the {{updated_at}} on the works, any bookmarks of series containing the works rise to the top of people’s bookmark pages. Support’s getting some complaints/questions about that behavior, which _does_ seem pretty undesirable.

Should we be using the works' {{revised_at}} instead? What are we hoping to accomplish using the {{updated_at}}?
column150:
02/Dec/22 5:29 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;It does use the works' {{revised_at}}, but it falls back to using the series' {{updated_at}} if none of the works are visible (which is the case for a fully-restricted series, because the indexer is treated like a logged-out user when it comes to dates).

And restricting all works in a series will update the {{updated_at}} for a series, because it changes the value of {{restricted}} for the series.

EDIT: I edited the issue text to say {{revised_at}} instead of {{updated_at}}, since it seems to be the cause of some confusion.

I’m not sure if we want to fix that in a separate issue or here, but I suspect the fix should involve making {{/users/username/series}} come from Elasticsearch.

column1: Make cache expiration in work and bookmark controllers configurable
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We want to use an {{ArchiveConfig}} variable where we set the cache expiration on the [latest works page|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/50f7b7e2c7c78aad7b2e5651f379cf52c28061cf/app/controllers/works_controller.rb#L125], the [latest bookmarks page|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/50f7b7e2c7c78aad7b2e5651f379cf52c28061cf/app/controllers/bookmarks_controller.rb#L137], and [certain work indexes|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/50f7b7e2c7c78aad7b2e5651f379cf52c28061cf/app/controllers/works_controller.rb#L103]. We’ll initially set the value to 30 minutes.

It’s important to note that the caching only applies to those certain work indexes if they are _un-updated_. Posting, deleting, or adding a chapter to those indexes will expire the cache, so logged in users will see the pages updated fairly quickly. Due to full page caching, logged _out_ users will not see updates for 40 minutes.

Because we are not touching the cache expiration code, we can only do limited testing of this.

*How to test*:

First, it is important to note the “Turn on caching (currently experimental)” admin setting is *enabled*.

For the latest works page:

* Log in
* Go to the latest works page at [https://test.ao3.org/works|https://test.ao3.org/works] to ensure it gets placed in the cache
* Post a work
* Refresh the latest works page and confirm the new work hasn’t appeared
* Wait 30 minutes
* Refresh the latest works page and confirm the new work has appeared

For the latest bookmarks page:

* Log in
* Go to the latest bookmarks page at [https://test.ao3.org/bookmarks|https://test.ao3.org/bookmarks] to ensure it gets placed in the cache
* Bookmark a work
* Refresh the latest bookmarks page and confirm the new bookmark hasn’t appeared
* Wait 30 minutes
* Refresh the latest bookmarks page and confirm the new work has appeared

For the work indexes:

* Go to a work index for a tag (e.g. https://test.ao3.org/tags/No%20Archive%20Warnings%20Apply/works), collection (e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/anonymous/works|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/anonymous/works]), pseud (e.g. https://test.ao3.org/users/testy/pseuds/testy/works), or user (e.g. [https://test.ao3.org/users/testy/works|https://test.ao3.org/users/testy/works]) and ensure the page loads

22/Jan/20 3:55 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;The reason that {{redirect_back_or_default}} doesn’t work here is because there’s no {{skip_before_action :store_location}} in the skins controller. That means that any calls to {{redirect_back_or_default}} will redirect back to the current URL (which is the one most recently stored with {{store_location}}), instead of to the referrer.

This means that the {{#set}} and {{#unset}} actions are actually visited twice any time you use the skin chooser. The first time stores its own path in {{session[:return_to]}}, then redirects “back” to that same path and sets {{session[:return_to] = "redirected"}}. The second time sees that it was redirected from the value of {{session[:return_to]}}, so it clears {{session[:return_to]}} in {{store_location}} instead of setting it, resulting in {{redirect_back_or_default}} falling back on the default.

column1: Add task to fill in user IDs for existing logged in kudos
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We need a Rake task that will iterate through all existing logged in kudos and fill in the empty user ID column. Note:

- The task should not touch guest kudos (have IPs but no pseud IDs).
- The task should not touch orphaned kudos (from deleted accounts: no pseud IDs, no IPs). We don't know what user ID to use anyway.
- The task should account for pseud IDs that no longer exist. We don't have foreign key constraints here so this is possible. Don't bother scrubbing the leftover pseud ID, as we'll remove that column in the end.
- The task should process kudos in batches and sensibly print its progress... it's a pretty big table.

*How to test*: this will be mostly on Rake specs. Admins should run this on staging (but after AO3-5850 gets to staging). Check that the number of kudos without user IDs go down, and that the remaining ones are indeed either guest or orphaned.

On beta, similarly this task should be run after AO3-5850 is also deployed.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Save the challenge settings.
# Sign up for your own gift exchange.
# Go to "Sign-ups (1)" in the sidebar.
# Click "Download (CSV)".

*What Should Happen:* You should be able to download a CSV file with your sign-up in it.

*What Actually Happens:* An error.

*Notes:* Prompts accept nested attributes for their tag sets. So if there are any fields on the sign-up form related to the tag set, even if those fields are left blank, the tag set will be created. When that happens, the CSV download hits an error on this line:
{code:ruby}
    tags = request.nil? ? [] : request.tag_set.tags.map {|tag| tag.name}
{code}

column1: GDPR script get_user_data.rb doesn't include some changes from the Devise upgrade
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When the sign-in system was moved to Devise, there were [five fields added to the users|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/7d30bf818a7ab3de6a259acfbc481c68ac3325ff/db/migrate/20181017032400_moves_users_to_devise.rb#L25-L29] table that are updated whenever the user signs in:

* {{sign_in_count}}
* {{current_sign_in_at}}
* {{last_sign_in_at}}
* {{current_sign_in_ip}}
* {{last_sign_in_ip}}

The IP addresses recorded in the audits table whenever one of those five values is updated (as well as the IPs in two of those fields) are not included in the script used to export the user's data.

There are a few more changes resulting from the Devise upgrade that aren't accounted for in the {{script/get_user_data.rb}} script:

# The field {{failed_login_count}} was renamed to {{failed_attempts}}. (But it may not be necessary to check {{failed_attempts}}, because Devise almost exclusively uses {{increment_counter}} to change {{failed_attempts}}, which doesn't call the {{before_update}} hook that the audited gem uses. Still, it might be good to double-check what gets added to the audits table when a failed login attempt occurs, when an account is locked, and when it's unlocked.)
# The field {{recently_reset}} is no longer used. Instead, Devise changes {{reset_password_token}}, {{reset_password_sent_at}}, and {{encrypted_password}} over the course of a password reset. (It may be necessary to leave in the code relating to {{recently_reset}} to account for older entries in the audits table, but I believe there needs to be new code for the new Devise fields regardless.)

The Devise upgrade also renamed various fields related to account activation (which is another activity that probably has the user's IP address associated with it).

----

After reviewing the above information, here are the changes needed:

* Add {{encrypted_password}} case to handle IPs recorded when someone changes their password.
* Add {{failed_attempts}} case to handle recorded IPs from failed login attempts, which are currently only logged in certain cases due to the way Devise updates the count of failed attempts.
* Add {{locked_at}} case to handle recorded IPs from the last failed login attempt before an account is locked due to too many login attempts.
* Clarify that the {{recently_reset}} case is from before the Devise change, and add a {{reset_password_sent_at}} case to handle IPs recorded for password reset requests now that we're using Devise.
* Add {{sign_in_count}} case to handle IPs recorded when someone successfully signs in to an account.

Ideally, to test this, someone would do each of the following with different IP addresses, and then we’d ensure each of those IP address appeared when a database admin ran the script:

* log in and change their account password
* log out and request a password reset
* attempt to log in to their account so many times they get locked out (50 tries, quickly)
* wait five minutes after being locked out and then log in successfully

Failing that, we should make sure the script works.

column27: *To replicate:* # Navigate to any canonical tag # Copy the link into an RSS reader # Open the reader # Select a creator's name *What happens:* The link takes you to {{href="/users/USERNAME/pseuds/PSEUD"}} *What should happen:* The link should take you to {{href="https://archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/pseuds/PSEUD"}} *Notes:* redsummernight found [some documentation on Atom|https://validator.w3.org/feed/docs/atom.html#recommendedEntryElements] and we’re doing authors wrong. {{/o\}} (That doesn’t mention the ability to have a {{uri}} for entry authors, only feed authors, but[ the second example here|https://validator.w3.org/feed/docs/rfc4287.html#rfc.section.1.1] shows you can). So wrong, apparently, that [The Old Reader|https://theoldreader.com/home] doesn’t even try to make the entry’s author names into hyperlinks, so YMMV when it comes to the bug’s exact behavior. {code:ruby} @works.each do |work| unless work.unrevealed? feed.entry work do |entry| entry.title work.title entry.summary feed_summary(work), :type => 'html' entry.author do |author| author.name text_byline(work, :visibility => 'public') end end end end{code} That is our current code, which is stuffing HTML for all of the authors into a single {{author}} element’s {{name}} element, like so: {code:xml} testy, testy2 {code} (Why is {{text_byline}} giving us HTML? Because {{text_byline}} is currently broken. It’s getting fixed in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5122|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5122|smart-link] because we need a text-only byline there. When it’s fixed, this bug will change slightly: rather than a broken relative link for the author, there will be no link at all. However, the links in the summary portion should continue to work. Clear as mud, yeah?) What we _should_ be doing is creating an {{author}} element for each work creator, and each of those should have a {{name}} element and a {{uri}} element. So, if you’ll forgive the pseudo code, we need to do something more like this: {noformat} @works.each do |work| unless work.unrevealed? feed.entry work do |entry| entry.title work.title entry.summary feed_summary(work), :type => 'html' for each pseud on the work do entry.author do |author| author.name plain text version of byline author.uri absolute URL for pseud's dashboard end end end end end{noformat} It will be a bit more complex than that because it’ll also need to handle cases where the work byline is “Anonymous” (which will have no link) and where the work has been imported by an archivist and has a byline like “external_author_name [archived by archivist_name]” (which should probably also have no link, for simplicity’s sake). h2. column1: Remove %{type} from the co-creator emails and standardize OD/Support link placeholders in invitation to claim emails (OD)
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h3. Issue 1

*What happens:*
On the co-creator notification emails ({color:#ff0000}user_mailer.creatorship_invitation{color} and {color:#ff0000}user_mailer.creatorship_notification_archivist{color}), there's a {color:#ff0000}%\{type}{color} variable. This variable can be replaced by different things (work, series, chapter) which have different grammatical genders for several languages, making it impossible to translate this string accurately.

*What should happen:*
Instead of a variable, there should be different versions of the affected paragraphs for each type of creation, making translation easier.

h3. Issue 2

*What happens:*

There’s some inconsistency in the strings used to refer to Open Doors and Support in the user_mailer.invitation_to_claim email:

* “by %\{open_doors_link}” (= “Open Doors”)
* “imported by Open Doors (%\{open_doors_link})” (= actual URL)
* “please %\{support_link}.” (= “contact Support”)
* “please contact Support at %\{support_link}.” (= actual URL)

This can be confusing for translators working on this email.

*What should happen:*

It would be easier if these links were named more consistently.
