column1: Change kudo uniqueness validation to use users instead of pseuds
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Update the Rails uniqueness validator on kudos to use user_id instead of pseud_id.

We won't clean up the duplicates in the database just yet, and as before people will still be able to get past this check on a dodgy connection, but it will be harder to leave duplicates from the same user (even when changing default pseuds).

When we do add the uniqueness constraint at the database level, we'll have the error handling ready at the application level (people will see "left kudos here :)" as usual).

For the rare cases where users can get past the Rails validation and run into the (future) database constraint, we should catch {{ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique}} exceptions, similar to what we do on user creations: https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/57e7cab589abc7cc666ddf4d3abe768d801b3493/app/controllers/users_controller.rb#L9-L24.

*How to test*:
- Check that leaving logged in kudos still works.
- Check that leaving logged in kudos a second time on the same work will get you the "left kudos here :)" message.
- Check that you can no longer leave logged in kudos after changing default pseuds.

column1: Add migration to update the primary key and unique constraints on the kudos table
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
This is the one prophesied to take down the site. Migration:

- Change the primary key type from INT to BIGINT.
- Add unique index for commentable_id + commentable_type + user_id. This will remove duplicate kudos for the same work from the same user.
- Add unique index for commentable_id + commentable_type + ip_address. This will remove duplicate kudos for the same work from the same guest IP.

The migration will be different depending on the environment:

- Add a usual Rails migration, to be used in dev and CI environments.
- Add a comment with the pt-online-schema-change command to be run on staging and beta (similar to AO3-5844).

*How to test*:
- (/) (Anyone) Test AO3-5868 first.
- (/) (Server admin) Test the migration:
-# Run the migration.
-# Copy the commands that it prints to a file.
-# Run the pt-online-schema-change command, but not any of the SQL commands that follow it.
-# Create a brand new kudos, and note the ID in the database.
-# Create another kudos on the same work, from the same user (by using the Rails console and skipping validation, {{.save(validate: false)}}). This is a duplicate of the kudos from the previous step.
-# Run the SQL commands. (RENAME TABLE, DROP TRIGGER, and DROP TABLE)
-# Check whether the kudos that you created is still there. Check that it has no duplicates (the duplicates should have been eaten by the pt-online-schema-change migration).
-# From the Rails console: try to insert a duplicate kudos, bypassing validations, and make sure that it generates an error.
- (/) (Server admin) Test that the migration can run up and down and up again.
- (/) (Anyone) Finally, in the post-migration world:
-- Check that leaving logged in kudos still works.
-- Check that leaving logged in kudos a second time on the same work will get you the "left kudos here :)" message.
-- Check that you can no longer leave logged in kudos after changing default pseuds.

We're trying out this migration process on a smaller table first: AO3-5807.

But that does make me think that just waiting a few weeks before deletion might be sufficient to delete the second table smoothly.
{quote}

Ongoing discussion: we want to wait for some time before dropping the remaining table. If the table is no longer in the buffer pool and the adaptive hash index, dropping it will be a lightweight operation (no need for the deletion to be replicated). column1: Blockquote styling overlaps with user icon in comment display
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps to reproduce*
Create a comment that contains a {{blockquote}} at the beginning of the comment body.

*What happens*
The text wraps around the floated user icon, the line indicating the blockquote however overlaps with the icon. The result is that the icon is positioned on top of the border and there's a large gap between the border and the text that has been pushed to the right by the icon. See attachment for an example.

*What should happen*
The comment content wraps around the floated user icon, the blockquote styling should be adjusted to work the same way. The gray line indicating the blockquote should be pushed to the right with the text, or the entire block should be pushed to below the icon.

*Notes*
This is not a render bug, the CSS behaves as we tell it to. We have to decide how blockquotes should behave in comments and adjust the CSS accordingly.

* Tested in Firefox 72.02, Safari 13.05, Chrome 79 on Mac OS X.
* Behaviour is the same with narrow, medium and wide viewport
* Example is a comment for a work, but should be the same for all comments everywhere

*Deploy notes*

Needs a skin recache.

this is a [block formatting context|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Block_formatting_context] issue and seems like there are three main ways to push the blockquote border to the right:

# {{overflow: auto}} - full browser support but technically not what {{overflow}} is for. it shouldn’t have side effects in the default skin, but could have some in some funky custom ones
# {{display: flow-root}} - the css3 keyword created for exactly this purpose, allegedly no side effects, [major browsers support since 2017-2020|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/display#browser_compatibility]
# {{display: flow-root}} with a fallback to {{display: table}} for older browsers - {{display: table}} will push the blockquote border to the right as well, but it’ll also make the blockquote element width match the text inside it instead of stretching to the whole comment, which would be visible e.g. if a site skin gave blockquotes a background. also not what {{display: table}} is for either, but possibly preferable to not having a fallback at all

- The task should only consider works with kudos.
- The task should use StatCounterIndexer. We want to update the existing indexed works, we don't have to reindex whole works. The task should not reindex bookmarked works (a different index that doesn't track kudos count).
- The task should process in batches and sensibly print its progress.

*How to test*:
- Admins can edit a work's stat_counter to have some absurd kudos count.
- Reindex the work to put it at the top of any kudos descending list.
- Run the task.
- Check that the work is positioned correctly in kudos descending lists.

On beta, this task should be run after AO3-5869.

column1: Chapter numbering allows for a "Chapter 0" and behaves weirdly when chapters posted afterwards
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
To reproduce the problem:

1. Post a single chapter for a multi-chapter work.
2. Use "Edit Chapter" option to identify it as chapter "0" (of something).
3. Post at least 2 other chapters, manually numbering them before posting as chapters 1 and 2.

What typically happens:

The original "Chapter 0" moves to the last slot, and there are duplicate chapter numbers. For example, if you post Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 after "Chapter 0", both Chapter 2 and "Chapter 0" are numbered as Chapter 3. There is no Chapter 2. The manually-entered numbers are overwritten with 3, 1, and 3, respectively (displayed in the order of 1, 3, and 3).

If you add additional chapters, manually entering the desired chapter number for each one (with a 0 starting point), the "Chapter 0" remains at the end. The last chapter number is duplicated, and the one before is skipped. (4 chapters are numbered as 1, 2, 4, and 4, and so on.)

Stopping at only Chapter 1 doesn't having any numbering issues, but "Chapter 0" is moved to the Chapter 2 slot.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
After AO3-5859, the pseud_id column of kudos should no longer be used anywhere in the site UI. We need to:

* Stop saving/deleting default pseud IDs on kudos.
* Remove the last mentions on pseud_id in kudos-related specs.
* Add a migration to remove the pseud_id column. The migration should use pt-online-schema-change for staging and production environments, following the pattern in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5807#icft=AO3-5807|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5807#icft=AO3-5807|smart-link] and AO3-5869.

*How to test the migration*:
1. Run the migration.
2. Copy the commands that it prints to a file.
3. Run the pt-online-schema-change command (but no SQL commands).
4. Leave a new logged in kudos. This kudos should have the user_id of your current user, but the pseud_id should be nil because we removed that code.
5. Run the SQL commands. (RENAME TABLE, DROP TRIGGER, and DROP TABLE)
6. Check whether the kudos that you created is still there. It should have no pseud_id at this point.

*How to test*:
After the migration, sanity check that you leave logged in and guest kudos as usual.

column1: Allow linking to each sign-up and each request on the Requests Summary page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Background:

- The Requests Summary page of a gift exchange is visible to all users, logged in or not, provided the option "Requests visible?" in the challenge settings is checked. Example: https://archiveofourown.org/collections/smut4smut2020/requests.
- The Prompts page of a prompt meme is visible to all users, logged in or not. Example: https://archiveofourown.org/collections/GenAndAroPrompts/requests.
- Note that when the Requests Summary/Prompts pages are visible, they don't show up on the challenge sidebar for logged out users ([gift exchange sidebar|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/views/challenge/gift_exchange/_challenge_sidebar.html.erb#L1], [prompt meme sidebar|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/views/challenge/prompt_meme/_challenge_sidebar.html.erb#L11]).

If the /requests page is visible as described above:

- The sign-up pages should be similarly visible, e.g. https://archiveofourown.org/collections/smut4smut2020/signups/220408. The sign-up page currently denies permission unless you own the sign-up or are a challenge mod.
-- A sign-up page should only show requests/prompts, _not offers_, unless you own the sign-up or are a challenge mod.
-- A sign-up page should not include anonymous requests/prompts.
-- A sign-up page should not be visible if there are no non-anonymous requests/prompts.
- The individual request/prompt pages within sign-ups should be similarly visible, e.g. https://archiveofourown.org/collections/smut4smut2020/prompts/1538164. In prompt meme's case, this issue overlaps AO3-3828.
- On the /requests page:
-- Each request/prompt should have a "All Requests in Sign-up" button at the bottom (next to the "Edit" button, if you own the request/prompt), allowing you to see other requests by that user and/or easily get the link to your own sign-up.
--- Exception: if the prompt is anonymous.
-- Each request/prompt's title (usually just "Request," unless the mod has enabled the "Title" field for sign-ups) should link to that request/prompt's page (e.g. https://archiveofourown.org/collections/smut4smut2020/prompts/1538164). Related: AO3-3828.
-- Each request/prompt's [byline|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/views/prompts/_prompt_blurb.html.erb#L10-L14] should link to the prompter's dashboard, just like on work blurbs, but only if the prompter isn't anonymous.

*How to test*: TBD.

16/Mar/20 9:47 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Some things to be careful of:

* The page showing all of the user’s requests in a gift exchange cannot show their offers to other people.
* If a prompt is anonymous, it definitely shouldn’t link to the sign-up.
* If a user has a mix of of anonymous and non-anonymous prompts, the non-anonymous prompts can (and probably should) link to the sign-up, but the sign-up view cannot include any of the user’s anonymous prompts.
* If a user has all anonymous prompts, the sign-up probably shouldn’t be visible. Even a blank page showing that the user has signed up for that particular prompt meme might be too revealing, because if there’s only one anonymous prompt in the prompt meme, it’s very clear who it belongs to. (They should probably also be excluded from the list of people who are signed up, but that’s a different issue.)

(The complexities of these permissions kind of makes me wonder if it would be better to have a separate controller for viewing other people’s request lists. Maybe it’d make sense as part of the requests controller?)

column1: Challenges: Possible to sign up for the same challenge more than once using multiple pseuds
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When creating a new {{ChallengeSignup}}, the validations [check whether the same pseud has already created a sign-up for the same collection|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/models/challenge_signup.rb#L72], but not whether a different pseud owned by the same user has already created a sign-up for the same collection. The only thing preventing a user with multiple pseuds from signing up with multiple pseuds is the code in {{ChallengeSignupsController#new}} that [redirects the user to the edit action if they already have a sign-up in the collection|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/controllers/challenge_signups_controller.rb#L200-L202]. However, this check only prevents displaying the form -- if you load multiple copies of the form before the first sign-up is created, you can submit as many sign-ups as you have pseuds.

*Steps to Reproduce:*
# Create a new challenge (either a gift exchange or a prompt meme) with open sign-ups.
# Log in as a user with multiple pseuds, or create several pseuds for this purpose.
# Visit the challenge profile.
# Open multiple copies of the challenge sign-up form in different tabs, one for each pseud.
# In the first tab, select your first pseud from the dropdown, fill out the rest of the form, and submit it.
# In the second tab, select your second pseud from the dropdown, fill out the rest of the form, and submit it.
# Repeat for the rest of your pseuds.

Note that if you click on the "My Signup" link in the sidebar, it'll only show you one sign-up. But if you view the list of requests, you should be able to see all of them. And if you view the list of all your challenge sign-ups, you can see all of them listed there as well.

All sign-ups created this way appear to be treated as valid sign-ups by the system. You can edit them without errors, and even run matching.

column27:
* The Archive currently offers two options to restrict commenting on works: the "Disable anonymous comments" option and the "Enable comment moderation" option. These options are offered on the new/edit work page and on the edit multiple works page. They are not on the import work page. We would like to add a third option that will allow users to disable comments entirely. This will require modifying the display of the current options. * Only the work creator(s), not admins, can modify a work’s comment settings. * When the creator(s) turns comments off, the comment form will be removed and replace with a blue notice that says, “Sorry, this work doesn’t allow comments.” This corresponds with what non-users see when anonymous comments are turned off. * If the work has comments, and the creator(s) turns comments off, the comments will remain visible. This corresponds with the behavior of existing anonymous comments when anonymous comments are turned off. * If you are composing a comment on a work and the creator disables comments before you submit yours, the comment will be discarded, and you will be given the error message, “Sorry, this work doesn’t allow comments.” Again, this will be consistent with what happens if anonymous comments are disabled in similar circumstances. In the future, for both instances, we can work out a way to include the text in an error message in case the user wants to preserve their comment. h3. Appearance of comment options on the new/edit work page !edit_single (d8aa17af-6697-4e6c-aeec-9a2fdd4eef5d).png|width=600! * In the “Privacy” {{fieldset}}, the existing “Disable anonymous comments checkbox” should be removed, as should its help pop-up. * Below the remaining options should be a section with all the comment options. The section should be called “Who can comment on this work,” and it should have a help pop-up link that will describe the behavior of the options. ** Text for the help pop-up is below. * The comment options should be presented as a list of three radio buttons in a {{fieldset}}, in the following order and with the following names: “Registered users and guests can comment,” which should be preselected; “Only registered users can comment;” and “No one can comment.” h3. column1: Rewrite hit counting to work with nginx caching
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h2. Background

We're going to start caching works for logged out users, which means whenever we serve up a cached work, we'll be skipping the code that triggers an increase in the work's hit count. That's not good!

To get around this, we will use JS to count hits, whether or not the page is cached, and whether or not the user is logged in. And since we are already here, we might as well rewrite how we count hits, to address AO3-4751.

How hits should work:
{quote}
You go to any chapter of a work. One hit is added. From there, you navigate to a different chapter of the work. No hits are added. You close the browser. Later or tomorrow, you come back to the work. One hit is added. You move through the work and again no hits are added.
{quote}

h2. Implementation

- Add JS on individual work/chapter pages to make an AJAX request to a new endpoint for logging hits. This JS code will be the same for logged out and logged in users. Hit counts will no longer be incremented as part of the work/chapter rendering.

- Log hits into Redis, then have background tasks periodically move new hit data into the database (the stat_counters table). This approach for database updates hasn't changed.

- De-duplicate hits on the same work (regardless of chapters), from the same visitor, within the same period of time (e.g. 24h). When logging a hit, save to Redis: the work ID, the visitor IP, and the time.

- Use Redis sets (tentative plan, see also the [actual implementation|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3796] which combines some of these sets).
-- Sets (A) with (work ID + timestamp) key, containing IPs of all visitors on that work within the time period identified by the timestamp. 
-- Sets (B) with (work ID) key, containing the names of all the existing (A) sets. We use them to clean up outdated (A) sets.
-- Sets (C) with (work ID) key, containing the count of IPs added since the last time we move hits to the database. When moving hits to the database, take only the unique count of IPs. The actual IPs remain ephemeral in Redis.
-- A single set (D) of all work IDs with changed hits.

- For the timestamp in the key of (A), use a configurable value that stays the same for 24h. For example, if we use "the most recent 3am", 3am is the fixed rollover time. After 3am, the same visitor on the same work can generate a new hit.

- Move hit counts to the database more frequently than the de-duplicating time period (24h). Whenever a new, unseen IP is added to (A) by SADD, we increment the counter in (C) by SADD's return value. This way users don't have to wait 24h before seeing hits change.
-- If (A) is a new set, we need to add it to (B). The work ID should also be added to (D). We should use Redis transactions to make sure all writes succeed.

- Have the background task (run more frequently than 24h) do 2 things:
-- Get works with changed hits from (D), add their counts from (C) to the database. Updating StatCounter models will automatically trigger reindexing on works. Empty (D) and reset (C) to 0.
-- Iterate through (B) and delete outdated (A) sets (e.g. more than 24h old).

h2. Notes

h3. Things we can remove

- The unused LogfileReader module for parsing nginx logs, and the module's tests.
- The last_visitor column on the stat_counters table.
- The last_visitor_old and hit_count_old columns on the works table.

h3. Cons of JS-based hit counters

- We will not count hits from users who disable JS.
- We will not count hits from users who have privacy blockers. For example, FanFiction.Net has [its hit counter URL blocked by EasyPrivacy|https://github.com/easylist/easylist/blob/9101fc9c8b3ba2f156d4a15b012619da6a11312a/easyprivacy/easyprivacy_specific.txt#L686].

h3. Counting hits from nginx (alternative)

We considered looking at the nginx logs to determine how many hits to add to the work. We would increase the hit count by one every time we serve the actual work (not the adult content warning) to a particular remote address, provided the previous hit was not also from that address.

Reference: [Keeping Hitcounts accurate when using an NGinx Caching Proxy|https://www.bentasker.co.uk/documentation/linux/253-keeping-hitcounts-accurate-when-using-an-nginx-caching-proxy].

We decided against this because making our application code and our nginx setup highly dependent on each other will be difficult to maintain in the long term, especially as the nginx configuration is not currently tracked in the public repository.

h2. Testing

1. Make sure that the owner's hits don't count:
- Find a work that you created, but haven't visited recently.
- View it multiple times logged-in as the creator. Note the hit count in the header.
- Wait at least 30 minutes for the stats to update.
- View the work and verify that the hit count hasn't increased.

2. Make sure that logged-in hits count:
- Find a work that you haven't visited recently.
- Log in as a user unrelated to the work.
- View the work multiple times. Note the hit count in the header.
- Wait at least 30 minutes for the stats to update.
- View the work and verify the hit count has increased by 1.

3. Make sure that logged-out hits count:
- Find a work that you haven't visited recently.
- View it multiple times logged-out. Note the hit count in the header.
- Wait at least 30 minutes for the stats to update.
- View the work and verify the hit count has increased by 1.

4. Make sure that cached hits count:
- Find a work that you haven't visited recently.
- Get two devices with different IP addresses ready (or one device with a proxy).
- While logged-out, view the work on the first device (to generate the cache). Note the hit count in the header.
- While logged-out, view the work on the second device.
- Wait at least 30 minutes for the stats to update.
- View the work again and verify that the hit count has increased by 2.

5. Make sure that interleaving multiple views only counts twice:
- Find a work that you haven't visited recently.
- Get two devices with different IP addresses ready (or one device with a proxy).
- Make sure you're logged out (or logged in as a user other than the owner).
- View the work on the first device.
- View the work on the second device.
- View the work on the first device again.
- Wait at least 30 minutes for the stats to update.
- View the work again and verify that the hit count has increased by 2.

6. Make sure that the rollover happens properly:
- Find a work that you haven't visited recently.
- Make sure you're logged out (or logged in as a user other than the owner).
- View the work slightly before 3 AM UTC. Note the hit count in the header.
- View the work again slightly after 3 AM UTC, with the same IP address.
- Wait at least 30 minutes for the stats to update.
- View the work again and verify that the hit count has increased by 2.

7. Make sure that viewing later chapters increments the hit count.
- Find a multichapter work that you haven't visited recently.
- Make sure you're logged out (or logged in as a user other than the owner).
- Copy the work URL and add /navigate to the end of the path to view the chapter index.
- Click on one of the later chapters. Note the hit count in the header.
- Wait at least 30 minutes for the stats to update.
- View the chapter again and verify that the hit count has increased by 1.

8. Re-test AO3-5639


h2. Post-deploy

h3. Staging

- (/) Remove cron jobs that run {{rake statistics}} tasks.
- (/) Run {{bundle exec rake statistics:update_stat_counters}} one last time *using an old version of the application code*.
- (/) Run {{bundle exec rake After:remove_old_redis_hit_count_data}} to clean up all traces of old hit counting in Redis.
- (/) Run all 3 migrations at leisure.

h3. Beta

- (/) Remove cron jobs that run {{rake statistics}} tasks.
- (/) Run {{bundle exec rake statistics:update_stat_counters}} one last time *using an old version of the application code*.
- (/) Run {{bundle exec rake After:remove_old_redis_hit_count_data}} to clean up all traces of old hit counting in Redis.
- (/) Run all 3 migrations at leisure.

column1: Adult content warning always appears when guests access adult works
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We currently use the session cookie to determine if we should show guests the adult content warning.

Unfortunately, now that we’ve implemented caching, this approach no longer works: even if you view an adult (Mature, Explicit, or Not Rated) work and press “Proceed” on the content warning, the next adult work you access will show you the warning as well.

We need to more this information out of the session cookie and into a separate one so we can use it with [cookie-aware nginx caching|https://dev.to/ale_ukr/how-to-make-nginx-cache-cookie-aware-2ffl]:

* [Setting the cookie in the works controller|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/eea20003da26c7cae66c2377a58816e20645f010/app/controllers/works_controller.rb#L194-L195]
* [Setting the cookie in the chapters controller|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/eea20003da26c7cae66c2377a58816e20645f010/app/controllers/chapters_controller.rb#L30-L31]
* [Checking the cookie in the application controller|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/09565b8ee6f850fe22eab08823940b7347b849bb/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L390]

*Testing*

* While logged out, clear cookies or open a private/incognito window
* Find a multichapter adult work in a work listing somewhere and follow the link to visit it
* You should get the adult content warning
* Press “Proceed”
* You should see the first chapter
* Press “Next Chapter”
* You should see the second chapter and no adult content warning
* Find another adult work in a work listing somewhere and follow the link to visit it (note that, if you’re testing this in private/incognito mode, you’ve got to stay in the tab you’re in)
* You should not see the adult content warning
* Close your browser
* Reopen your browser, 
* Go to staging
* Find an adult work in a listing somewhere and follow the link
* You should get the adult content warning, because the cookie is a session cookie and you’re in a new session

Additionally, after pressing “Proceed” on the warning, you should use your browser’s developer tools to check the cookies… there should be one called {{view_adult}} and its value should be {{true}}. This is what that looks like in Safari:

!safari_cookies (003291db-37d5-4de9-8154-02537f66abd4).png|width=1280,height=216!

Note: We had some trouble with the session cookie not being sticky enough for logins, which is why even a non-"Remember me" log in lasts two weeks. We might have to set the expiry on this to 2 weeks as well.

column1: Generate sharing options when the user pushes the "Share" button, not when the work page is loaded
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Currently, the "Share" button on work pages is set up so that all of the sharing options are rendered and embedded in the work page, and the "Share" button just shows them (without performing another HTTP request). This means that:

# The server is performing unnecessary work for any user who views the work page and doesn't press the "Share" button.
# The twitter and tumblr buttons included in the sharing options mean that the user sends an HTTP request with AO3 listed as the referrer ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5818#icft=AO3-5818|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5818#icft=AO3-5818|smart-link]) to both twitter and tumblr when they view a work.

It would be good to move the sharing options off of the work page and into their own controller, to be loaded dynamically when the user presses the "Share" button.

The “Share” button is not currently presented to users who don’t have JavaScript disabled, and this behavior should continue. 

*Testing Instructions:* Make sure that you can still use the "Share" button on works.

column1: Redirecting to a multi-chapter work's first chapter uses an absolute URL, forcing users onto the secure site
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps to reproduce for works*

# Log out (to ensure you are viewing multi-chapter works in chapter by chapter mode)
# Go to the _insecure_ address for a multi-chapter work on production, e.g. [http://insecure.archiveofourown.org/works/17922041|http://insecure.archiveofourown.org/works/17922041]

*What happens*

You are redirected to the work's first chapter on the HTTPS site, i.e. [https://archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317183|https://archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317183]

*What should happen*

You should be redirected to the work's first chapter on the insecure site, i.e. [http://insecure.archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317183|http://insecure.archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317183]

*Steps to reproduce for chapters*

# Log out (to ensure you are viewing multi-chapter works in chapter by chapter mode)
# Go to the _insecure_ address for a specific chapter of an adult-rated multi-chapter work on production, e.g. [http://insecure.archiveofourown.org/works/15922211/chapters/37119413|http://insecure.archiveofourown.org/works/15922211/chapters/37119413]

*What happens*

After clicking "Proceed", you are redirected to the chapter on the HTTPS site, with the {{?view_adult=true}} parameters added, i.e. [https://archiveofourown.org/works/15922211/chapters/37119413?view_adult=true|https://archiveofourown.org/works/15922211/chapters/37119413?view_adult=true]

*What should happen*

You should be redirected to the chapter on the insecure site, with the {{?view_adult=true}} params, i.e. [http://insecure.archiveofourown.org/works/15922211/chapters/37119413?view_adult=true|http://insecure.archiveofourown.org/works/15922211/chapters/37119413?view_adult=true]

*Testing notes*

We don’t have an insecure staging site, so probably the best you can do is make sure you’re redirected to the proper page on staging, and then we can check on production to make sure the insecure to secure switch doesn’t happen.

column1: Simplify Elasticsearch query to sort bookmarkables by "Date Bookmarked"
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Initial write-up: [Bookmark sorting in Elasticsearch|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i8ModbjUFKum2i4KOix3WwTs_BTgfOcQUiY4lQHblqU/preview].

When sorting bookmarkables (instead of bookmarks, e.g. on a page like {{tags/X/bookmarks}} instead of {{users/X/bookmarks}}) by "Date Bookmarked", we have to calculate on the fly the value for sorting, which is the maximum {{created_at}} time of all "child" bookmarks for each "parent" bookmarkable. This value is [stored in the result score|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/4579eacc4145a325cf89cf28a01037430e3b3e1e/app/models/search/bookmarkable_query.rb#L96-L106]. Queries like this are complicated and show up in the [slow query log|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.8/index-modules-slowlog.html].

We should keep the query simple, by sorting on a new field last_bookmarked_at of the indexed parent bookmarkable. Every time a new bookmark is made, reindex its bookmarkable. To avoid reindexing the bookmarkable too much (e.g. on popular works), we can batch updates, similar to the StatCounterIndexer.

We basically move the calculation from query time (happens for every search) to index time (happens only when new bookmarks are created).

*How to test*:
For tag listings:
# On a {{tags/X/bookmarks}} page, sort by "Date Bookmarked". Find an older bookmarked work in the listing, note its position, then bookmark it. After reindexing, the work should show up at the top of the listing.
# Delete the bookmark you just made. Wait for reindexing. Then on the same page, sorted by "Date Bookmarked", the work should return to its former place in the listing.

For bookmark searches:
# On https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search, select Sort by option "Date Bookmarked", and search for whatever you want. Find an older bookmarked work in the search results, note its position, then bookmark it. After reindexing, the work should show up at the top of the search results.
# Delete the bookmark you just made. Wait for reindexing, then rerun the search. The work should return to its former place in the search results.

*Note*: We will need to reindex all bookmarkables (not bookmarks though).

column1: Parent skin names are case insensitive, potentially leading to users having access to others' skins
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
What should happen:
When a user saves a skin after having added a parent skin, the skin assigned as the parent skin should belong to the user (or be public) and should match the case of what the user entered.

What happens instead:
When a user enters the name of a skin to be used as a parent skin, regardless of what capitalization they use, when the save the child skin the parent skin actually assigned will be whatever skin was first created with that name disregarding capitalization/cases. This will happen even if that skin does not belong to the user who is trying to add a parent skin.


To replicate:

1) make a site skin with a unique name using one account
2) switch to a different account
3) make another site skin with the same name, but different cases/capitalization
3) make a third skin and try to add the second skin as its parent

The child skin will have the first skin listed as a parent skin instead of the second skin, and if you use that child skin and inspect what css is being applied, you will see the css from the first skin being applied but not any from the second skin.

column1: Modify batch kudos notification code to avoid the Redis KEYS command
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Currently, the batch kudos notification code calls the Redis {{KEYS}} command once for each author who received kudos in the past day:
{code}
      keys = REDIS_KUDOS.keys("kudos_#{author_id}_*")
{code}
[(source)|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/030fa4607d3c59fba2cacbe4e9c99b3c49fbc1cb/app/models/redis_mail_queue.rb#L19]

However, the Redis docs discourage the use of {{KEYS}} in production code:
{quote}
Warning: consider KEYS as a command that should only be used in production environments with extreme care. It may ruin performance when it is executed against large databases. This command is intended for debugging and special operations, such as changing your keyspace layout. Don't use KEYS in your regular application code.
{quote}
[(source)|https://redis.io/commands/keys]

The batch kudos notification code should be rewritten to avoid the use of {{KEYS}}.

h3. Notes

The deploy for this may be a bit tricky. Ideally, all users should be notified about all kudos they receive, even those that were recorded by the old kudos notification code right before the new kudos notification code goes live. There are several different possible approaches to take, including the following:

# Deploy the new code, then run {{rake notifications:deliver_kudos}} one last time on an old copy of the code (like AO3-5905). This would result in an extra kudos email.
# Split this issue over two deploys: one to add extra sets for bookkeeping purposes (that aren't immediately used, because the data added just before the deploy wouldn't be tracked properly), and one to get rid of the call to {{KEYS}} (deployed at least a day later).
# Write an After task, to be run immediately after deploy, to make sure that all of the information added prior to the deploy is updated to match the new code.

h3. Testing Instructions

The instructions for how to test the change from the old kudos notification code to the new kudos notification code will depend on the approach taken. However, the instructions for testing the new code should be the same in all cases:
# Find (or create) a work by an account whose email you have access to.
# Leave a logged-in kudos on the work.
# Leave a logged-out kudos on the work.
# Wait until the kudos notification emails are sent.
# Make sure that the email includes both of the kudos that you left.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Similar to AO3-5905 where we move hit count data out of REDIS_GENERAL and into a separate Redis instance, we want to do the same for reading data.

- Create new configuration REDIS_READINGS; update reading code to use it; update tests to flush it.
- Start an extra Redis instance for REDIS_READINGS in Travis; use an existing Redis instance for it in Codeship.
- Remove reading_tasks.rake and move the task to resque-scheduler, with a schedule of {{55 * * * *}}.

How to test:
- Visit some works (once or multiple times), wait for the scheduled task to run, then check that your reading history is updated as expected (view count up, last visited time changes).

Post-deploy:
- Run {{rake readings:to_database}} one last time on an old copy of the code (like AO3-5905), to move all data from the old Redis instance to the database.

column1: Fix some flaky tests related to login with JS and tag wrangling with Elasticsearch
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
There are a number of automated tests that fail intermittently. The goal of this issue is to make some of those tests pass more consistently. (Hopefully.)

h3. features/works/work_create.feature:52

For this test, the HTML snapshot from cucumber seems to indicate that the user isn't logged-in, even though there's a step immediately beforehand which is supposed to make the user log in:

{code:ruby}
Given /^(?:I have )?(?:a|an|the) (hidden)?(?: )?(anonymous)?(?: )?(moderated)?(?: )?(closed)?(?: )?collection "([^\"]*)"(?: with name "([^\"]*)")?$/ do |hidden, anon, moderated, closed, title, name|
  step %{I am logged in as "moderator"}
  step %{I set up the collection "#{title}" with name "#{name}"}
{code}

It seems like something about the log-in step may be causing it to fail:

{code:ruby}
Given /^I am logged in as "([^"]*)" with password "([^"]*)"$/ do |login, password|
  user = find_or_create_new_user(login, password)
  step("I am logged out")
  step %{I am on the homepage}
  find_link('login-dropdown').click

  fill_in "User name or email:", with: login
  fill_in "Password:", with: password
  check "Remember Me"
  click_button "Log In"
  step %{confirmation emails have been delivered}
end
{code}
It may be that after the "Log In" button is clicked, cucumber moves onto the next step and loads the next page before the request to log in has finished processing. If that's the case, it would result in the user sometimes failing to be treated as logged-in. It would be possible to fix this just by adding an extra step to the log-in step that checks whether the user sees the appropriate page after login (because this only occurs in tests tagged with {{@javascript}}, which means that if the browser doesn't immediately see the appropriate page, it will wait for the page to finish loading before declaring defeat).

This is a common issue that may also contribute to these intermittent failures:
{code}
features/tag_sets/tag_set.feature:141
features/tags_and_wrangling/tag_wrangling_freeforms.feature:6
features/tags_and_wrangling/tag_wrangling_characters.feature:6
features/tags_and_wrangling/tag_wrangling_relationships.feature:6
{code}

h3. features/tags_and_wrangling/tag_wrangling.feature:25

The line the failure typically occurs on is 235, the last line in this block of code:
{code}
    When I follow "Unwrangled"
    Then I should see "Showing Unwrangled Character Tags"
      And I should see "Samantha Carter"
      And I should not see "Jack O'Neill"
      And I should not see "Daniel Jackson"
      And I should not see "Anubis Arc"
{code}
If you look at the snapshot of HTML that cucumber prints out when this failure occurs, you can see that "Anubis Arc" is correctly listed as "Unwrangleable," which ought to mean that it doesn't show up on the "Unwrangled" page. But the "Unwrangleable" mark is determined from the SQL database; the choice of which tags to include is an Elasticsearch query. So it must be that Elasticsearch isn't up to date.

Tags automatically reindex themselves when the value of {{unwrangleable}} changes:
{code}
    if tag.saved_change_to_unwrangleable?
      tag.reindex_document
    end
{code}
However, tags can't refresh Elasticsearch automatically. And because the tag automatically reindexes itself, the test doesn't currently include the joint reindex/refresh test step. So Elasticsearch isn't guaranteed to perform a refresh in between the change to unwrangleable and the page that performs the query. It may be that refreshing is all that's needed to fix this test.

h3. Testing Instructions

This should be tested during the review phase by running the Travis builds enough times to see if the tests are less flaky than they used to be. Doesn't require any QA once it's deployed to staging.

Sometimes, a database admin has to look up comments by email for the Support committee. Comments aren't currently indexed on email. Doing so would make this a bit faster.

column1: Add a unique constraint for name and user ID on the pseuds table
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We are enforcing uniqueness on pseud names per user in Rails but not at the database level. Users who somehow end up with duplicate pseuds will be unable to change their passwords, because their duplicate pseuds are not valid (this symptom is similar to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3589#icft=AO3-3589|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3589#icft=AO3-3589|smart-link]).

We need:

* A rake task to rename existing duplicates (e.g. "pseud" to "pseud_2") so they don't prevent the creation of a unique index.
* A migration to add said unique index. The table has more than 500k rows, so we probably want to use pt-online-schema-change here. [There’s an example of how to write such a migration here.|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3805/files]

*How to test*:

* You need to have duplicate pseuds on staging. Database admins can force them into existence if necessary. Check that you cannot change your password ("Invalid pseud error").
* (Server admin) Run the rake task and make sure the duplicate pseuds get renamed.
* (Server admin) Run the migration.
* Check that you can change your password.

h1. Steps to reproduce We’re going to post a work with two chapters and then delete the first chapter: # Log in # Post > New Work # Fill in required fields and, on the way down, check "This work has multiple chapters." You don't have to do anything special in this field. # Press "Post" # Follow the "Add Chapter" link # Fill in required fields # Press "Post" # Follow the "Previous Chapter" link to return to Chapter 1 # Follow the "Edit Chapter" link # Press "Delete Chapter" and press "OK" to confirm deletion h1. What happens Many things\! But I'm reasonably sure they all relate to what's going on at the database level, which is the {{Chapter}} object's position attribute remains {{position: 2}}. Here, let me show you: {code:ruby}2.6.5 :002 > w = Work.find(1071170) => # 2.6.5 :003 > w.chapters => #This is chapter two.

", position: 2, work_id: 1071170, created_at: "2020-04-21 05:15:58", updated_at: "2020-04-21 05:17:05", posted: true, title: "", notes: "", summary: "", word_count: 4, hidden_by_admin: false, published_at: "2020-04-21", endnotes: "", content_sanitizer_version: 1, notes_sanitizer_version: 1, summary_sanitizer_version: 1, endnotes_sanitizer_version: 1>]> {code} Now, the practical, user-facing consequences of this are: * The title of the remaining chapter says "Chapter 2" * If you follow the "Edit Chapter" link on the chapter, you will see it listed as Chapter Number 2 of ? on the form, and the chapter text will appear in the Chapter Text field * If you follow the "Edit" link to edit the work, you will see the chapter's text in the Work Text field, which usually only happens for Chapter 1 of a work (until Chapter 2 is posted, then the text is no longer there) h1. * Calling {{includes(:work)}} alone doesn’t make rails select both tables in a single query. The joint query is caused when you have {{includes(:work).references(:works)}}, or {{includes(:work)}} combined with some {{where}} queries that reference the {{works}} table (which causes an implicit call to {{references(:works)}}). column1: Use Codecov Bash uploader for coverage
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Our code coverage tend to fluctuate (when it should be sitting pretty at 89% in April 2020). That's partly because our tests themselves are flaky (but we're not talking about that here), and partly, possibly because the gem codecov-ruby attempts to upload coverage data just once and [does not retry|https://github.com/codecov/codecov-ruby/issues/50].

The gem is updated infrequently. We can switch to the [Codecov Bash uploader|https://docs.codecov.io/docs/about-the-codecov-bash-uploader], which is more actively maintained and does have retrying behavior. It also [uses the pull request commit HEAD on Travis, if available|https://github.com/codecov/codecov-ruby/pull/51].

Codecov has [an example repo|https://github.com/codecov/ruby-standard-2/] showing how to set this up.

*How to test*: check https://codecov.io/gh/otwcode/otwarchive/branch/master ~1h after the change is merged. The most recent commit should be marked with "(/) CI Passed" and the latest number on the graph should be ~89%.

column1: Concurrency issue with comment threading
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When creating a new comment, {{threaded_left}} and {{threaded_right}} are supposed to be adjusted to accommodate the new comments. However, if two replies are being added to the same comment at exactly the same time, both new comments will end up with the same {{threaded_left}} and {{threaded_right}} values. This is because {{CommentsController#create}} loads the commentable (i.e. the parent comment) outside of the transaction, and it's not reloaded inside the transaction, so its {{threaded_left}} and {{threaded_right}} values (which are used to compute the new comments' {{threaded_left}} and {{threaded_right}} values) are out-of-date when the second comment is saved.

Currently, {{threaded_left}} and {{threaded_right}} are only used to compute the number of descendants that a given comment had ({{children_count}}), which is only displayed when the max depth has been reached and the comments are hidden. So on top of being tricky to replicate thanks to concurrency, it's almost impossible to notice.

*Testing Instructions:* This is basically impossible to replicate, so I'm not sure it can be tested manually. But it would be good to try replying to some comments and make sure that it still works as expected.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Go to insecure staging: [http://test.archiveofourown.org|http://test.archiveofourown.org/]
# Log out to ensure you're accessing works in chapter-by-chapter mode
# Find and access a multi-chapter work, and double check that you are still on the insecure site
# Open the Chapter Index, choose a chapter using the select menu, and press "Go"

h1. What happens

You are taken to the chapter, but on [https://test.archiveofourown.org|https://test.archiveofourown.org/] – the secure site. This is a problem if you're on an older device and can't access the secure site.

h1. What should happen

You should stay on the insecure site.

30/Apr/20 2:05 PM;5e8e2b8ee053b30b7a9fdd41;I took a look in the browser console and what seems to happen is this:

# The user selects a chapter in the chapter index dropdown and clicks on “Go”
# JavaScript/jQuery submits the form and sends a GET-Request for [http://insecure.archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317183?utf8=%E2%9C%93&selected_id=42317189&commit=Go|http://insecure.archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317183?utf8=%E2%9C%93&selected_id=42317189&commit=Go]
# The response returns a 302 and redirects the user to [http://archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317189|http://archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317189]
# This redirect triggers another 302, which sends the user to [https://archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317189|https://archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317189]

The response to the first request should return a redirect to [http://insecure.archiveofourown.org|http://insecure.archiveofourown.org] to keep the user on the insecure site. Double-checking the request exchange on the secure site confirms that there should only be one 302 happening, not two.

Tested on this work: [https://archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317183|https://archiveofourown.org/works/17922041/chapters/42317183]

If this happens before the request is put into Rails, Rails might not even be receiving the first request as insecure.ao3 at all. It might be getting it simply as [http://ao3|http://ao3], which would then return a [http://ao3|http://ao3] referral and make the browser request [http://ao3|http://ao3] without the “insecure”-part, which would then be redirected to https.

column1: Remove cookie-based redirection to the last visited page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
On most page loads, we save the current path in the session cookie (as {{session[:return_to]}}) so in the future, we can redirect the user back to this page if necessary. This feature behaves unpredictably at best, and any brokenness is exacerbated for guest users by [nginx-level full page caching|https://archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/15379], which ignores cookies.

We are removing this feature entirely. A non-exhaustive list of things to remove:

* Any references to {{session[:return_to]}}.
* The {{store_location}} callback.
* The unused method {{set_flash_cookie}}.
* The method {{redirect_back_or_default}}. Most of the time, this method can be replaced with a simple {{redirect_to}} targeting whatever we used to have as the {{default}} argument. In some cases, however, we do want to preserve the user's last visited location (e.g. when logging in, when logging in after viewing a restricted work as a guest). If we need to remember the last visited location, we should add the URL to redirect back to into the login form.

There are a number of GET actions that modify or update data, and should probably be changed to one of POST, PATCH, PUT, or DELETE:

* [/works/:id/mark_for_later|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/17307a8a6294d2af7fab882ea5aa14eb786d51af/config/routes.rb#L317]

* [/collections/:name/participants/join|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/17307a8a6294d2af7fab882ea5aa14eb786d51af/config/routes.rb#L413]
* [/collections/:name/assignments/generate|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/17307a8a6294d2af7fab882ea5aa14eb786d51af/config/routes.rb#L433]

* [/collections/:name/assignments/default_all|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/17307a8a6294d2af7fab882ea5aa14eb786d51af/config/routes.rb#L438]

* [/collections/:name/potential_matches/cancel_generate|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/17307a8a6294d2af7fab882ea5aa14eb786d51af/config/routes.rb#L450]
* [/collections/:name/potential_matches/regenerate_for_signup|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/17307a8a6294d2af7fab882ea5aa14eb786d51af/config/routes.rb#L451]

This is related to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5685|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5685|smart-link] [,|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5685,] and should be completed before [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5949|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5949|smart-link] .

25/Feb/22 7:54 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Is there a creatorship with the ID from the error? It seems like that error could occur in one of two cases: (a) the creatorship somehow didn’t get deleted when the creation did, or (b) the creatorship was loaded right before the creation was destroyed.

That error’s not a {{RecordNotFound}} error like the ones listed in this issue, so it wouldn't be covered by [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4037|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4037|smart-link]. It’s a very similar issue to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5956|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5956|smart-link] and [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6294|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6294|smart-link]. The initial object (creatorship, subscription) loads fine, but one of its associations doesn’t load (creation, user). But because associations aren’t required to exist, it just returns nil (causing a later {{NoMethodError}}) instead of immediately throwing a {{RecordNotFound}} error.

Many emails have to check {{user.preference}} to fetch the user’s locale, which means that this issue is everywhere. So I’m not sure what the best way to tackle it is. We could just add code everywhere to abort if something is nil, but it feels like there ought to be a more systematic way to solve it. I hesitate to abort on {{NoMethodError}} the way we abort on {{RecordNotFound}}, because that could potentially hide a bigger problem, but maybe it’d be okay to retry as long as the error bubbles up to the Resque failures queue if it persists. (Though that wouldn’t help in cases where the creatorship didn’t get deleted. If there are cases where the creatorship didn’t get deleted.)

The way we test authentication and user permissions in specs is not ideal:

* We set up instance variables {{@current_user}} and {{@current_admin}} which exist only in tests. If we use them we're not actually testing anything.

column1: Allow guest users to choose site skin
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*How to test*:

For guests:

* A guest user should see the "Choose Skin" section in the footer.
* A guest user should be able to pick one of the 4 options in the chooser (Default, Low Vision Default, Reversi, and Snow Blue). The chosen site skin should stick around while the guest user browses different pages, and after the guest closes and opens a new browser session (unless the old session was private/incognito).
* Multiple guest users can browse the site at the same time with different site skins (a guest should not see another guest's cached version of a page).

Site skin set by "Choose Skin" should still take precedence over site skin set in a user's preference:

* If a guest chooses site skin A from the footer, then logs in as a user with no default site skin set in their preferences, they should keep using A.
* If a guest chooses site skin A from the footer, then logs in as a user with a default site skin B set in their preferences, they should keep using A. If they then pick Default from "Choose Skin", they should start using B (not necessarily the Archive's default).

*Notes*: for guest site skins to work with full page caching by nginx, we need to:

* Change skin actions (set/unset) to not use GET requests ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5953#icft=AO3-5953|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5953#icft=AO3-5953|smart-link]).
* Fix redirection after the set/unset skin actions ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5949#icft=AO3-5949|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5949#icft=AO3-5949|smart-link]), to reduce confusion.
* Move the session skin for guests and users into a separate cookie instead of keeping it in the session cookie, for nginx's cookie-aware caching (similar to what we did with the adult warning preference in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5906#icft=AO3-5906|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5906#icft=AO3-5906|smart-link]).

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Our code for sending invitations appears to be struggling at least some of the time, so ideally we can determine why and optimize the process.

For manual testing, the best we can do is make sure both the "Send invite codes to people in our invitations queue" option and the task we use for the automated queue work. Then we'll see if things are better on production.

h1. "Send invite codes to people in our invitations queue" option

Full details, although I am certain not all are relevant:

* We started with these settings: Account creation enabled, Account creation requires invitation, and Invite from queue enabled. The "Number of people to invite from the queue at once" was set to 15,000, "How often (in days) should we invite people from the queue" was set to 1, and "How many weeks you have to activate your account before we purge it" was set to 2.
* The [Manage Queue page|https://archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/manage] showed 4,053 as the position of the last user in the queue.
* On the [admin invitations/Invite New Users page|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/invitations], the text in the "Send invite codes to people in our invitations queue" section said, "There are 4037 requests in the queue."
* Eight more people joined the queue.
* At about 06:00 UTC, an admin entered 4061 (4053 + 8) in the "Number of people to invite" field.
* The admin then went to the settings page and unchecked "Invite from queue enabled" and set "Number of people to invite from the queue at once" to 1.

The invitations began to slowly go out. No, I mean _slowly_: about one invitation was sent every half hour. As of 23:10 UTC later that day, "Send invite codes to people in our invitations queue" said, "There are 3933 requests in the queue" and the Manage Queue page showed the last user with a position of 3947.

That's 114 invitations sent in 17 hours, or an average of about 7 an hour.

This option only sees occasional use, so we're not sure if this is always a problem.

h1. The automated queue

This is with the same invitation-related admin settings.

PAC chair Matty reports that the invitations can be slow to send with this option as well and notes, "there have been a few days when they didn't go out at all, but those have been very sporadic. and some days when only some of them went out, but again, that's very sporadic. I have noticed lately that it's a lot slower than it used to be."

h1. Deploy notes

Has a migration to drop a column: {{bundle exec rake db:migrate:up VERSION=20220622075958}}. This should be run after the code has been deployed.

In addition, this replaces the {{rake invitations:check_queue}} task with a job in the Resque scheduler, so that task should be removed from the crontab.

column1: Updating a user's email address does not delete any invitation requests that exist for that address, leaving the request lingering in the queue
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce:

# Follow the "Get Invited!" link on the homepage
# Submit an email address
# Log in to an account
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Profile > Edit My Profile > Change Email
# Change the email to the one you put in the queue
# Have a database admin run the task for sending invitations
# Log in as an admin
# Invitations > Manage Queue

h1. What happens:

The address is still there, at the top of the queue, and an admin has to delete it.

h1. What should happen:

The address should not be lingering in the queue, requiring manual cleanup.

h1. Notes:

When the task to send out invitations runs, [invitations are not created for/sent to any addresses that match existing accounts|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/df7cac7f4103b8fa1a42cfe509097ad4cb71e9e2/app/models/invitation.rb#L10]. However, presumably because [the same method that creates the invitation also deletes the invitation request|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/df7cac7f4103b8fa1a42cfe509097ad4cb71e9e2/app/models/invite_request.rb#L57-L65], when we can't make the invitation, we also fail to delete the request.

You [cannot join the queue with an email address that is already used on an account|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/df7cac7f4103b8fa1a42cfe509097ad4cb71e9e2/app/models/invite_request.rb#L6].

If you create an account that uses an address that currently has a request in the queue, [the request is deleted|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/df7cac7f4103b8fa1a42cfe509097ad4cb71e9e2/app/models/user.rb#L35].

column1: Add task to fix tags with leading or trailing spaces
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
If a tag has surrounding spaces (e.g. "   Shinji   ") and there exists a version of that tag with no spaces (e.g. "Shinji"), then you can (not) edit the first tag, because of a Rails validation that squishes the tag, removing the spaces, resulting in an unsaveable duplicate tag (e.g. [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2349#icft=AO3-2349|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2349#icft=AO3-2349|smart-link]).

Rails 4 might have exacerbated the problem. From [~accountid:557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6]:

{quote}[https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/b5245da94a7c7667b57bb2184fa9aa7beb998da6|https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/b5245da94a7c7667b57bb2184fa9aa7beb998da6]

So any tags created before that update with non-breaking spaces can't be saved/updated except by admins because the name automatically gets squished (and the nbsp removed), which means that name doesn't match the previous name.{quote}

We should have a one-time After task to:

* Loop through all existing tags (in batches and sensibly printing its progress, of course).
* If running {{squish}} on a tag's name returns a different name, then save the tag with its spaces replaced with underscores. See Rails' implementation of {{squish}} for how to detect spaces.
* At the end of the task, print to stdout in CSV format for each updated tag: its ID, its old name, its updated name. Tag wranglers can use this list to check and further edit the tags if necessary.

*How to test*:
Run the task on staging. If the task updates no tags, then get database admins to manually screw up some tags.

Check that you (as a wrangler) can edit the changed tags on the site.

column1: Try to prevent cases where a tag's merger_id is non-nil but its merger is nil, and handle existing cases with fewer errors
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
There are some tags that have a nil {{merger}}, but still have their {{merger_id}} set.

This could be caused by issues with the {{Tag:delete_unused}} [rake task|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/35c4983e2586ad7745af136ca0f38ed66bf1bbb1/lib/tasks/tag_tasks.rake#L40-L45]:
{code:ruby}
    Tag.where(canonical: false, merger_id: nil, taggings_count_cache: 0).each do |t|
      if t.taggings.count.zero? && t.child_taggings.count.zero? && t.set_taggings.count.zero?
        deleted_names << t.name
        t.destroy
      end
    end
{code}
All of the unfilterable, unused tags are loaded at the beginning of the loop, but if the loop takes a while to run (which might happen if there are a lot of zero-use tags in tag sets), a tag could become canonical between the start of the loop (when the tag is loaded), and the middle of the loop (when the tag is processed). This could result in the tag being mistakenly deleted, so that any synonyms of the tag (added after the tag became canonical) would end up with a nil {{merger}} and a non-nil {{merger_id}}.

To address this, it might be necessary to do some or all of the following:
# Lock the tag before it's deleted, and recheck the {{canonical}}/{{merger_id}} values. This should help prevent canonical tags from being deleted, because no other transaction can set the tag to canonical while the lock is in effect, and the lock is only released once the tag is deleted.
# Set up the {{mergers}} association with {{dependent: :nullify}}, so that if any tags do have mergers when they're destroyed, the mergers will have their {{merger_id}} set to nil.
# Add a foreign key constraint to the {{merger_id}} field.
# Modify the tag code so that tags that are already in this state can be edited.

h3. Testing Instructions

This is probably difficult to replicate in the wild, but it would be good to test the behavior of the tags controller on pre-existing tags with this issue:
# In the console, create a tag with a {{merger_id}} pointing to a deleted tag.
# Go to the tag edit page and make some changes.
# Press "Update" and make sure that you get a success message instead of an error.

column1: Add a new column to the works table to store whether the work has comments disabled
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
In order to allow users to disable comments for AO3-5897, the works table needs to be modified to add a new column. This column should have type {{tinyint}}, so that it can take on three different values:

* {{0}} ({{enable_all}}) when all commenting on the work is enabled.
* {{1}} ({{disable_anon}}) when anonymous commenting is disabled, but registered comments are enabled.
* {{2}} ({{disable_all}}) when all commenting on the work is disabled.

There also needs to be a rake task to copy the existing value from {{anon_commenting_disabled}} to the new column.

(Note: From a migration perspective, it'd be easier to change the display width of the existing column and rename it, both of which are metadata-only changes and should be fairly instantaneous. But renaming columns with no downtime generally requires adding a copy of the column under the new name anyway, so we might as well change the type of the new column at the same time.)

h3. Deploy Steps

# Run the migration to add the new column.
# Do a rolling restart of the unicorns to make sure that they know that the new column exists.
# Once all unicorns have finished restarting, run the rake task {{After:copy_anon_commenting_disabled_to_comment_permissions}} to copy the contents of {{anon_commenting_disabled}} to the new column.

h3. Testing Instructions

# Find an old work that hasn't been edited since the deploy, with anonymous commenting disabled.
# Using the rails console, check the value of {{comment_permissions}} for that work. Make sure that it equals {{disable_anon}}.
# Edit the work to allow anonymous comments.
# Use the rails console, check the value of {{comment_permissions}} for that work. Make sure that it equals {{enable_all}}.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required fields
# Check "Enable comment moderation"
# Press "Post" to post the work
# Log out
# Go to the work you posted
# Fill in the comment form
# Press "Comment"
# Log out
# Log in as an admin
# Go to the work you posted
# Follow the "Unreviewed Comments (1)" link at the top of the work to view all unreviewed comments

h1. What happens

There is [an "Approve All Unreviewed Comments" link|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/148004d1f4c29f4ee4f31a2f25633e06e0dff63a/app/views/comments/unreviewed.html.erb#L7] at the top of the page. 

h1. What should happen

The button should not be there for admins. (Confirmed with Policy & Abuse Committee.) Fortunately, it doesn't do anything, so if someone accidentally presses it, it's harmless.

column1: Rename "Blacklisted Emails" to "Banned Emails"
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We'd like to rename the admin "Blacklisted Emails" feature "Banned Emails."

This includes all uses of the term "blacklist" in the interface as well as the code – even the table name, translation keys, and validator. The table has less than 300 rows, so a regular Rails migration should be fine.

h2. Migration

During the migration, we will maintain both the existing table and the new renamed table simultaneously.

Because the table can only be modified by a small set of admins, we can simply ask folks to not ban any emails while the migration is happening, instead of having measures in place to keep data in sync between the two table.

# Before deploying, run a migration to create the new table {{admin_banned_emails}}. The migration should also run a {{INSERT ... SELECT}} statement to copy data from the old table over.
# Deploy code changes, which use the new table. No downtime is expected.
# At this point, the old table {{admin_blacklisted_emails}} should be unused. Run a second migration to delete the old table, at leisure.

h2. Text

User-facing text is already handled by [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6394|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6394|smart-link].

h2. Testing

* As a database admin, run the first migration to add the new table.
* Log in as admin and make sure the banned list is not empty, and that you can add and remove emails from the banned list.
* As a guest, make sure you can’t comment with a banned email, and that you _can_ comment once the email is unbanned. Also test that you can’t comment with a variation of a banned email, e.g. {{myemail+variation@example.com}} can’t be used if {{myemail@example.com}} is banned.
* Also as a guest, make sure you can add an email to the invitation queue, but you can’t add a variation of it, e.g. {{myemail+variation@example.com}} can’t be added if {{myemail@example.com}} is already in the queue.

27/May/21 9:05 AM;557058:bb48f715-7c87-43a5-81b8-a60c77a4c45b;Not a rails expert, but we from a DB perspective we should be able to do this without downtime by creating a new table as a copy of the previous one and switching the app to use that one so the old table hangs around until it gets dropped later (after we’re satisfied everything is working as intended).  We just need keep the tables in sync which shouldn’t be a big deal if there’s only a few hundred rows and not a large volume of writes, or we can make the table read-only for the duration of the deployment (not sure what that’s like in prod).

It may also be worth it to separate this work into two tasks, one to make all the user-facing changes without the need the need to touch the DB, and another for the DB shenanigans, so we can isolate those deployments.

Finally, sort of related, do we want to also change usage of “whitelist” throughout the codebase to something like “allow list”? (Probably should be it’s own separate issue.)
column148:
24/Nov/22 11:57 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;I just noticed that activating a rollout setting would probably not be enough, because {{table_name}} is changed when its setter is called. So we either need to call {{table_name=}} from the Rails console or restart the Rails server for it to take effect.

{quote}we should be able to do this without downtime by creating a new table as a copy of the previous one and switching the app to use that one so the old table hangs around until it gets dropped later (after we’re satisfied everything is working as intended). We just need keep the tables in sync which shouldn’t be a big deal if there’s only a few hundred rows and not a large volume of writes, or we can make the table read-only for the duration of the deployment (not sure what that’s like in prod).{quote}

Yeah, it should be possible to migrate with zero downtime. The tricky part is keeping the 2 tables in sync.

* The most correct approach, courtesy of GitLab, is to [atomically rename the table and create a view with the old name|https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/development/database/rename_database_tables.html]. When the application is using the view, we need to have [workarounds in place to make sure ActiveRecord can find the schema details from the actual table|https://github.com/gitlabhq/gitlabhq/blob/492f99eac8d349e03e22d9c3eed8923b80bcc297/lib/gitlab/database/schema_cache_with_renamed_table.rb].
* It’s also possible to use database triggers to keep the tables in sync, like pt-online-schema-change does. We will need to write the triggers ourselves, unfortunately. pt-online-schema-change already uses table renames for its normal operations and doesn’t support migrations involving table renames themselves.
* We can make the old table read-only, using {{GRANT}}/ {{REVOKE}}, but I think we need a database superuser to do so. I'd like to avoid extra unusual manual deploy steps if possible.

That said, since the table is small, and only site admins (PAC, Support, superadmin, as of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6394|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6394|smart-link]) can make changes to it, we can probably get away with… asking people not to ban emails while deploy is happening. So the steps could look like:

* Pre-deploy, run a migration to create the new table with the same schema, and copy the data over (can be done as part of the migration with an {{INSERT ... SELECT}} statement).
* The application code’s new version uses the new table. Deploy it as usual - a rolling restart of our servers, no downtime.
* At this point, the old table should be unused. Run a second migration to delete the old table, at leisure.

{quote}It may also be worth it to separate this work into two tasks, one to make all the user-facing changes without the need the need to touch the DB, and another for the DB shenanigans, so we can isolate those deployments.{quote}

The user-facing changes happened in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6394|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6394|smart-link] so we can keep this issue for the database migration and the rest of the code changes.

{quote}Finally, sort of related, do we want to also change usage of “whitelist” throughout the codebase to something like “allow list”? (Probably should be it’s own separate issue.){quote}

Yeah definitely. I can make an issue for it. AFAIK the only instance we can’t really change is [https://github.com/teampoltergeist/poltergeist#url-blacklisting--whitelisting|https://github.com/teampoltergeist/poltergeist#url-blacklisting--whitelisting], where the gem has been archived.

column1: Clean up chapter creatorships without corresponding work creatorships
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Users sometimes transfer works from one account to another:

- Edit Multiple Works, add new co-creator to works and save
- Edit Multiple Works, select the same works and choose "Remove Me As Co-Creator"

Before the co-creatorship rewrite in AO3-5658, it's possible that the old Edit Multiple form [didn't actually remove chapter creatorships when removing pseuds from a work|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/add90c35fa46c5240b4579b608323c79c8d914a0/lib/pseudable.rb#L34-L48]. There [wasn't a callback to remove pseuds from chapters|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/add90c35fa46c5240b4579b608323c79c8d914a0/app/models/work.rb#L20-L22] when they're removed from the work.

So we can end up with a chapter with a leftover approved creatorship for the old pseud, but with no corresponding creatorship on the work.

- If the old pseud still exists, it shows in the chapter byline, but the old pseud's user cannot edit the chapter or the work.
-- However, if said user somehow has creatorship on the work through a different pseud, they can edit the work and fix the pseuds on the chapter.
- If the old pseud doesn't exist, AND the current work creator somehow does not have a creatorship for the chapter, the work is editable by no one. The presence of the leftover creatorship prevents the current work creator from editing the chapter and [automatically filling in the missing chapter creatorship|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/69ad1a7620026e7a240b135da9e59adce6c8b919/app/models/chapter.rb#L37-L43].

Leftover approved chapter creatorships should be removed.

*Note*: This issue was originally for adding a new admin troubleshooting option. We then found that broken creatorships were created long before AO3-5658. Thanks to [tickinginstant] for root causing the issue!

*How to test*: TBD.
