Our official accounts that we use to communicate on the Archive are just regular user accounts, making it impossible for users to verify their authenticity. We need to alter the appearance of comments left by these accounts to make clear that this is official AO3 communication and to make it harder for users to imitate official accounts.

* Add a new user role "official" (like the role we already have for tag wranglers, translators, etc.) and make this role assignable to users by a superadmin (and open_doors, tag_wrangling, and policy_and_abuse – the admins who can assign roles)
* Change the appearance of comments left by users with the "official" role to indicate that it is an official account by adding the text {{(Official)}} next to the user name
* Comments left by official accounts should have the class {{official}} added to the {{<li>}}, i.e., {{<li class="official comment group">}}
* The {{(Official)}} should be in  {{<span class="role">}}  (literally the word “role”) and it should be styled bold with CSS

*Testing*

* Leave a comment with a regular user account
* Log in as superadmin and assign the role "official" to the user account you used in the previous step
* Use this new official account to leave another comment (works, news post)
* Check that both – the old and the new comment – appear differerent from regular user comments and are in some way marked as official
* Also check that using a pseud with the official account works

*Accounts*

These accounts should be granted the official status:

* OTWLegal
* AO3_ADT
* AO3_Support
* OTW_Finance
* Ao3_Tag_Wranglers
* OTW_Translation
* OTW_Board
* AO3_Policy_and_Abuse
* AO3_Docs
* Open_Doors
* OTW_devmem
* AO3_Systems
* OTW_Communications
* OTW_Elections
* OTW_VolunteersandRecruiting

*Deploy notes*

Run {{bundle exec rake defaults:create_roles}}

Afterwards, add the official role to all of the listed accounts, either via the console or the admin interface.

Then -touch all of the comments from the official accounts to expire the cache- just dump the entire cache for fun and profit.

There are CSS changes for this.

column150: 21/May/22 8:33 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;The fix for [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4120|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4120|smart-link] actually won’t resolve this caching issue, because {{user.roles}} is a has-many-through relation and is automatically saved when it’s set, not when you call {{user.save}}. column1: Generate sharing options when the user pushes the "Share" button, not when the bookmark page is loaded
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Similar to AO3-5907 for works.

The "Share" button on bookmark pages (single bookmark pages, bookmark listings) is set up so that all of the sharing options are rendered and embedded in the page, and the "Share" button just shows them (without performing another HTTP request). This means that:

# The server is performing unnecessary work for any user who views the bookmark pages and doesn't press the "Share" button.
# The twitter and tumblr buttons included in the sharing options mean that the user sends an HTTP request with AO3 listed as the referrer ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5818#icft=AO3-5818|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5818#icft=AO3-5818|smart-link]) to both twitter and tumblr when they view a work.

It would be good to move the sharing options off of the bookmark pages and into their own controller, to be loaded dynamically when the user presses the "Share" button.

The “Share” button is not currently presented to users who don’t have JavaScript disabled, and this behavior should continue.

*Testing Instructions:* Make sure that you can still use the "Share" button on bookmarks.

column1: Use ActiveJob for delayed emails instead of ResqueMailer
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
ResqueMailer doesn't appear to be actively developed anymore (it hasn't been updated since 2017). Fortunately, Rails's built-in Active Job allows sending emails asynchronously (i.e. as a delayed job), and supports Resque out of the box. It also supports more argument types (e.g. it preserves strings vs. symbols), and has better error handling for deserializing arguments.

It would be good to remove ResqueMailer and replace it with the built-in Active Job. This involves all of the following:
- Remove the {{resque_mailer}} gem from the gemfile.
- Don't {{include Resque::Mailer}} in any mailers.
- Change the configuration files to make Active Job use Resque for the queue.
- Replace all calls to {{deliver!}} (which currently delivers synchronously) with a call to {{deliver_now}}.
- Replace all calls to {{deliver}} (which currently delivers asynchronously) with a call to {{deliver_later}}.
- Modify the {{deliver_after_commit}} monkeypatch to work with Active Job.

There may also be other changes necessary.

01/Sep/20 3:16 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;This one’s tricky.

The {{app/models/skin.rb}} file calls {{include HtmlCleaner}}, but it calls it outside of the {{Skin}} class, which means that if the {{Skin}} class is loaded, all methods in {{HtmlCleaner}} will be available to all objects (including {{AdminMailer}}). But if the {{Skin}} class isn’t loaded, those methods won’t be available.

In testing and development, the factories are loaded, including {{factories/skins.rb}}, which accesses the constant {{Skin}} in its definition (instead of passing {{"Skin"}} as an argument to avoid loading it). In staging and production, however, {{FactoryBot}} isn’t included, and so the skin factory isn’t guaranteed to be loaded, and neither is {{app/models/skin.rb}}. This means that {{lib/html_cleaner.rb}} isn’t guaranteed to be included. That explains why it can’t be replicated in development (at least not without changing the skin factory definition).

This appears to caused by the 5.2 upgrade rather than the ActiveJob switch, because it looks like the Resque workers don’t load {{Skin}} both in {{master}} and {{master~}} (the version before this PR was merged), but do load {{Skin}} in {{master~3}} (the version before the 5.2 PR was merged).

More specifically, I think this may have been caused by upgrading Resque to 2.0. The new version was changed to respect the {{eager_load}} config setting, but apparently there’s an issue with rake and {{eager_load}} that can cause issues with Resque 2.0: [https://github.com/resque/resque/issues/1680|https://github.com/resque/resque/issues/1680|smart-link]. Unfortunately, {{rake_eager_load}} isn’t available in 5.2. Maybe instead it’d be better to manually add {{include HtmlCleaner}} to the {{AdminMailer}} file, and possibly modify the includes in {{app/models/skin.rb}} so that we don’t run into loading issues again in the future.

(Should [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5765|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5765|smart-link] be marked as broken on test? Or does this need a new issue under the epic?)

In the {{comments}} table, we have a boolean column named {{approved}}. Would you like to guess what this column is for?

The issue summary gives the answer away (it's for indicating whether the comment was marked as spam), but if it hadn't, you might be inclined to guess that it was used to indicate whether a moderated comment on a work had been approved by the work's creator. column1: Update comment factories to better resemble valid Archive comments
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Our [comment factories|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3b2cf664ea303b1066f7372b6930c9b51cef64b0/factories/comments.rb#L4-L39] have two issues that make them inconsistent with how comments on the Archive function:

# *They create comments that are simultaneously from registered users and guests*, which is not how Archive comments typically function.
## *For the* [*comment*|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3b2cf664ea303b1066f7372b6930c9b51cef64b0/factories/comments.rb#L4-L11]*,* [*unreviewed_comment*|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3b2cf664ea303b1066f7372b6930c9b51cef64b0/factories/comments.rb#L31-L39]*, and* [*adminpost_comment*|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3b2cf664ea303b1066f7372b6930c9b51cef64b0/factories/comments.rb#L13-L20] *factories*, they should either have a name and email (making them guest comments) _or_ belong to a pseud, not both. This may ultimately require the creation of separate factories for logged in comments and guests. (A [guest_comment factory|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3862/files/eb06c9ba978a9b8e369ed1055f3d594bc071803f#diff-4da5fde62dda7db086377e2dd829fd9f] for works will be introduced in the pull request for AO3-5765.)
## *For the* [*tag_comment factory*|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3b2cf664ea303b1066f7372b6930c9b51cef64b0/factories/comments.rb#L22-L29], they should only belong to registered users, as only tag wranglers can comment on tags.
# *The* [*comment factory*|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3b2cf664ea303b1066f7372b6930c9b51cef64b0/factories/comments.rb#L4-L11] *and* [*unreviewed_comment factory*|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3b2cf664ea303b1066f7372b6930c9b51cef64b0/factories/comments.rb#L31-L39] *assign the comments to works*, but comments are [actually on chapters, not works|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3b2cf664ea303b1066f7372b6930c9b51cef64b0/app/models/comment.rb#L367-L369].
## This may be causing [an issue mentioned in a Cucumber step definition|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/3b2cf664ea303b1066f7372b6930c9b51cef64b0/features/step_definitions/work_search_steps.rb#L137-L146]. If possible, this step should be updated to use the factories.

If updating the factories results in any test failures, the tests should be updated as well.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Ever since we stopped preloading guest comment forms with name/email people have used before (AO3-5162), the Policy and Abuse committee has received an increased number of reports from people who left guest comments but accidentally let their browser autofill their real names.

There are no reliable ways to [disable this browser behavior|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/15738259/disabling-chrome-autofill], but we've found that changing the field names can help.

From [~Ariana]:
{quote}
I logged out in Chrome where I’m logged in as an account called Ariana, and indeed, it offered to fill in my real name \[...\]. If I change the label in dev tools to "Guest name:", my real name stops coming up and I get the suggestion Commenter instead.
{quote}

We will rename the fields of the guest comment form from "Name" and "Email" to "Guest name" and "Guest email".

*How to test*:
- Open a guest comment form on production in Chrome and see how form autofill works. Try that on staging and see if the autofilled values are different.
- Make sure the fields have new names, and label association works (clicking on the label puts the focus/cursor on the field next to it).
- Make sure you can still post guest comments.

column1: Avoid having subscription types in hidden fields where browsers can translate them into unexpected values
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
When a user creating a subscription has auto-translation in their browsers, the values of [the hidden field "subscribable_type"|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/a7bb25ac11754fd8079b4ac9d6c877f541735842/app/views/subscriptions/_form.html.erb#L12] on the form gets translated (e.g. "User" to "用户"), which leads to an error because we expect the type to be [one of the known classes|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/a7bb25ac11754fd8079b4ac9d6c877f541735842/app/models/subscription.rb#L14-L15] (Work, User, Series). The error shows up like this [in New Relic|https://rpm.newrelic.com/accounts/115892/applications/190034/traced_errors/82454007-c0de-11ea-af78-0242ac11000a_0_7376]:

{code:java}NameError
SubscriptionsController#create

Error message
NameError: wrong constant name 用户

…app/releases/20200701075721/app/models/subscription.rb:  31:in `name'
…0701075721/app/controllers/subscriptions_controller.rb:  30:in `create'{code}

We've had this issue before, with tag names: [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5007|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5007|smart-link].

While we have validations in place to prevent invalid subscriptions from being created, returning errors in these cases is not great. We can stop putting the class names in hidden field values. One possible alternative is have 3 optional hidden fields {{user_id}}, {{work_id}}, {{series_id}} and use one of them depending on which subscribable type we're looking at (similar to how we handle [bookmarkables|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/a7bb25ac11754fd8079b4ac9d6c877f541735842/app/controllers/bookmarks_controller.rb#L23-L34]).

*How to test*:
Make sure you can subscribe to works/users/series without errors.

column1: Add i18n-tasks to normalize locale files and add tests to detect missing and unused translation keys
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
As we internationalize more and more of the site, we will inevitably run into these problems with the i18n gem:

* Missing keys will only cause errors at runtime.
* Unused keys may stick around without us knowing.

We should [install i18n-tasks and its tests|https://github.com/glebm/i18n-tasks#installation], which provides checks against both problems.

We also want to run its normalize task on our English locale files and commit the results. (Phrase organizes translations on export.)

*How to test*: none, automated.

Right now, we don't have an admin role to give to anyone from Legal! /o\ 

Typically, they coordinate with PAC rather than doing anything themselves, so this isn't a huge deal. However, we should still have a {{legal}} role that allows them to:

* Comments
** Delete comments on works, tags, and admin posts
** Hide comments on works, tags, and admin posts
** See the IP address and guest email address on comments 
** Freeze and hide admin post comments, and approve moderated admin post comments (note: all admins can do these regardless of role)
* Creations
** Delete works, series, bookmarks, or external works
** Hide works, series, bookmarks, or external works
** See the IP address on works
** See the Original Creator ID on orphaned works
* Users
** Search for users (might as well give them both Find Users and Bulk Email Search)
** Access users' admin user pages (including the ability to troubleshoot and activate users)

To test, give an admin account that role and make sure it can do those things.

*Code is complete in the linked PR, but we cannot actually merge due to* [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4997#issuecomment-2608350559|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4997#issuecomment-2608350559|smart-link] .

We have to provide guests with the data we collect about them. To make that easier on ourselves, we need a script that can be run from the Rails console. It should contain:

* User agents from any comments, abuse reports, or support tickets from the email address
* Name, summary, and content of any abuse reports from the email address
* Name, summary, and content of any support tickets from the email address

** The list of audited changes for the {{update}} action that we need IP addresses from is the same a[s the list in get_user_data.rb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/a3a88a4ed830db48a5fe35f590318792ac7805b8/script/get_user_data.rb#L84-L124], but it *also* needs to include the IP for the {{destroy}} action

23/Aug/26 9:35 PM;712020:c6679159-6662-4054-9969-6e556eb0bd39;I've opened a PR with a new approach, since PR #4997 was closed over the LIKE '%email%' full table scan on audits. The script now works in two parts:

# Fast path (default): Account history is found through indexed lookups instead of scanning audits. User ids come from users.email, users.unconfirmed_email, and user_past_emails (AO3-7249), and then audits are loaded by auditable_id, which is indexed. This covers guests and any account that still exists, with no expensive queries.
# Deep search (opt-in): The fast path can't find deleted accounts, since they're gone from all three tables (user_past_emails is dependent: :destroy) and their data only survives in audits. For those cases, the script asks the operator whether to search the audits table, and only then runs the LIKE query, split into bounded primary-key chunks so no single query runs unbounded on the table. Since GDPR requests for deleted accounts should be rare, the cost is only paid when it's actually needed, and ideally at low-traffic times.

A few implementation notes:

* The LIKE match is verified against the exact email afterwards, so a search for [guest@example.com|mailto:guest@example.com] can't pull in data from [aguest@example.com|mailto:aguest@example.com].
* IPs from audits recorded by an admin (for example, when an admin deleted the account) are excluded, following the same principle as AO3-5486 about not revealing admins' IP addresses.
* User agents from abuse reports and IP addresses from support tickets are not persisted in the database (they're only in-memory attributes), so the script can't include them.
* Accounts deleted before the audits table existed (July 2015) can't be found at all, since that data doesn't exist anywhere.

Feedback welcome on whether the opt-in scan is an acceptable trade-off.
column148:
06/Sep/26 9:27 AM;712020:c6679159-6662-4054-9969-6e556eb0bd39;Following up on the opt-in scan question: after discussing it with Brian and sarken on Slack, the deep search has been removed from PR #5998. Reading the whole audits table on the live database is a no-go even as an opt-in.

Instead, the script prints the audits query at the end of the report and does not run it. Support can hand that query to Systems to run on a secondary database, and Systems passes the resulting user ids back. This is the only way to find deleted accounts, since their data only survives in audits.

What the script runs on the live database:

* User ids from users.email (indexed), users.unconfirmed_email, and user_past_emails, with audits loaded by auditable_id.
* Guest data from comments (indexed on email) and the abuse_reports, feedbacks, and fannish_next_of_kins tables, as in get_user_data.rb.

None of these queries touch audits without an id.

The implementation notes from the previous comment still apply: admin-recorded IPs are excluded (AO3-5486), user agents from abuse reports and IPs from support tickets aren't stored in the database, and accounts deleted before July 2015 have no audit data to recover.

h1. What happens

The email says “{color:#bf2600}*pseud*{color} left the following comment on {color:#bf2600}*_Work Title_*{color}:” and the pseud name is a link to the user’s dashboard rather than the pseud’s. This is confusing.

h1. What should happen

The email should say “{color:#bf2600}*pseud (username)*{color} left the following comment on {color:#bf2600}*_Work Title_*{color}:” and the whole “pseud (username)” part should be a link to the pseud’s dashboard.

If you are using the pseud that matches your username, it should just say “{color:#bf2600}*username*{color} left the following comment on {color:#bf2600}*_Work Title_*{color}:” but the username should link to the appropriate pseud dashboard.

(This is the behavior of the username/pseud links on the comments themselves.)

Additionally, it should say “*_(Registered User)_*” in bold and italics (but not red) after the username to distinguish it from guest comments ( [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6548|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6548|smart-link] ):

column1: Prevent wranglers, but not tag wrangling admins, from adding subtags via a tag's edit page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h1. Steps to reproduce
# Log in as a user with the tag wrangling role, e.g. testy
# Go the the edit page for a canonical tag, e.g. [the edit page for Testing|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/edit]

h1. What happens
Toward the bottom of the form, you will find a "SubTags" area with the options to add or remove subtags. Sometimes, wranglers enter a tag in the "add" field, assuming it will make the current tag a subtag of the tag they entered. However, it does the opposite: it makes the _entered_ tag a subtag of the one they are editing.

Tag Wranglers note: 
{quote}So, we have an ongoing issue where tag wranglers sometimes mistakenly pop tags into the wrong field on the tag edit page and instead of subtagging their tag to Alternate Universe (or-what-have-you) they instead end up subtagging Alternate Universe to their tag. It stresses them out and makes more work for us and them as sometimes these issues aren’t noticed immediately and its just all around a bit of a pain. It’s also been known to cause issues when we’re trying to construct and deconstruct trees.

Since this particular error almost always occurs because of the subtag field on the tag edit page being mistaken for the metatag field, we were thinking a reasonable solution to this problem might be to just make the subtag field on the tag edit page non-editable on non-admin accounts. That way only the metatag field could be edited thus making it considerably more difficult to accidentally make this particular error.{quote}

h1. What should happen
The "Add" field in the "SubTags" area should be disabled for non-admins, but stay enabled for admins. The back end code should also be updated to give an error that says, "Only an admin can add a subtag from this page."

The "Remove" checkboxes should remain enabled for everyone.

h1. Testing
To test the error message, you can remove the "disabled" attribute from the "Add" field using your browser's developer tools.

An admin should make sure they can still use this field.

column1: Rename creator invitations to co-creator requests
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
We've received Support requests from users who expect to find their Archive invites at the "Creator Invitations (#)" link in the dashboard menu. We'd like to rename "creator invitations" to "co-creator requests" to hopefully avoid this confusion:

* The dashboard menu link should be "Co-Creator Requests (#)".
* If a user has a pending co-creator request on a chapter/work/series, they should see a notice on that chapter/work/series with the text "To accept or reject the invitation, visit your Co-Creator Requests page.", where "Co-Creator Requests page" is a link to the page.
* The page itself:
** should have the HTML title "Co-Creator Requests".
** should have the heading "Co-Creator Requests".
** if there are no requests, should display "No co-creator requests found."
** if there are any requests, should have "List of Co-Creator Requests" as the legend of the mass request edit form (this element is not visible by default).
* On the user's preferences page, the help-popup for the Privacy section should show (changed text in bold) "You won't be listed as a co-creator anywhere on the site until you have accepted the *request*. If you have this option enabled, you can find any *requests* you receive in your Dashboard under "*Co-Creator Requests*". You will also receive an email notifying you of the *request*."
* When a user is added as a co-creator by an archivist, the "Archivist co-creator notification" email should include "Because they are acting in their official capacity as an Open Doors archivist, they are allowed to add you without a *request*, even if you have co-creation disabled.".
* When a user with co-creation enabled is added as a co-creator by another user, the notification email:
** should have the subject "Co-creator request" instead of "Co-creator invitation",
** should include in its body "You can accept or reject this *request* on your *Co-Creator Requests* page". Note that "Co-Creator Requests" should be a link to said page in the HTML version of the email.

Finally, for consistency, we should rename a few things not visible to users:

* The translation key in the notice of pending co-creator requests for [works|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e0f7ce52129a09f5483199a71802d5f30b9c433e/app/views/works/show.html.erb#L19-L20],  [series|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e0f7ce52129a09f5483199a71802d5f30b9c433e/app/views/series/show.html.erb#L4-L5], chapters ([list|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e0f7ce52129a09f5483199a71802d5f30b9c433e/app/views/chapters/show.html.erb#L10-L11], [partial|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b7b26d0b1836122e4b0b0129efa78fce90e6d0de/app/views/chapters/_chapter.html.erb#L11-L12]).
* [The translation key of the "Co-creator request" email notification|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e253777e4440213b149fa2e1f5c7a799207bb4f5/config/locales/mailers/en.yml#L89].
* [The test step for accepting all co-creator requests|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/59219f5fb28ec51e724f258b6a6715d26ceb1cbb/features/step_definitions/user_steps.rb#L208].
* [The test path alias for the Co-Creator Requests page|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/35c4983e2586ad7745af136ca0f38ed66bf1bbb1/features/support/paths.rb#L104].

column1: Works hidden by an admin can be viewed on various collection-related pages
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
h3. Collection Steps

# Log in as User A.
# Create an open, unmoderated collection.
# Log in as User B.
# Post a work to User A's collection.
# Log in as an admin with permission to hide works.
# Hide User B's work.
# Log in as User A.
# View your collection.
# Follow "Manage Items."
# Follow "Approved" to see approved collection items.

h3. Prompt Meme Steps

# Log in as User A.
# Create a prompt meme.
# Post a prompt.
# Log in as User B.
# Claim User A's prompt.
# Post a work fulfilling User A's prompt.
# Log in as an admin with permission to hide works.
# Hide User B's work.
# Log out.
# View User A's prompt meme.
# Click on the "Prompts (#)" link to see all prompts.

h3. Assignment Steps

# Log in as User A.
# Create collection with an attached gift exchange.
# Open sign-ups on the gift exchange.
# Sign up for your own gift exchange.
# Log in as User B.
# Sign up for User A's gift exchange.
# Log in as User A.
# Close sign-ups.
# Run matching.
# Send out assignments.
# Log in as User B.
# Go to your assignments page.
# Press the "Fulfill" button.
# Post a work fulfilling the assignment.
# Log in as an admin with permission to hide works.
# Hide the work that B posted.
# Log in as User A.
# View the collection for the gift exchange.
# Follow "Assignments."
# Follow "Complete" to see completed assignments.

h3. What Happens

In all three cases, there's a link to the hidden work. The user will get an error if they try to follow the link.

h3. What Should Happen

The work should not be visible.

In the case of the gift exchange, the assignment probably shouldn't be considered complete if the work is hidden.
